title: mRNA-based seasonal influenza vaccines: an overview of immunogenicity, efficacy, and safety.
abstract: Available seasonal influenza vaccines, most of which are still produced in eggs, have several limitations. Messenger RNA (mRNA) technology has emerged as a transformative approach capable of overcoming some of these shortcomings. This overview synthesizes clinical trials evaluating the immunogenicity, efficacy, and safety of standalone and combination mRNA influenza vaccines. Moderna's mRNA-1010 (now approved in the United States) and Pfizer's modified-nucleoside RNA candidate (modRNA) represent the most advanced standalone platforms, while Moderna's combination influenza and COVID-19 vaccine, mRNA-1083, was recently granted European authorization. Following iterative platform optimization, these vaccines induce robust humoral and cell-mediated responses, especially against influenza A strains, characterized by extended germinal center reactions, continuous somatic hypermutation, enhanced Fc-mediated effector functions, and strong T helper 1 engagement. In phase III relative efficacy trials, an optimized mRNA-1010 formulation achieved superiority over standard-dose vaccines with a relative efficacy of 26.6% (95% CI: 16.7%, 35.4%) in adults aged ≥50 years. Pfizer's first-generation quadrivalent modRNA candidate showed 34.5% (95% CI: 7.4%, 53.9%) relative efficacy against a standard-dose comparator in younger adults aged 18-64 years, but failed to demonstrate non-inferiority in older adults (≥65 years), showing a relative efficacy of -5.8% (95% CI: -47.2%, 23.8%). However, whether mRNA platforms offer incremental benefits over enhanced formulations (such as high-dose, adjuvanted, or recombinant vaccines), which are the preferred options in some countries for older adults, remains to be established. The safety profile aligns with licensed COVID-19 mRNA vaccines; although reactogenicity is higher than with conventional vaccines, adverse reactions are predominantly mild-to-moderate and transient. Operationally, transitioning to single-dose pre-filled syringes alongside expanding refrigerated stability data significantly mitigates historical cold-chain bottlenecks. However, while standalone and combination mRNA platforms represent a major technological advance, real-world implementation challenges may affect their broader global health impact.

title: Perception of COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness perception in older racialized communities: role of major racial discrimination and health literacy.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Vaccination has been scientifically proven to be safe and to prevent infectious diseases. The COVID-19 vaccine has been crucial in combating the pandemic. In Canada, despite widespread vaccine hesitancy, little has specifically addressed older adults from racialized communities. This study investigates perceptions of COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness among older adults by racial background, examining the influence of major racial discrimination and health literacy. STUDY DESIGN: A cross-sectional pan-Canadian study. METHODS: Data were collected using Computer-Assisted Web Interviewing (March 2025). The COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness was tested with t-tests, ANOVA, and multivariable linear regression. RESULTS: 581 participants were included: Arab (11.5%), Asian (15.8%), Black (16.2%), Indigenous (9%), and White (35.8%); including men (48.2%), women (43.0%), and 8.8% identifying as non-binary. Participants 65 years and above reported significantly greater perceived COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness versus 55-64 years old (t(579) = 2.17, p = .015)). Asian and White participants were more likely to have a good perception of COVID-19 vaccines versus Black and Indigenous (F(6,574) = 2.88, p = .009) participants. Multivariable linear regression revealed that major racial discrimination was the strongest predictor of lower perception of vaccine effectiveness (β = -0.42, p = .006), along with literacy (β = 0.09, p = .002) and identifying as Black compared to White (β = -1.49, p = .020). CONCLUSIONS: Perceptions of COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness among 55+ in Canada varied substantially across racial groups, with differences linked to experiences of discrimination and literacy levels. These findings highlight the need for targeted, equity-oriented public health strategies that address both structural racism and misinformation to improve vaccine confidence among older adults in marginalized communities.

title: Household and Community Clustering of Concurrent Vaccine Hesitancy in China: Multicenter Survey.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Vaccine hesitancy remains a persistent global challenge, especially in the context of major public health emergencies. While individual-level factors have been widely studied, whether and how household and community contexts shape hesitancy clustering has received little attention. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to assess household- and community-level clustering of COVID-19 booster vaccine hesitancy (CBVH), identify key associated factors, and explore potential intervention targets. METHODS: In March 2023, a household-based cross-sectional survey was conducted among Chinese adults across 4 provinces. Concurrent CBVH was defined as hesitancy reported for both current and future booster intentions within the same survey. The analytical samples included 5462 participants for current CBVH, 5437 for future CBVH, and 5407 for concurrent CBVH. Three-level logistic regression models were used to quantify variance attributable to individual, household, and community levels and to identify associated factors. Network analysis was also used to examine interrelationships among key factors and identify central intervention targets. RESULTS: Among 5407 participants, 1461 (27.0%) exhibited concurrent CBVH. The unweighted prevalence of current and future CBVH was 28.4% (1553/5462) and 30.1% (1636/5437), respectively. The corresponding poststratified prevalence estimates were 30.88% and 32.55%, respectively. In the null model, the combined household- and community-level intraclass correlation coefficients were 77.73% (95% CI 72.40%-82.29%) and 78.84% (95% CI 73.57%-83.30%), respectively. Prior COVID-19 vaccination, self-efficacy, perceived benefits, trust in vaccine developers, and knowledge of the vaccine were associated with lower CBVH, while perceived barriers, perceived severity, household income, chronic disease, history of allergies, and living in the eastern region were associated with higher hesitancy. Network analysis revealed that self-efficacy and prior COVID-19 vaccination had the strongest associations with CBVH. Perceived barriers and trust in vaccine developers formed the strongest association among nodes. The current and future CBVH networks showed similar configurations. CONCLUSIONS: The substantial household and community clustering highlights the need for group interventions. Household-centered vaccine education, community-based vaccine counseling services, and transparent vaccine communication may help reduce vaccine hesitancy and strengthen preparedness for future infectious disease outbreaks.

title: Distinct systemic metabolic phenotypes associated with blood culture positivity and bacterial etiology in community-acquired pneumonia (CAP).
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, particularly among young children and older adults. Bacterial pathogens account for a substantial proportion of CAP cases, yet early identification of bacteremia and etiologic agents remains challenging. Blood cultures are slow and often have a limited clinical impact. We hypothesized that plasma metabolomics can capture systemic metabolic signatures associated with blood culture positivity and bacterial etiology at the time of hospital admission. METHODS: Plasma samples from 80 patients with bacterial CAP (40 culture-positive and 40 age- and sex-matched culture-negative) were collected on the first day of admission. Metabolomic profiling was performed using complementary platforms, including untargeted 1H-NMR, GC-MS, and targeted LC-DIMS/MS. Multivariate and univariate analyses were applied to identify discriminating metabolic features. RESULTS: Distinct metabolic phenotypes were observed between culture-positive and culture-negative patients across all platforms. OPLS-DA models demonstrated significant discrimination, with GC-MS and 1H-NMR showing strong internally cross-validated discriminatory performance (Q2 > 0.45, AUROC > 0.90). Culture-positive CAP was characterized by increased phenylalanine, urea, and mannose, alongside decreased amino acids and fatty acids, indicating coordinated alterations in nitrogen metabolism, energy pathways, and lipid remodeling. Furthermore, metabolomic profiles enabled discrimination of Streptococcus pneumoniae from other bacterial causes, with GC-MS and LC-DIMS/MS achieving strong internal discrimination (Q2 ≈ 0.4, AUROC > 0.90). CONCLUSIONS: Plasma metabolomics identified distinct systemic metabolic patterns associated with blood culture positivity and, in exploratory analysis, with S. pneumoniae etiology. These discovery-stage findings demonstrate reproducible systemic metabolic patterns associated with blood culture positivity and bacterial etiology and support further validation of targeted metabolite signatures in independent CAP cohorts.
journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

title: Point-of-care lactate in pediatric sepsis: a single-center observational study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Lactate is a key biomarker in the assessment of sepsis, reflecting tissue hypoperfusion and correlating with disease severity and outcomes. However, reliance on standard laboratory testing may delay clinical decision-making in time-sensitive situations. Point-of-care (POC) lactate testing provides rapid bedside assessment, potentially facilitating earlier risk stratification and intervention. This study aimed to evaluate the predictive value of POC lactate for pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) admission and mortality in pediatric patients with sepsis. METHODS: This was a retrospective observational study of children aged 3 months to 14 years presenting to the pediatric emergency department in a tertiary care children's hospital with a diagnosis of sepsis. Data were extracted from electronic medical records. RESULTS: A total of 149 pediatric patients with sepsis were included, of whom 90 underwent POC lactate testing. Elevated POC lactate levels were observed in 38.9% of tested patients. Elevated POC lactate was significantly associated with PICU admission, as well as the need for mechanical ventilation and inotropic support. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis demonstrated modest but statistically significant predictive performance for PICU admission (AUC = 0.641), whereas no predictive value was observed for mortality (AUC = 0.544). CONCLUSIONS: Point-of-care lactate may serve as a practical supplementary biomarker that can facilitate early risk stratification by identifying children with sepsis at increased risk of PICU admission and requiring advanced interventions. Nevertheless, its modest discriminatory performance necessitates interpretation in conjunction with clinical assessment and additional biomarkers rather than as an independent predictor of sepsis severity.

title: A Diagnostic Dilemma: Urosepsis Mimicking ST-elevation Myocardial Infarction: A Case Report and Review of the Literature.
abstract: Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) remains a leading global cause of morbidity and mortality. Healthcare systems worldwide have established national guidelines to facilitate the timely identification and transfer of patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) to centers capable of performing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Typically, ST-segment elevation (STE) on an electrocardiogram (ECG) is indicative of STEMI, prompting early intervention. However, rare cases of STE have been documented in the setting of sepsis or septic shock, with subsequent coronary angiography or imaging revealing normal coronary arteries. There is limited information regarding the exact mechanisms responsible for STE in the context of sepsis. We report the case of a 79-year-old Indian female who presented with epigastric pain and vomiting. Her initial ECG showed STE in leads I, aVL, and V2, accompanied by markedly elevated cardiac biomarkers. In accordance with the national STEMI network protocol, she received prehospital dual antiplatelet therapy and intravenous heparin before hospital arrival and was transferred directly for primary PCI. She was initially managed as a case of ACS; however, coronary angiography demonstrated normal coronary arteries. Further evaluation led to the diagnosis of septic shock secondary to extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Escherichia coli urosepsis, requiring mechanical ventilation, four concurrent vasopressors, and continuous venovenous hemodiafiltration, with complete clinical recovery. Notably, her ECG abnormalities resolved within 72 h following prompt management of the septic shock. While STEMI remains the most common cause of STE on ECG, sepsis and septic shock are rare but important differential diagnoses. The underlying pathophysiology may involve inflammatory myocardial injury, transient coronary vasospasm, or global hypoperfusion. This case highlights the critical importance of recognizing septic shock as a potentially life-threatening STEMI mimic, to avoid unnecessary invasive interventions and to guide appropriate, targeted management.
journal: Heart views : the official journal of the Gulf Heart Association

title: A Miniaturized, Multilayer Structured Vertical Flow Paper Device Enabled One-Step, Multiplex, Spontaneous Detection of Biomarkers in Microliter Blood for Disease Screening.
abstract: Developing a miniaturized, portable device for multiplexed detection of a library of protein biomarkers from microliter blood sample is critical for early disease screening in many scenarios, such as home healthcare and emergency care. However, major challenges remain, including multiplexed detection without cross-interference, system-level miniaturization, reliable flow manipulation, and simple user operation. Here, we present a miniaturized, multilayer structured vertical flow paper device that enables one-step, multiplexed, spontaneous detection of biomarkers in microliter blood for screening of heart disease, kidney disease, and inflammation. The device is designed with a multilayer membrane structure that integrates 3D-printed glass fiber membranes, wax-printed nitrocellulose membranes, and cellulose absorption membranes, enabling autonomous wicking of the sample through the device while concurrently distributing the sample into multiple equal parts and executing the sandwich immunoassay and washing steps. Simultaneous quantification of 12 biomarkers is achieved, and clinical performance is validated using clinical samples from patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI), acute kidney disease (AKD), or sepsis. The device requires about 60 μL of sample, delivers results in 15 min, and is also compact (12.5 cm3). Overall, this platform provides a novel and universal strategy for miniaturized multiplexed immunoassays for rapid clinical screening.

title: [Autumn vaccinations for older adults: Influenza, Covid-19 and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)].
abstract: Today, the Federal Commission on Vaccination (EKIF) recommends two vaccinations for people aged 65 and over in the autumn: one against flu and one against Covid-19. The new RSV vaccines are recommended for people aged 75 and over and for people aged 60-74 with relevant underlying conditions, but basic health insurance does not yet cover the costs. These vaccines each reduce the risk of illness and hospitalisation to varying degrees, and the risk of serious side effects is very low. The flu vaccine reduces the risk of heart attack, at least in terms of secondary prevention. However, the high Number Needed to Vaccinate (NNV) to prevent respiratory infection- or pneumonia-related hospitalisation (over 1000 for covid vaccines and well over 3000 for flu vaccines) may lead doctors to question the effectiveness of vaccination. For the new RSV vaccines, the NNV is lower at approximately 250 for individuals aged over 75. Additionally, the protective effect lasts for at least two seasons. Although the EKIF strongly recommends the high-dose flu vaccine, it is 50 % more expensive and, in a randomised head-to-head comparison involving 466 000 participants, only slightly more effective than standard-dose vaccines (NNV = approx. 1832).

title: Systemic immune inflammation index and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio as predictors of neonatal sepsis in low birth weight infants.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The systemic immune inflammation index (SII) and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) are hematological parameters calculable from standard laboratory assessment. Despite extensive adult medicine implementation, neonatal applicability remains incompletely characterized. Early identification of sepsis in neonates remains challenging and sepsis is a significant global health problem associated with high morbidity and mortality, particularly among vulnerable low birth weight (LBW) infants. This study aimed to evaluate the predictive value of SII and NLR for neonatal sepsis in LBW infants. METHODS: This observational analytic case-control study was conducted at Dr. Hasan Sadikin General Hospital, Bandung, between January 2024 and June 2025. A total of 290 LBW infants were enrolled in this study, comprising 145 infants with neonatal sepsis and 145 without sepsis. SII and NLR values were calculated from complete blood counts obtained at the initial evaluation within six hours after birth. Data were analyzed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves to determine the area under the curve (AUC), optimal cut-off values, sensitivity, specificity and likelihood ratios (LR). RESULTS: Both biomarkers were significantly associated with the subsequent development of culture-confirmed neonatal sepsis. Comparative predictive performance analysis revealed superior performance of SII (AUC: 0.778; 95%CI: 0.726-0.825) relative to NLR (AUC: 0.678; 95%CI: 0.620-0.731; p < 0.001). At an optimal cut-off value of ≤ 657,962.56, SII yielded a sensitivity of 57.9% and specificity of 88.3% with positive predictive value 83.2%, LR + 4.95 and LR - 0.48. The optimal NLR cut-off value of ≤ 3.1 showed a sensitivity of 59.3% and specificity of 73.1% with LR + of 2.20. CONCLUSIONS: Both SII and NLR are significant predictors of neonatal sepsis in LBW infants. SII demonstrates superior predictive performance and higher specificity compared with NLR.

title: Screening for Left Ventricular Dysfunction in Sepsis Using a Smartphone ECG Analysis Application: A Multicenter Validation Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sepsis-induced left ventricular (LV) dysfunction complicates fluid resuscitation, increasing the risk of pulmonary edema and worsening outcomes. Echocardiographic assessment is often delayed, and natriuretic peptides such as N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) have limited diagnostic accuracy in this setting. We evaluated a smartphone-based electrocardiogram (ECG) analysis application for screening LV dysfunction in patients with sepsis. METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective observational study, we included 425 adult sepsis patients from three university hospitals who underwent both a 12-lead ECG and transthoracic echocardiography within 72 hours of emergency department admission. ECG images displayed on a monitor were photographed and analyzed using an artificial intelligence (AI)-based smartphone application (ECG BuddyTM), which generated a quantitative digital biomarker for LV dysfunction (quantitative electrocardiogram scores for LV dysfunction [QCG-LVDys]). LV dysfunction was defined as a left ventricular ejection fraction ≤ 40%. The diagnostic performance of QCG-LVDys for detecting LV dysfunction was evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC). A predefined comparison with NT-proBNP was performed in the single center where NT-proBNP was routinely measured. RESULTS: In the overall multicenter cohort, QCG-LVDys showed high diagnostic performance for LV dysfunction, with an ROC-AUC of 0.901. Using an optimized threshold (37.35), QCG-LVDys achieved a sensitivity of 89.6%, specificity of 75.1%, and negative predictive value (NPV) of 97.5%. In the NT-proBNP subset, QCG-LVDys outperformed NT-proBNP (ROC-AUC 0.911 vs. 0.637, P < 0.001). Higher QCG-LVDys values were associated with increased lactate levels (P = 0.002) and 28-day in-hospital mortality (P < 0.001). CONCLUSION: AI-driven ECG analysis via a smartphone app provided a rapid, accessible, and accurate screening tool for LV dysfunction in sepsis and outperformed NT-proBNP. Its high NPV suggests potential utility for early risk stratification and for informing cautious hemodynamic management, although prospective studies are needed to define its role in sepsis treatment protocols.

title: Comparing two case definitions for including severe acute respiratory infection patients in influenza and COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness studies among older adults using the test-negative design: VEBIS hospital network, seven European countries, 2023/24.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Two severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) case definitions (CDs) are often used in test-negative design (TND) hospital-based vaccine effectiveness (VE) studies. SARI-CD1 requires ≥1 symptom (cough, fever, shortness of breath, anosmia, ageusia, or dysgeusia); SARI-CD2 requires both fever and cough. Using VEBIS hospital network end-of-season 2023/24 data, we compared the effect of these CDs on influenza and COVID-19 VE estimates in Europe. METHODS: Using the TND, we restricted analysis to seven countries recruiting patients using SARI-CD1; we created a subset of SARI patients also meeting SARI-CD2. Cases were RT-PCR-positive for influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), or SARS-CoV-2; controls were influenza or SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR-negative. We estimated VE among patients ≥65 years using logistic regression adjusted for country, onset date, age, sex, and chronic conditions. We estimated VE overall, by age group (65-79, ≥80 years) and time since vaccination (14-59, 60-119, ≥120 days). Absolute VE differences ≥10% were considered relevant. RESULTS: Patient characteristics and outcomes were similar across CDs. SARI-CD1 had slightly more vaccinated cases, with little difference in controls between the two CDs. For influenza, the absolute VE difference between SARI-CD1 and SARI-CD2 was 10% for influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 (34% vs 44%), 19% among those aged ≥80 years (21% vs 40%) and 18% at 60-119 days post-vaccination (4% vs 22%). For SARS-CoV-2, absolute VE differences were 11% overall (29% vs 40%), 11% among ≥80 years (33% vs 44%), and 12% at 60-119 days (34% vs 46%). All other absolute VE differences were < 10%. CONCLUSIONS: VE was similar for influenza A(H3N2), adults 65-79 years and 14-60 days post-vaccination. We observed signals of higher VE with SARI-CD2 for influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 and SARS-CoV-2, particularly among adults ≥80 years and ≥ 60 days post-vaccination, although 95% CIs overlapped. These signals suggest CDs may contribute to VE variability and VE studies should clearly indicate CDs used.

title: Safety and immunogenicity of Thailand Government Pharmaceutical Organization (GPO) produced, COVID-19 vaccine, 10 μg HXP-GPOVac: A Phase III, double-blind, randomized trial in comparison with VAXZEVRIA.
abstract: BACKGROUND: HXP-GPOVac is a Thailand-produced, egg-based, inactivated recombinant Newcastle disease virus (NDV)-chimera vaccine expressing a membrane-anchored, prefusion-stabilized SARS-CoV-2 spike (NDV-HXP-S), developed to expand vaccine access. This phase III trial evaluated the safety and immunogenicity of a single HXP-GPOVac dose in healthy or clinically stable Thai adults who had completed a two-dose primary series of an authorized COVID-19 vaccine. METHODS: In this double-blind, randomized, active-controlled trial in Nakhon Phanom, Thailand, 4000 participants were randomized 3:1 to receive HXP-GPOVac or VAXZEVRIA (AstraZeneca, ChAdOx1 nCoV-19). Safety outcomes included incidence, severity, and vaccine-relatedness of adverse events (AEs). AE incidence was compared between vaccine groups using Chi-square or Fisher's exact test. Immunogenicity was assessed by pseudovirus neutralization assay for 50% neutralizing antibody titers (NT50) and ELISA for anti-Spike IgG. Non-inferiority was prespecified for NT50-based endpoints at day 14, defined by (i) a geometric mean concentration (GMC) ratio (HXP-GPOVac/VAXZEVRIA) with 95% CI lower bound >0.67 and (ii) a seroconversion rate (SCR) difference with 95% CI lower bound > -10%. RESULTS: Solicited AEs occurred in 43.7% of HXP-GPOVac recipients versus 53.5% of VAXZEVRIA recipients (p = 0.01). Most solicited AEs were mild. No vaccine-related serious AEs were reported. At day 14, the NT50 GMC ratio (HXP-GPOVac/VAXZEVRIA) was 0.83 (95% CI lower bound: 0.74), and the SCR difference was -2.35% (95% CI lower bound: -8.72%), both meeting non-inferiority criteria. CONCLUSION: HXP-GPOVac was well-tolerated and demonstrated non-inferior immunogenicity compared with VAXZEVRIA at 14 days after vaccination. These findings provide rationale for larger studies to assess HXP-GPOVac clinical efficacy.

title: Cardiac Magnetic Resonance-Supported Diagnosis of Acute Myocarditis Mimicking Acute Coronary Syndrome in a Patient With Sepsis Due to a Massive Perianal Abscess.
abstract: Acute myocarditis is a rare but potentially life-threatening inflammatory disease that may mimic acute myocardial infarction, particularly in septic patients where myocardial injury may have other causes. We report the case of a 46-year-old man with sepsis secondary to a massive perianal abscess who underwent emergency surgical drainage under general anesthesia. Postoperatively, persistent respiratory deterioration and elevated cardiac biomarkers prompted further cardiac evaluation. Echocardiography showed newly reduced left ventricular (LV) systolic function, with an ejection fraction (EF) of 35%, and moderate-to-severe mitral regurgitation (MR). Although acute myocardial infarction was initially suspected, coronary angiography showed non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA), with only a 40% right coronary artery stenosis. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) demonstrated elevated T2 values and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) of the interventricular septum, with additional enhancement of the LV lateral wall, consistent with myocardial edema and inflammation and supportive of acute myocarditis. The patient received source control, broad-spectrum antibiotics, intravenous diuretics, norepinephrine and dobutamine, oxygen therapy, and heart failure-directed therapy. EF improved to 45% at 10 days, with complete recovery of cardiac function and resolution of MR at the 3-month follow-up. This case highlights the diagnostic challenge of acute myocarditis in septic surgical patients and suggests that early multidisciplinary assessment, coronary evaluation, and CMR may help clarify the diagnosis and guide management.

title: Dynamic Co-Evolution of C-Reactive Protein and Albumin in Early Sepsis: A Group-Based Dual-Trajectory Analysis for Risk Stratification.
abstract: The coupled evolution of inflammation and metabolic dysfunction during early sepsis is incompletely characterized. Although C-reactive protein (CRP) and albumin (ALB) are established markers of these processes, their joint longitudinal patterns have rarely been examined. We used group-based dual-trajectory modelling (GBDTM) to identify distinct coevolutionary patterns of CRP and ALB and to evaluate their associations with mortality in patients with sepsis. This retrospective observational study included patients admitted to the ICU of Beijing Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Capital Medical University, between June 2014 and March 2025. All included adults met the Sepsis-3 criteria. Among 462 patients with sepsis, serial CRP and ALB measurements obtained on days 1, 3, 5, 7 and 14 after ICU admission were analysed using GBDTM. The selected three-class model showed acceptable classification quality (entropy = 0.80; class-specific average posterior probabilities [AvePPs] = 0.84-0.92) and identified slow-decreasing (79.65%), rapid-decreasing (10.39%) and increasing (9.96%) inflammatory phenotypes. The 28-day mortality rate was highest in the increasing group (52.2% vs. 32.6% and 33.3%; log-rank p = 0.034). In the fully adjusted Cox model, the increasing trajectory was associated with 28-day mortality (HR 1.943, 95% CI: 1.202-3.140; p = 0.007) and 60-day mortality (HR 1.946, 95% CI: 1.218-3.108; p = 0.005). Parsimonious models adjusted for age, sex, and SOFA or the Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II (APACHE II) score yielded broadly similar estimates. Joint CRP-ALB trajectories identify clinically interpretable dynamic phenotypes during early sepsis. These findings support the joint trajectory as a hypothesis-generating, complementary phenotyping marker that requires external prospective validation.
journal: Journal of cellular and molecular medicine

title: Transparency of clinical trials: Reproducing and extending analyses.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Between 2021 and 2023, deidentified patient-level data and associated programming code from the biologics license application for Pfizer's covid-19 vaccine were published on the Internet. The release, which appears to be unprecedented in permitting public access to such granular data, allows new researchers to independently reproduce published analyses and extend published findings by conducting analyses that the original investigators did not report. METHODS: We downloaded 2370 files (26 gigabytes), including more than 30 SAS programming files, 2 data reviewer's guides, and 180 SAS Transport datasets from phmpt.org. We documented programming files and adapted them to run in our environment, aiming to reproduce four published tables and a figure reporting efficacy and safety results. We also sought to estimate vaccine efficacy against covid-19 hospitalization, a clinically meaningful and public health relevant measure of potential protection against serious disease that has not been reported. RESULTS: We were able to reproduce 334 of 352 data elements from four published efficacy and safety tables. Lacking original code, we could not reproduce one key efficacy analysis (a cumulative incidence curve). For our extended analyses, we judged that vaccine efficacy against covid-19 hospitalization could not be reliably calculated using the available datasets due to a paradoxical (and therefore unreliable) finding of more covid-19 hospitalizations (n = 43) than cases of severe covid-19 (n = 31). DISCUSSION: The public release of original datasets and patient-level data enabled the exact reproduction of most published efficacy and safety analyses, establishing a firm basis for further analyses. Our experience highlights the feasibility and enormous value of publicly releasing and analyzing patient-level clinical trial datasets.

title: Pentosan polysulfate sodium limits pulmonary inflammation in a SARS-CoV-2 mouse model.
abstract: UNLABELLED: Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection remains prevalent globally, causing severe pulmonary inflammation and mortality in up to 10% of patients. While the introduction of effective vaccines has substantially reduced the number of severe coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) cases, there are currently few available therapeutics that have been developed. Pentosan polysulfate sodium (PPS) has been shown to possess potent anti-inflammatory activity in influenza infection and allergen-induced rhinitis models and was recently demonstrated to inhibit SARS-CoV-2 infection in vitro. As such, we hypothesized that PPS may represent an attractive therapeutic that could be utilized for SARS-CoV-2 infection and COVID-19. Using the K18-hACE2 mouse model of SARS-CoV-2 infection, we administered PPS (6 mg/kg) from either 1 (early) or 3 (late) days post-infection via intranasal instillation and then examined the efficacy in mitigating viral-induced inflammation and severe disease outcomes. We found that the early administration of PPS was accompanied by significant improvements in weight loss, clinical disease presentation, and neutrophilic airway inflammation. Early PPS administration also significantly reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine production at both the mRNA and protein levels while having no impact on viral titers or interferon and antiviral gene expression. Histologically, early treatment significantly prevented severe pulmonary inflammation and tissue remodeling. Comparatively, late administration of PPS worsened weight loss and clinical disease presentation following SARS-CoV-2 infection. Moreover, late administration was unable to prevent significant increases in pro-inflammatory cytokines and was further associated with significantly downregulated antiviral-associated genes. Histological examination also showed no protection in the late PPS administered groups. Taken together, these findings underscore the significance of time-dependent administration and demonstrate the therapeutic potential of PPS for treatment of SARS-CoV-2-induced inflammation. IMPORTANCE: Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) continues to cause infections globally, with most cases resulting in mild to moderate disease outcomes. However, approximately 10% of patients experience virally induced hyperinflammation leading to poor outcomes. As such, new or repurposed therapeutics need to be rapidly implemented to address this urgent medical need. Here, we show that pentosan polysulfate sodium (PPS) is a leading Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved therapeutic that significantly mitigates SARS-CoV-2-induced pulmonary inflammation. Critically, timing of PPS during the infection establishment and progression is critical for PPS efficacy, highlighting time-dependent responses that must be considered for further human clinical implementation. The findings from this study demonstrate that PPS holds significant promise as a repurposed anti-inflammatory agent for SARS-CoV-2 infection.

title: From early recognition to precision medicine: advances in the diagnosis and management of adult sepsis and septic shock-a narrative review.
abstract: PURPOSE: Emerging diagnostic, computational, and precision approaches are expanding the ability to detect, classify, and biologically characterise sepsis, but their translation into clinical benefit depends on whether added information changes management and, ultimately, improves patient-centred outcomes. This review evaluates selected advances in adult sepsis and septic shock through a framework of clinical actionability. METHODS: A focused PubMed search was supplemented by major international guidelines, targeted searches, and reference-list screening through August 2026. Priority was given to randomised trials, systematic reviews and meta-analyses, multicentre studies, and prospective or external validation studies relevant to clinical implementation. RESULTS: We developed a two-gap framework to distinguish gains in information from clinically meaningful translation. The information-to-action gap describes situations in which improved detection, prediction, biological classification, or physiological assessment does not alter management; the decision-to-outcome gap describes management changes without demonstrated patient-centred benefit. Digital alerts, rapid diagnostics, host-response assays, physiology-guided resuscitation, and phenotype- or biomarker-guided strategies show differing degrees of actionability. Across these domains, reproducibility, transportability, workflow integration, timing, temporal stability, and treatment-predictive validity remain key constraints. CONCLUSION: Most of the emerging diagnostic, computational, and precision approaches reviewed here have not yet established a routine role in sepsis care. Established evidence-based management therefore remains the clinical foundation, while newer strategies should be evaluated prospectively for their ability to close the information-to-action and decision-to-outcome gaps.

title: Intranasal immunization expressing S1 antigen can confer functionally sterile protection against an intranasal SARS-CoV-2 challenge in mice.
abstract: Currently approved COVID-19 vaccines have shown significant protective efficacy against disease onset and progression after SARS-CoV-2 infection. However, systemic immune responses induced by intramuscular vaccination have limited impact on protection of viral transmission. Intranasal vaccination is an important strategy for induction of mucosal immune responses for protection of viral transmission. Here, we investigated the potential of intranasal immunization expressing a SARS-CoV-2 spike (S) antigen to prevent SARS-CoV-2 infection in a mice model. Intranasal immunization with a Sendai virus vector expressing SARS-CoV-2 S1 domain fused with the trimerization domain of T4 fibritin induced neutralizing antibodies detected not only in plasma but also in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) in BALB/c mice. After an intranasal challenge with a mouse-adapted SARS-CoV-2 strain QHmusX, all the unimmunized mice (n = 9) showed significant body weight loss and high viral load in BALF. In contrast, the intranasally-immunized mice (n = 8) had no detectable viral sgRNA nor infectious viruses in BALF except for one mouse with marginal level of sgRNA, showing no body weight loss. This study indicates that intranasal immunization expressing S1 antigen can confer functionally sterile protection against SARS-CoV-2 infection.

title: Procalcitonin and Interleukin-18 in Umbilical Cord Blood as Early Diagnostic Biomarkers for Early-Onset Neonatal Sepsis: A Case-Control Study.
abstract: <b>Background and Objective:</b> Early-onset neonatal sepsis (EONS) is a major cause of neonatal morbidity and mortality globally, yet its early diagnosis remains challenging due to the limited availability of rapid, reliable biomarkers at the time of birth. This study aimed to analyze procalcitonin (PCT) and Interleukin-18 (IL-18) levels measured from umbilical cord blood as early diagnostic biomarkers for EONS. <b>Materials and Methods:</b> An observational case-control study was conducted on 66 neonates born with at least one EONS risk factor at four hospitals in Riau Province, Indonesia. Subjects were classified into an EONS group (n = 33) and a non-EONS group (n = 33). Umbilical cord blood PCT and IL-18 were measured using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Normality was assessed using the Shapiro-Wilk test. Between-group differences were analyzed using the Mann-Whitney U test (α = 0.05). <b>Results:</b> The PCT levels in umbilical cord blood were significantly higher in the EONS group compared to the non-EONS group [median 322.77 (range: 66.70-2599.57) pg/mL vs. 45.9 (4.90-321.97) pg/mL; p<0.001]. The IL-18 levels were similarly elevated [median 564.00 (216.40-1979.00) pg/mL vs. 107.60 (-19.60-773.38) pg/mL; p<0.001]. Maternal fever history was significantly more frequent in the EONS group (36.4% vs. 6.1%; p = 0.005), as was colored amniotic fluid (93.9% vs. 45.5%; p<0.001). <b>Conclusion:</b> Umbilical cord blood PCT and IL-18 levels are significantly elevated in neonates with EONS and may serve as early diagnostic biomarkers for EONS when measured at the time of birth. Their combined use may improve early risk stratification and clinical decision-making in at-risk neonates.
journal: Pakistan journal of biological sciences : PJBS

title: Effectiveness of Diphtheria and Tetanus Toxoids and Acellular Pertussis Vaccine in Children Aged 6 Months-6 Years During a Statewide Pertussis Outbreak - Alaska, May-November 2024.
abstract: Widespread use of pertussis vaccines in children has resulted in a >90% reduction in the number of annual pertussis cases in the United States. After a period of low U.S. pertussis incidence during and shortly after the COVID-19 pandemic, incidence increased in 2024. Data on the real-world effectiveness of diphtheria and tetanus toxoids and acellular pertussis vaccine (DTaP) against pertussis during this disease resurgence are limited. In response to documentation of a record high pertussis incidence in Alaska during May-November 2024, DTaP vaccine effectiveness (VE) against pertussis in Alaska children aged 6 months-6 years was evaluated. Adjusted VE was 96.2% among children who had completed the 3-dose primary DTaP series and 85.3% among those who were partially vaccinated. Compared with children who had received ≥3 DTaP doses, the odds of laboratory-confirmed pertussis were approximately 26 times as high in unvaccinated children (adjusted odds ratio [OR] = 26.1), and approximately 4 times as high in those who had received 1-2 DTaP doses (adjusted OR = 3.8). These findings reinforce the importance of following pertussis vaccination recommendations to protect for children from the disease and reduce the occurrence of pertussis outbreaks.
journal: MMWR. Morbidity and mortality weekly report

title: Temporal Changes in Inflammatory Markers and Laboratory Parameters in Relation to Risk of Neonatal Sepsis.
abstract: Background/Objective: Early diagnosis of neonatal sepsis remains a challenge due to the nonspecific nature of clinical symptoms and the delayed dynamics of conventional inflammatory markers. The traditional diagnostic approach is based on static cut-off points, which often do not consider the nonlinear nature of the inflammatory response. The aim of this study was to identify dynamic variables associated with sepsis progression, constituting the foundation for future artificial intelligence (AI) models. Methods: A retrospective analysis was performed using anonymised clinical and laboratory data from a cohort of newborns (n = 122) with suspected sepsis, along with maternal clinical data. Using feature engineering, descriptive statistics parameters were generated for selected parameters, including rates of change in the 24 h and 48 h time windows. This was combined with the verification of clinical and perinatal parameters that affect the assessment of clinical status and diagnosis of sepsis. The correlation analysis was performed using Spearman's rank correlation coefficient (p < 0.05). Results: Dynamic parameters showed significant associations with sepsis progression than static measurements. The highest correlation was recorded for the rate of CRP growth (CRP_abs_change_rate_max, r = 0.613, p < 0.001), compared with the maximum values (CRP_value_max, r = 0.591, p < 0.001). High correlations were also observed for leukocyte parameters, especially neutrophils (NEUT_%_pct_change_rate_max, r = 0.547, p < 0.001) and basophils (BASO_%_value_max, r = 0.606, p < 0.001), with the strongest correlations observed within the first 24 h (r > 0.70). Conclusions: Neonatal sepsis progression may be more comprehensively characterised by temporal changes in laboratory parameters, not by their absolute values. Rates of change in inflammatory markers may provide clinically relevant complementary information on the course of the disease, reflecting the complex and nonlinear nature of the inflammatory response. The results indicate that the analysis of the trajectory of changes in parameters provides a promising basis for the future development and validation of predictive models based on artificial intelligence for earlier and more accurate diagnosis of neonatal sepsis.

title: National variation in acute kidney injury diagnosis and monitoring across adult intensive care units in china: a nationwide cross-sectional survey.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is common in critically ill patients and strongly associated with adverse outcomes, yet national ICU-level evidence on AKI diagnosis and monitoring in China remains limited. METHODS: We conducted a nationwide anonymous cross-sectional web survey of adult ICUs in China from June 25 to September 26, 2025. The survey assessed AKI diagnosis and staging, UO and SCr monitoring across clinical scenarios, biomarker use, early warning systems, and changes in UO monitoring after AKI. We used multivariable logistic regression to identify factors associated with UO-monitoring practices, with FDR correction for multiple comparisons. An exploratory 0-100-point AKI-MIS summarised ICU-level monitoring implementation, with higher scores indicating broader implementation. RESULTS: Of 2,002 responses, 1,896 unique adult ICU units were included. AKI diagnosis was reported by 97.9% of ICUs, whereas 63.2% explicitly implemented staging and 75.9% used both UO and SCr for diagnosis. Hourly UO monitoring increased from 49.6% in routine practice to 74.1% in sepsis, 75.0% in AKI, and 77.7% in sepsis-associated AKI. Dynamic UO monitoring was implemented in 14.8% of ICUs; 83.5% reported increased nursing workload, and 69.9% identified workload or insufficient staffing as the main barrier. After FDR correction, geographic region, nurse-to-bed ratio, and baseline monitoring intensity were associated with UO-monitoring practices. The median AKI-MIS was 68.1 (IQR, 60.3-74.9), with higher adjusted scores in teaching hospitals. CONCLUSIONS: Among participating adult ICU units across all 31 provincial-level administrative regions of mainland China, AKI diagnosis and monitoring were widely reported, but substantial heterogeneity remained across monitoring systems. These findings provide a broad descriptive benchmark and identify priorities for strengthening standardisation, risk-responsive escalation, and closed-loop response pathways.

title: Longitudinal measurements of inflammatory mediators in patients at risk of sepsis in the Emergency Department.
abstract: Sepsis is a complex condition with time‐dependent evolution, and longitudinal biomarker dynamics may improve its characterisation. We hypothesised that biomarker kinetics are associated with sepsis, the intensity of organ dysfunction, and patient survival. This single‐centre, prospective, observational study included adult patients presenting to the Emergency Department with suspected infection and a National Early Warning Score 2 (NEWS2) ≥3. Blood samples were collected at baseline, 4 and 24 h and pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory cytokines, chemokines, as well as other inflammatory mediators or acute-phase reactants, were analysed. Linear and nonlinear mixed-effects models assessed associations between biomarker trajectories over time, sepsis diagnosis, and organ dysfunction severity. Joint models evaluated the predictive value of biomarker kinetics during the first 24 h for in‐hospital mortality. Of 214 screened patients, 173 were analysed and 137(79%) developed sepsis. Linear and nonlinear mixed models showed significant time‐dependent decreases in IL10 (β -0.016, 95%CI -0.028 to -0.004), IL1RN (β -0.014, 95%CI -0.024 to -0.004), and IL6 (β -1.021, 95%CI -1.609 to -0.433 for the first spline 0-4 h). Sepsis diagnosis was associated with higher IL1RN (β 0.378, 95%CI 0.153-0.603) and TNFRSF1A (β 0.40, 95%CI 0.21-0.58); a significant interaction between sepsis and time was observed only for IL6 (β -0.33, CI95% -0.653 to-0.007) for the second spline 4-24 h. Increasing SOFA scores correlated with elevated IL10 (β 0.048), IL1RN (β 0.044), CCL2 (β 0.046), TNFRSF1A (β 0.050), and procalcitonin (PCT; β 2.15), all p < 0.01. The SOFA score-time interaction was significant only for IL6 (β 0.122, 95%CI 0.006 to 0.238 during the first spline 0-4 h followed by β -0.080, 95%CI -0.133 to -0.027 for the second spline 4-24 h). Joint survival models adjusted identified associations between longitudinal IL8 (HR 0.655, 95%CrI 0.582-0.728), TNFRSF1A (HR 0.505, 95%CrI 0.419-0.682), and PCT (HR 1.004, 95%CrI 1.001-1.008) concentrations and survival outcome. However, IL8 and TNFRSF1A showed an unexpected inverse association with survival, and the overall discriminatory performance was modest. In conclusion, Sepsis status and organ dysfunction severity were associated with distinct inflammatory biomarker levels and kinetics. IL6 showed a unique time‐dependent relationship, whereas the dynamics of TNFRSF1A, IL8 and PCT showed exploratory associations with survival. Further studies are warranted to confirm our results.

title: [L-lactylation regulatory network in orthopedic degenerative diseases].
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To explore the therapeutic potential of L-lactylation in degenerative disc disease, arthritis, muscle degeneration, exercise metabolism, and osteoporosis. METHODS: Literatures about L-lactylation in metabolic regulation, inflammatory response, and bone homeostasis at home and abroad in recent years were extensively reviewed. Emphasis was placed on analyzing the molecular regulatory networks of L-lactylation and its related clinical therapeutic potential in intervertebral disc degenerative diseases, arthritis, muscle degeneration and exercise metabolism, and osteoporosis. RESULTS: L-lactylation reprograms metabolic flux by modifying key enzymes, and regulates chromatin dynamics through histone/non-histone modifications, thereby modulating macrophage polarization, osteoclast-osteoblast balance, and extracellular matrix remodeling. In intervertebral disc degeneration, tumor necrosis factor α activates glycolytic enzymes to promote L-lactylation, while glutamine supplementation reduces L-lactylation levels and activates the adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase catalytic subunit α pathway; hypoxia inducible factor 1α promotes the extracellular transport of L-lactylation by upregulating monocarboxylate transporter 4. In osteoarthritis, lactate dehydrogenase A (LDHA) overexpression leads to elevated histone L-lactylation levels, which in turn upregulates the transcriptional activity of triosephosphate isomerase 1 and accelerates cartilage degradation. In rheumatoid arthritis, artemisinin induces L-lactylation of pyruvate kinase M2 and inhibits the proliferation and migration of fibroblast-like synoviocytes. In tendinopathy, L-lactylation exerts regulatory effects in the aspects of extracellular matrix, immunity, nerves and blood vessels. In osteoporosis, L-lactylation affects osteogenic differentiation and bone resorption through regulatory axes such as Forkhead box F1, crystallin alpha B/ferritin heavy chain 1, and JunB, and interventions including LDHA regulation and scopolamine administration can promote osteogenic differentiation. CONCLUSION: L-lactylation plays a dual regulatory role in orthopedic degenerative diseases, and its spatiotemporal dynamics and tissue specificity provide new opportunities for precise treatment. Although target specificity and clinical validation still face challenges, targeting L-lactylation modification is expected to become a new direction for disease-modifying therapy of orthopedic degenerative diseases.

title: Disseminated Tuberculosis With Ocular Involvement After 12 Years of Anti-TNF-α Therapy.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Ocular tuberculosis (TB) is an uncommon yet potentially vision-threatening manifestation of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, particularly difficult to diagnose in immunocompromised individuals. The increasing use of anti-tumor necrosis factor-α (anti-TNF-α) agents has markedly heightened the risk of TB reactivation, often with disseminated or extrapulmonary involvement despite negative baseline screening. CASE PRESENTATION: We describe a 52-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis receiving long-term adalimumab and methotrexate who developed disseminated TB with pulmonary, splenic, and ocular involvement after 12 years of anti-TNF-α therapy. Baseline screening had shown a negative tuberculin skin test and an indeterminate interferon-γ release assay. She presented with constitutional and respiratory symptoms, whereas chest computed tomography demonstrated diffuse micronodular infiltrates consistent with miliary TB. Microbiological confirmation was obtained via bronchoalveolar lavage. Ophthalmologic evaluation revealed bilateral choroidal granulomas with subretinal edema, leading to a diagnosis of ocular TB. Standard antitubercular therapy (ATT) was initiated but required modification due to drug-induced liver injury. Adjunctive systemic corticosteroids were introduced after antimicrobial therapy and gradually tapered. The patient achieved progressive clinical, radiological, and ophthalmologic improvement, with gradual regression of choroidal lesions. DISCUSSION: This case underscores the persistent long-term risk of TB reactivation during prolonged anti-TNF-α therapy and highlights the limitations of current screening strategies in immunosuppressed patients. Ocular TB requires integration of systemic, clinical, and imaging findings; in this patient, microbiologically confirmed disseminated TB together with characteristic bilateral choroidal granulomas supported a definitive diagnosis. Management relies on prompt ATT, discontinuation of immunosuppression, and judicious use of adjunctive corticosteroids. Long-term follow-up is essential given the risk of persistent lesions and late recurrence. Reintroduction of biologic therapy may be feasible in selected cases but requires careful risk stratification. CONCLUSION: TB should remain a diagnostic consideration in patients receiving biologic therapy who develop compatible systemic or ocular manifestations, even after long-term treatment and negative baseline screening. Close multidisciplinary collaboration is essential for the diagnosis and management of ocular TB in this population.

title: Application of CAR-T cell therapy in orthopedics: From bone malignancies to non-malignant musculoskeletal disorders.
abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy has transformed hematologic oncology, but its application in orthopaedic diseases remains at an early stage. In bone malignancies, including osteosarcoma, chondrosarcoma, Ewing sarcoma, and bone metastases, antigen heterogeneity, limited trafficking and persistence, and the immunosuppressive skeletal microenvironment restrict efficacy. CAR-engineered approaches are also emerging in non-malignant disorders: CD19-directed CAR-T therapy has shown early clinical activity in refractory rheumatoid arthritis and other autoimmune rheumatic diseases, whereas senolytic CAR-T strategies for osteoarthritis remain preclinical. This review summarizes current evidence across malignant and non-malignant orthopaedic conditions, with emphasis on target selection, safety, and translational feasibility. Key barriers include antigen escape, impaired infiltration, limited persistence, local immunosuppression, manufacturing complexity, and on-target/off-tumour toxicity. Emerging strategies include multi-target receptors, chemokine receptor engineering, locoregional delivery, safety-control systems, and allogeneic or point-of-care manufacturing. Current evidence supports CAR-T and related CAR-engineered cells as potential complementary approaches for selected refractory orthopaedic conditions, although further translation requires stronger clinical evidence and improved biological and manufacturing strategies. The Translational Potential of this Article: This review identifies disease-specific targets, barriers, and engineering priorities relevant to translating CAR-engineered cell therapies into orthopaedic practice. These considerations may inform preclinical validation and early-phase trials in refractory bone malignancies and selected non-malignant musculoskeletal disorders.

title: Targeting pathogenic immune cells in rheumatoid arthritis: emerging immunotherapeutic frontiers.
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a persistent autoimmune condition that predominantly affects the joints resulting in inflammation, pain and progressive disability. Immunological imbalance, especially the stimulation of pathogenic immune cells, including T and B cells, macrophages, amongst others, is the cause of the disease, as it is critical to the development of the disease. The limitation of traditional anti-RA medications, such as non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs (DMARDs), in the treatment of the disease led to the development of more specific medicines. One of the most promising biologic agents, including monoclonal antibodies, cytokine inhibitors and cell-based therapies, are specifically targeting immune cells and inflammatory pathways in RA. This review examines these new immunotherapies, their mechanisms of action, clinical efficacy, and challenges associated with them, including resistance to treatment, safety issues, and the necessity to use personalised therapy. Also, the new immunotherapeutic approaches, which include targeting autoantibodies, gene therapy, and precision medicine, are promising new approaches that could result in more effective and personalised treatments. Finally, the review concludes with a discussion of future directions, where in combination therapies, next-generation biologics, and personalised treatment regimens are also possible and can change the way RA can be managed in the future. To preserve analytical depth, this review explicitly distinguishes established (regulatory-approved) therapies from investigational and experimental approaches and indicates the level of clinical evidence for each.

title: RNA therapeutics in rheumatoid arthritis, systemic lupus erythematosus, and systemic sclerosis: a compartment-aware translational framework.
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA), systemic lupus erythematosus/lupus nephritis (SLE/LN), and systemic sclerosis (SSc) remain major causes of chronic inflammation, disability, organ damage, and treatment burden despite therapeutic advances. RNA therapeutics offer programmable transcript suppression, network-level microRNA modulation, transient restoration of protective proteins, and targeting-ligand functions. Existing reviews largely catalogue modalities or individual delivery systems; this review instead asks whether a candidate forms an interpretable translational program across target biology, disease compartment, intended cell, productive intracellular access, direct target engagement, pathway pharmacodynamics, repeat-dose safety, and manufacturing feasibility. RA is primarily a synovial immune-stromal delivery problem in which RNA programs must also demonstrate an advantage over effective biologic or targeted synthetic therapies. SLE/LN offers interferon, B-cell, co-stimulatory, microRNA, messenger RNA (mRNA), and complement opportunities, but therapeutic nucleic acids and carriers must not intensify nucleic-acid sensing, interferon activity, or complement-associated injury. SSc combines strong antifibrotic RNA biology with an accessible skin proof-of-mechanism window, whereas lung, vascular, and internal-organ programs remain more delivery-limited. We separate human pathway validation, RNA-platform evidence outside the target disease, disease-specific RNA evidence, and patient efficacy. Recent human complement-factor-B pharmacodynamic data strengthen the platform-level evidence but do not establish efficacy in RA or LN. The most informative early trials will therefore be biomarker-enriched and mechanism-rich, with prespecified criteria that distinguish target failure from delivery, dose, endotype, or safety failure.

title: A gut microbiota-metabolite-host gene score for subtyping and predicting the treatment response in rheumatoid arthritis: integrative analysis with in silico knockout validation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The pathogenesis of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) involves a complex interplay between immune dysregulation and metabolic disturbance, with the gut microbiota and its metabolites playing pivotal roles. However, integrated biomarkers based on the "gut microbiota-metabolite-host gene" regulatory axis that can quantify its impact on RA stratification and therapeutic response are lacking. METHODS: We integrated multiple RA transcriptomic datasets to screen for host genes explicitly associated with the gut microbiota and metabolites using the gutMGene database. A gut microbiota-metabolite-host score (GMS) was constructed via principal component analysis (PCA). Immune infiltration patterns were evaluated using CIBERSORT. Furthermore, scRNA-seq was employed to map the cellular origins of key genes, and in silico knockout analysis using scTenifoldKnk was performed to simulate the functional ablation of core host genes within this regulatory axis. Additionally, molecular docking was conducted to validate the binding affinities between the key host proteins and the optimal small molecule. RESULTS: We identified seven microbiota-metabolite-host hub genes (FOS, JUN, IDO1, PEMT, EGFR, ABCC4, and FADS3) and constructed the GMS. The GMS stratified patients with RA into two distinct functional subtypes: an adaptive immune activation subtype and an inflammatory-metabolic composite subtype. Notably, the GMS demonstrated superior performance in predicting responses to anti-TNF and rituximab therapies. The scRNA-seq analysis revealed high expression of FOS and JUN in T cells and NK cells. In silico knockout analysis further revealed the central transcription factors FOS and JUN as key executors of this axis, as their ablation significantly affected osteoclast differentiation and the enrichment of TNF/MAPK inflammatory pathways. These computational findings support the core mechanism by which gut microbiota-metabolite signalling drives RA joint pathology via FOS/JUN. Molecular docking results confirmed strong binding interactions between the identified active molecules and their respective target proteins. CONCLUSION: This study establishes a GMS based on the gut microbiota-metabolite-host gene regulatory axis as a robust tool for molecular subtyping and predicting biological therapy responses in patients with RA. Crucially, through integrated computational modelling, including in silico knockout and molecular docking validation, we identified FOS/JUN as critical executor genes linking the gut microenvironment to RA bone destruction, providing novel targets for therapeutic strategies aimed at the gut-joint axis.

title: Superior sagittal sinus thrombosis with intracranial hemorrhage in a patient on infliximab: a case report.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Superior sagittal sinus thrombosis (SSST) is a rare but life-threatening form of cerebral venous thrombosis. Although several prothrombotic and autoimmune conditions are recognized risk factors, SSST occurring in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) receiving tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α) inhibitor therapy remains exceptionally rare and poorly described in the literature. CASE PRESENTATION: We present a 59-year-old Caucasian female with RA treated with infliximab who developed extensive superior sagittal sinus thrombosis with concurrent intracranial and subarachnoid hemorrhage. The patient was managed with anticoagulation, blood pressure control, and seizure prophylaxis, with subsequent clinical and radiologic improvement at one-month follow-up. Hypercoagulability evaluation was overall unrevealing, and no other clear provoking etiology was identified. CONCLUSIONS: Given the rarity of this presentation, we report this case to raise awareness of a possible association between cerebral venous thrombosis and TNF-α inhibitor therapy in patients with rheumatoid arthritis. This is especially important given the increasing and widespread use of biologic agents in the treatment of autoimmune diseases.

title: Therapeutic potential of zinc supplementation in rheumatoid arthritis: clinical evidence, molecular mechanisms, and formulation-specific effects.
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic inflammatory autoimmune disorder primarily affecting the synovial joints, characterized by persistent synovitis, progressive joint destruction, and systemic complications that contribute to significant morbidity. Despite advances in disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs and biologic therapies, many patients fail to achieve sustained disease control or experience treatment-related adverse effects, highlighting the need for safe adjunctive strategies. Zinc, an essential trace element with critical roles in immune regulation, antioxidant defense, and inflammatory signaling, has gained increasing attention in the pathogenesis and management of RA. Clinical studies consistently report altered zinc homeostasis and reduced circulating zinc levels in RA, which are associated with increased disease activity, oxidative stress, and immune dysregulation. However, human interventional studies evaluating zinc supplementation remain limited, involve relatively small sample sizes, and report heterogeneous findings. In contrast, experimental studies in validated animal models have more consistently demonstrated anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory effects of zinc, including modulation of macrophage and T-cell activation, cytokine production, synovial fibroblast behaviour, and bone remodelling. Importantly, the therapeutic effects of zinc appear to be formulation-dependent, as organic zinc salts, chelated forms, and emerging nano-based formulations have demonstrated superior bioavailability and anti-inflammatory efficacy compared with conventional inorganic salts. This review aims to explain the molecular and immunological mechanisms underlying the effect of zinc in RA, evaluates findings from clinical and preclinical studies of zinc supplementation, and highlights formulation-specific considerations relevant to clinical practice. While existing evidence supports the potential of zinc as a safe and beneficial adjunct to conventional RA therapy, further well-designed randomized clinical trials are required to establish optimal dosing strategies and identify patient populations most likely to benefit.
journal: Biometals : an international journal on the role of metal ions in biology, biochemistry, and medicine

title: Diagnostic utility of the modified inflammatory burden index and PCT/LYM ratio for sepsis stratification and early prediction of septic shock.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the diagnostic performance of a modified inflammatory burden index (mIBI) and conventional biomarkers in sepsis and septic shock and assess the clinical utility of their combined application with the PCT/LYM ratio. METHODS: A retrospective analysis included 45 patients with sepsis, 77 with septic shock, and 54 with non-septic infectious inflammation (control). Levels of procalcitonin (PCT), C-reactive protein (CRP), interleukin-6 (IL-6), neutrophil count (NEU), and lymphocyte count (LYM) were measured. Composite indices including mIBI, PCT/LYM, CRP/LYM, and NLR were calculated. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated the independent diagnostic value of mIBI and PCT/LYM after adjusting for confounders. RESULTS: Inflammatory markers and composite indices increased progressively from control to sepsis to septic shock, whereas LYM decreased (all P < 0.05). For sepsis diagnosis, PCT/LYM showed strong diagnostic performance (AUC = 0.851, 95% CI: 0.775-0.928; sensitivity 80.00%, specificity 81.48% at cutoff 0.91), followed by mIBI (AUC = 0.806, specificity 88.89%). For septic shock, PCT/LYM (AUC = 0.880) and mIBI (AUC = 0.877) were comparable to PCT and IL-6 (all AUC = 0.879). Multivariable analysis revealed that after adjustment for age, sex, qSOFA, diabetes, and renal insufficiency, both log10(mIBI) (OR = 2.771, P < 0.001) and PCT/LYM (OR = 1.045, P = 0.002) were independent predictors for sepsis. For septic shock, log10(mIBI) retained independent predictive capacity (OR = 1.399, P = 0.030), whereas PCT/LYM showed a borderline association (OR = 1.004, P = 0.053). CONCLUSION: The composite framework integrating PCT/LYM and mIBI addresses limitations of single biomarkers. PCT/LYM demonstrated independent predictive value, with a numerically higher AUC than PCT alone for both sepsis and septic shock, although the direct DeLong comparison did not reach statistical significance, supporting its potential utility as part of a composite screening approach. Modified IBI showed strong independent diagnostic value for sepsis and high univariate discriminative ability for septic shock. These routinely available indicators offer timely, cost-effective advantages for early sepsis identification and risk stratification.
journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

title: Eosinophils, malignant brain edema, and functional outcome after mechanical thrombectomy: a mediation analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To examine the independent associations of admission eosinophil count with malignant brain edema (MBE) and with poor 3-month functional outcome after mechanical thrombectomy (MT), and to quantify the statistical contribution of MBE to the eosinophil-outcome association using mediation analysis. METHODS: A total of 442 consecutive AIS patients who underwent MT between May 2017 and January 2023 were analyzed. Multivariable logistic regression analysis was used to assess the association of eosinophils with MBE and poor outcome. Mediation analysis was performed to quantify the statistical contribution of MBE. RESULTS: MBE developed in 98 (22.17%) patients. After full adjustment for confounders, each 1-standard deviation increase in standardized eosinophils was independently associated with a lower risk of MBE (OR = 0.165; 95% CI: 0.055-0.498; p = 0.00137). Consistent findings were observed when eosinophils were dichotomized by the median value (OR = 0.168; 95% CI: 0.086-0.328; p < 0.00001). Standardized eosinophils were also independently associated with reduced risk of poor outcome (OR = 0.620; 95% CI: 0.475-0.810; p = 0.00045). Mediation analysis showed a small statistical contribution of MBE to the eosinophil-outcome association: the indirect effect was -0.2109 (95% CI: -0.4016 to -0.0500; p < 0.001), and the mediated proportion was 12.05% (95% CI: 2.92-26%). CONCLUSION: Lower admission eosinophil levels were independently associated with higher risks of MBE and poor 3-month functional outcome. Mediation analysis indicated that MBE statistically accounted for 12.05% (95% CI: 2.92-26%) of the eosinophil-outcome association. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require external multicenter validation.

title: Case Report and literature review: complications of the association between rheumatoid arthritis and tuberculosis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Pulmonary tuberculosis is one of the major public health issues globally. According to the World Health Organization, it is among the top 10 causes of death caused by a single pathogen. In Romania, its reported incidence rate in 2024 was approximately 60 per 100,000 people, making it the country with the highest incidence in Europe. Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a systemic chronic autoimmune inflammatory disease characterized by the destruction of the small joints along with symmetrical distribution and multiorgan involvement. Pulmonary manifestations are more common in males with positive serology and can involve the lungs, airways, or pleura. Short-term corticotherapy may be initiated in patients with severe symptoms, and biological therapy (anti-TNF alpha drugs) may be used in those with inefficiency of disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs, with an increased risk for disseminated forms of tuberculosis in those with latent infection. CASE DESCRIPTION: We present the case of a 38-year-old male patient with a 5-year history of seropositive RA who was treated with methotrexate and methylprednisolone, without any prior investigations for latent tuberculosis infection or any chest radiography performed, and was admitted with severe respiratory failure. The results of thoracic computed tomography showed bilateral pneumothorax and pneumomediastinum, with pulmonary lesions suggestive of a diagnosis of tuberculosis, which was confirmed by bacteriological testing of samples. CONCLUSION: The coexistence of two severe diseases-one requiring immunosuppressive treatment and the other one favored by immunosuppression-in a country with a high prevalence of tuberculosis infection and in the absence of latent tuberculosis infection screening or periodic pulmonological assessment can lead to severe, life-threatening complications that require complex, multidisciplinary, long-term, and expensive management.

title: Dual-phase CTA filling pattern is associated with reperfusion-related complications after mechanical thrombectomy in late-window anterior circulation stroke.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether pre-treatment dual-phase computed tomography angiography (CTA) filling patterns are independently associated with reperfusion-related complications after late-window mechanical thrombectomy and whether they provide incremental prognostic value beyond conventional clinical and imaging variables. METHODS: We conducted a prospective single-center cohort study including 80 consecutive patients with anterior circulation large-vessel occlusion who underwent mechanical thrombectomy within 6-24 h after stroke onset or last known well. Dual-phase CTA filling patterns were classified as good early filling, delayed filling, or persistent poor filling; delayed and persistent poor filling were combined for the primary analyses. The primary outcome was a composite of reperfusion-related complications within 72 h, including hemorrhagic transformation ≥HI2, malignant cerebral edema, or early neurological deterioration. Secondary outcomes were 90-day functional independence and all-cause mortality. Independent predictors were identified using Firth penalized logistic regression. Incremental model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis, bootstrap internal validation, reclassification metrics, and decision-curve analysis. RESULTS: Reperfusion-related complications occurred in 28 patients (35%) and were significantly more frequent in patients with delayed or poor filling than in those with good early filling (56% vs. 20%; p < 0.001). Delayed or poor filling independently predicted reperfusion-related complications after adjustment for age, baseline NIHSS score, and ASPECTS (adjusted OR 3.97, 95% CI 1.22-14.10; p = 0.022). Older age was also independently associated with increased risk (adjusted OR 2.14 per 10-year increase, 95% CI 1.24-4.12; p = 0.005), whereas higher ASPECTS was protective (adjusted OR 0.35 per point, 95% CI 0.18-0.61; p < 0.001). The full model incorporating dual-phase CTA achieved excellent discrimination (AUC 0.895; optimism-corrected AUC 0.867). Addition of the dual-phase CTA filling pattern improved patient risk reclassification, although the increase in discrimination beyond the clinical-plus-ASPECTS model was not statistically significant. Patients with delayed or poor filling had substantially worse 90-day outcomes, including lower functional independence (24% vs. 70%) and higher mortality (38% vs. 4%) (both p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Delayed or persistent poor filling on dual-phase CTA is an independent imaging marker of reperfusion-related complications following late-window mechanical thrombectomy. Although its incremental contribution to model discrimination was modest, dual-phase CTA may improve early risk stratification and help identify patients who may benefit from intensified post-procedural monitoring. External validation is warranted before routine clinical implementation.

title: Dynamic perioperative thrombo-inflammatory biomarkers correlate with early functional outcomes after mechanical thrombectomy for acute ischemic stroke.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Inflammatory and coagulation responses continue to evolve after mechanical thrombectomy for acute ischaemic stroke. A single admission measurement may therefore miss clinically relevant perioperative biology. We examined whether longitudinal thrombo-inflammatory biomarker profiles were associated with early functional and neurological outcomes after thrombectomy. METHODS: This single-centre retrospective cohort study grouped routine laboratory measurements into baseline (-3 to 0 days), postoperative days 1-3, 4-7, and 8-14. The primary endpoint was an unfavourable discharge modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 3-6. Failure of in-hospital early neurological improvement, defined as an admission-to-discharge NIHSS reduction of <4 points without a discharge NIHSS of 0-1, was examined as a secondary dynamic neurological endpoint. Biomarker associations were estimated using logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, and admission NIHSS. The clinical and combined models were compared in the same 586-patient complete-case subset. RESULTS: Amongst 963 registry patients, 801 had discharge mRS data; 428 had favourable and 373 had unfavourable outcomes. Higher baseline NLR (OR 1.30, 95% CI 1.08-1.58), peak first-week NLR (OR 1.26, 95% CI 1.08-1.48), peak 1st-week D-dimer (OR 1.07, 95% CI 1.01-1.14), and lower baseline fibrinogen (OR 0.78, 95% CI 0.63-0.97) and minimum first-week lymphocyte count (OR 0.67, 95% CI 0.54-0.84) were independently associated with an unfavourable discharge outcome. Baseline platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio and white blood cell count on postoperative days 4-7 and 8-14 were also associated after adjustment. The principal biomarker signals were directionally consistent for failure of in-hospital early neurological improvement. In the matched subset, the clinical model had an AUC of 0.709 and the combined model an AUC of 0.726; the paired AUC difference was 0.017 (95% bootstrap CI -0.003 to 0.037). CONCLUSION: Dynamic perioperative thrombo-inflammatory profiles were associated with early disability and neurological recovery after thrombectomy. Their incremental discrimination beyond basic clinical variables was small and statistically uncertain. These findings are exploratory and require prospective, multicentre validation with standardised sampling before clinical implementation.

title: Differences in SARS-CoV-2 rapid diagnostic testing usage by COVID-19 vaccination status can bias vaccine effectiveness estimates against symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection from a test-negative design.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Use of rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs) may bias vaccine effectiveness (VE) estimates from test-negative design (TND) studies. We conducted individual-level simulations using national, US COVID-19 surveillance data to assess potential bias at varying likelihoods of visiting a healthcare facility and prevalence of RDT use. METHODS: Twenty-one scenarios that varied the probabilities of visiting a healthcare facility and RDT use by vaccination status were simulated. VE was calculated as 100 × (1 - odds ratio), comparing the odds of symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection between vaccinated and unvaccinated groups of people. VE estimates were compared to VE estimates from simulations without RDT testing to calculate the bias in percentage points (pp).
