RESULTS: VE was underestimated when either vaccinated people were more likely (probability of .5) than unvaccinated people (probability of .3) to visit a healthcare facility after a positive RDT [-5.8%age points (pp); 95% uncertainty interval (UI): -9.1, -2.4] or unvaccinated people were more likely than vaccinated people to visit a healthcare facility after a negative RDT (bias = -6.1 pp; UI: -9.9, -2.5). Conversely, VE was overestimated when either vaccinated people were more likely than unvaccinated people to visit a healthcare facility after a negative RDT (bias = 5.2; UI: 2.4, 7.7) or unvaccinated people were more likely than vaccinated people to visit a healthcare facility after a positive RDT (bias = 8.4 pp; UI: 5.6, 11.3). CONCLUSION: VE estimates against symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection from a TND may be under- or overestimated, depending on differences in RDT usage between vaccination groups.

title: Incremental Predictive Value of Dynamic Platelet-to-Lymphocyte Ratio Beyond ESR and CRP for Glucocorticoid Sparing in Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Multi-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To identify independent predictors of sustained glucocorticoid (GC) sparing in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) initiating biological or targeted synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (b/tsDMARDs), specifically we evaluated whether the longitudinal platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (ΔPLR) trajectory provides superior prognostic value compared to conventional measurements. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study analyzed 264 patients from the Taipei Medical University Clinical Research Database. Sparing success was defined as achieving predefined dose reduction targets at month 6 and maintaining stability for ≥ 12 weeks. Candidate predictors were screened using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, followed by multivariable logistic and Cox proportional hazards modeling. Clinical utility was assessed using "rescue rate" analysis. RESULTS: Sustained GC sparing was achieved by 139 (52.7%) patients. First-line b/tsDMARD initiation was the strongest predictor (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 4.23, p < 0.001) of GC-sparing success. Although static baseline inflammatory markers were non-predictive, every 10% reduction in 6-month ΔPLR independently increased success odds (aOR 1.05 [inverted from 0.95 per 10% increase], p = 0.009) and significantly accelerated the sparing rate (hazard ratio [HR] 1.02, p = 0.021). Conversely, concomitant nonsteroidal antiinflammatory drug use hindered success. Notably, incorporating ΔPLR into the predictive model "rescued" 16.5% of unrecognized candidates for de-escalation-patients capable of successful GC sparing who were misclassified by standard clinical models. CONCLUSION: Although static baseline inflammatory markers are nonpredictive, 6-month ΔPLR offers significant incremental prognostic value beyond conventional erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP). By identifying 16.5% of viable candidates overlooked by standard assessments, dynamic PLR monitoring offers a potential strategy to optimize precision steroid de-escalation in RA.

title: Real-World Outcomes of the SolitaireTM and ReactTM Devices from India's First Multicenter Mechanical Thrombectomy Registry.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: There is a low utilization of mechanical thrombectomy (MT) in India and lack of a nationwide registry or data. This registry aimed to study the systems of care, functional outcomes, and cost effectiveness of MT treatment in patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS). METHODS: Patients were treated with SolitaireTM X and/or ReactTM catheter as the primary device/s. Subjects with AIS due to large vessel occlusion, within 24 hours of symptom onset with the Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score (ASPECTS) score >5 and the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) ≥6 were included. An independent Core lab and clinical events committee assessed outcomes. Good functional outcome was defined as modified Rankin score of 0-2 at 90 days. Successful revascularization was defined as the modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction (mTICI) ≥ 2b. Performance measures included door to needle time, door to groin puncture time, and groin puncture to recanalization time. A cost-effectiveness model was also developed. RESULTS: Of the 200 patients screened, 190 (mean age, 59.6±14.35 years) were included. The mean baseline NIHSS score was 14.7 ± 5.38, median door to needle time was 50 (10-173) mins, door to groin puncture time was 99 (11- 478) mins, and groin puncture to revascularization time was 40 (10-170) mins. The first pass mTICI≥2b was 127 (66.8%) and the final pass mTICI≥2b was attained in 167 (87.9%). A good functional outcome was seen in 123 (65.8%) patients. Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 4 (2.1%). Device and/or procedure-related serious adverse events occurred in 27 (14.2%). Combined therapy of MT and Intravenous Tissue Plasminogen Activator [IV-tPA]was cost-effective compared with MT alone with an expected gain of 1.5 QALYs. CONCLUSIONS: This study results are comparable with global clinical registries and randomized clinical trials with favorable functional outcomes and excellent first pass and final recanalization. Combined therapy (MT + IV-tPA) was cost-effective compared to MT or IV-tPA alone.

title: Impact of cerebral venous outflow on futile recanalization despite complete reperfusion following mechanical thrombectomy.
abstract: BACKGROUND: A substantial proportion of patients with acute ischemic stroke remain functionally dependent despite complete angiographic reperfusion (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction [mTICI] 3) after mechanical thrombectomy (MT). This mismatch, commonly termed futile recanalization, may reflect tissue-level hypoperfusion not captured by arterial reperfusion grading. We investigated whether cerebral venous outflow, assessed using the Cortical Vein Opacification Score (COVES), provides prognostic information beyond conventional clinical and arterial imaging variables. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 420 adults with anterior-circulation large-vessel occlusion who underwent MT between 2015-2025 and achieved mTICI 3 reperfusion. Venous outflow was graded on baseline computed tomography angiography using COVES. Futile recanalization was defined as a 90-day modified Rankin Scale score of 3-6. Independent associations with futile recanalization were evaluated using multivariable binary logistic regression. RESULTS: Futile recanalization occurred in 191 patients (45.5%). After adjustment for age, admission NIHSS, ASPECTS, total passes, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, previous stroke, and arterial collateral status, higher COVES remained independently associated with lower odds of futile recanalization (OR per 1-point increase, 0.649; 95% CI, 0.537-0.784; p < 0.001). Age (OR, 1.031; p = 0.005), admission NIHSS (OR, 1.091; p = 0.001), and total passes (OR, 1.538; p < 0.001) were independently associated with higher odds of futile recanalization. Arterial collateral status was not independently associated with outcome. COVES showed greater discrimination than admission NIHSS (AUC, 0.742 vs 0.624). CONCLUSIONS: Baseline COVES was independently associated with 90-day functional outcome among patients achieving complete reperfusion after MT. COVES may serve as a complementary prognostic imaging marker rather than a treatment-selection tool. Prospective external validation is required.

title: Leucine-rich α-2-glycoprotein 1 as a promising biomarker and therapeutic target in sepsis: A review.
abstract: Sepsis is primarily characterized by a dysregulated host immune response. Identifying specific biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets has become a critical focus and key challenge in current research. Serum leucine-rich α-2-glycoprotein 1 (LRG1) is significantly elevated in sepsis. We aim to elucidate the potential roles of LRG1 in sepsis and its associated organ dysfunction as a specific biomarker for early diagnosis, prognosis assessment, or as an intervention target. This review summarizes the underlying mechanisms by which LRG1 contributes to the pathogenesis and progression of sepsis, particularly through its involvement in inflammation regulation, vascular function, and cell survival. Additionally, it consolidates current knowledge on LRG1 in sepsis, highlights its clinical application potential, and provides new support for precise diagnosis, prognostic evaluation, and targeted therapy. In conclusion, LRG1 emerges as a promising biomarker and therapeutic target for sepsis, playing a crucial role throughout the disease's onset, progression, and prognosis. This review offers new perspectives on LRG1 research and its application in sepsis.

title: Lung-brain-axis-mediated mechanisms of sepsis-associated encephalopathy secondary to lower respiratory tract infection: A narrative review.
abstract: Lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) represent one of the most frequent causes of sepsis. Sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE), a serious complication of sepsis, markedly increases patient mortality and the risk of long-term cognitive impairment. The emerging concept of the lung-brain axis offers a novel framework for understanding the pathogenesis of SAE. Unlike general reviews covering all-cause sepsis-associated encephalopathy, this review specifically focuses on SAE secondary to LRTI, and discriminates its unique epidemiological, clinical and mechanistic signatures from SAE triggered by abdominal, urinary or bloodstream infection. This review systematically summarizes the epidemiological characteristics of SAE induced by LRTIs, the anatomical and immunological basis of lung-brain interactions, and key pathological mechanisms including neuroinflammation, blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption, neurotransmitter imbalance, and mitochondrial dysfunction. Additionally, it highlights advances in biomarker research and clinical management strategies. By integrating evidence from molecular‐biology and neuroimaging studies, this article describes how pulmonary infections drive brain dysfunction via neural, immune, and endocrine pathways. These findings provide a theoretical foundation to support early diagnosis and targeted therapeutic interventions.

title: Early functional outcomes after mechanical thrombectomy in patients with large vessel occlusion and active cancer.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Evaluating mechanical thrombectomy (MT) in patients with large vessel occlusion stroke (LVOS) and active cancer (AC) is challenging because cancer-related mortality substantially affects conventional functional outcomes. This study aimed to assess the association between MT and early functional outcomes while minimizing the confounding impact of cancer-related death. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patients with LVOS and AC between January 2016 and December 2024. Patients were categorized into MT and non-MT groups. The primary outcome was the distribution of modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores at 2 weeks, analyzed using ordinal logistic regression. A sensitivity analysis excluding patients who died from cancer progression within 2 weeks of stroke onset was also performed. LVOS was defined as ischemic stroke with occlusion of the intra- or extracranial internal carotid artery, middle cerebral artery (M1 or M2 segments), or basilar artery. RESULTS: Among 72 patients with LVOS and AC (median age, 76 years; 36 women), 32 (44%) underwent MT (28 MT alone, and 4 MT procedures combined with intravenous thrombolysis), whereas 3 patients in the non-MT group received intravenous thrombolysis alone. At 2 weeks, MT was significantly associated with a favorable shift in mRS distribution (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 3.48, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.22-9.97; p = 0.020). In a sensitivity analysis excluding cancer-related deaths, this association remained significant, with a larger effect size (adjusted OR, 6.21, 95% CI, 1.89-20.47; p = 0.003). CONCLUSION: MT was associated with improved early functional outcomes in patients with LVOS and AC.
journal: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association

title: Transformative improvement with staggered gains in rheumatoid arthritis remission and sustained remission, but higher relapse rates: a population-based cohort study from 1990 to 2019.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To report population-level data describing long-term trends in remission, sustained remission and relapse among patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA). METHODS: We conducted a population-based inception cohort study of adults with incident RA in Olmsted County, Minnesota, USA, meeting 1987 or 2010 ACR criteria between 1990 and 2019. Patients were followed through 31 December 2023. We estimated cumulative incidence of first remission, sustained remission (≥6 months) and relapse after remission, accounting for competing risk of death. Cox models comparing calendar periods were adjusted for age, sex, baseline body mass index and serostatus. RESULTS: Among 1179 patients followed for a median of 9.4 years, 816 achieved remission and 630 achieved sustained remission. One-year remission, defined by our prespecified criteria, increased from 12.8% in 1990–1999 to 26.4% in 2010–2019. Median time to remission shortened from 6.4 years to 2.8 years. Despite these gains, relapse within 5 years after remission increased from 62.8% in 1990–1999 vs 79.2% in the 2010–2023 period. CONCLUSION: Remission in RA has become earlier and more frequent over time, but durability has not improved. Strategies to sustain remission remain a critical unmet need.

title: Sleep-Disordered Breathing Is Associated With Adverse Short- and Long-Term Outcomes in Acute Ischemic Stroke and TIA: A Retrospective Cohort Study From the Bern Sleep-Stroke Registry.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sleep-disordered breathing (SDB) is common after ischemic stroke and has been associated with adverse outcomes, yet evidence from large stroke cohorts remains limited. We evaluated the association of SDB severity with all-cause mortality, major adverse cardio- and cerebrovascular events (MACCE), and 3-month functional outcome. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients with ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack admitted to Inselspital Bern between 2017 and 2021 who underwent in-hospital respiratory polygraphy. SDB severity was classified according to the apnea-hypopnea index as mild (5-<15 events/h), moderate (15-<30 events/h), or severe (≥30 events/h). Outcomes included all-cause mortality, first postindex MACCE, and modified Rankin Scale scores at 3 months. Multivariable Cox and logistic regression models adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, vascular risk factors, admission National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale, intravenous thrombolysis, and mechanical thrombectomy. RESULTS: Among 1083 patients (mean age, 66.0±14.5 years; 62.6% male), SDB (apnea-hypopnea index ≥5 events/h) was present in 819 patients (75.6%), including mild (29.8%), moderate (22.9%), and severe (22.9%). Median follow-up was 51.1 months (interquartile range, 39.1-67.8) for mortality and 47.7 months (interquartile range, 36.9-65.5) for first postindex MACCE; 178 deaths and 153 of 880 patients experienced a first postindex MACCE. Severe SDB was independently associated with increased all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.73 [95% CI, 1.04-2.89]). Mild, moderate, and severe SDB were associated with first postindex MACCE (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.78 [95% CI, 1.03-3.06]; 2.20 [95% CI, 1.26-3.84]; and 2.16 [95% CI, 1.23-3.78], respectively; P for trend=0.009). Moderate and severe SDB were associated with unfavorable 3-month functional outcome (adjusted odds ratio, 1.74 [95% CI, 1.01-3.04] and 2.48 [95% CI, 1.45-4.31], respectively; P for trend <0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Severe SDB was independently associated with all-cause mortality, whereas SDB severity was associated with first postindex MACCE and unfavorable 3-month functional outcome. Acute-phase SDB assessment may improve prognostic risk stratification.

title: SGLT2 inhibitors and exercise in diabetic kidney disease: mechanistic rationale, emerging clinical evidence, and future perspectives.
abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is a major complication of diabetes and a leading cause of chronic kidney disease and kidney failure worldwide. Despite substantial advances in pharmacological therapy, residual risks of renal and cardiovascular disease remain considerable, underscoring the need for complementary therapeutic strategies. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors have emerged as cornerstone therapies for DKD because of their glucose-independent renoprotective and cardioprotective effects. Exercise, meanwhile, provides broad metabolic, cardiovascular, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant benefits and is recommended as an integral component of diabetes and chronic kidney disease management. Increasing evidence suggests that these two interventions may exert complementary effects on several interconnected pathways involved in DKD progression, including glomerular hyperfiltration, metabolic dysregulation, oxidative stress, inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and renal fibrosis. This review summarizes the pathophysiological mechanisms underlying DKD and examines the mechanistic rationale for integrating SGLT2 inhibitors with exercise. We further discuss emerging experimental and clinical evidence regarding their potential effects on renal function, metabolic control, cardiovascular health, and exercise capacity, together with important safety considerations and challenges in individualized exercise prescription. Although available evidence provides a biologically plausible basis for potentially additive interactions between these interventions, direct clinical evidence supporting the superiority of combined therapy over either intervention alone remains limited. We therefore highlight key knowledge gaps, including the lack of adequately powered randomized controlled trials, standardized exercise protocols, and validated biomarkers for monitoring treatment response. Future studies should establish the efficacy, safety, and optimal implementation of combined SGLT2 inhibitor and exercise strategies across different stages and phenotypes of DKD, thereby facilitating their translation into individualized cardiorenal care.

title: Fibrotic remodeling and stromal reprogramming in osteoarthritis: mechanisms, mechanobiology, and emerging therapeutic perspectives.
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) has traditionally been regarded as a degenerative joint disorder characterized primarily by cartilage erosion. However, growing evidence suggests that OA is a disorder of maladaptive whole-joint remodeling in which fibrotic remodeling represents an important yet underappreciated contributor to disease progression. Fibrotic remodeling is best documented in the synovium and joint capsule, with related stromal and extracellular matrix (ECM) changes also occurring in the infrapatellar fat pad and other joint compartments. Recent studies suggest that OA-associated fibrotic remodeling extends beyond passive scar formation and involves persistent stromal reprogramming, chronic inflammatory signaling, and mechanobiological adaptation. In this review, stromal reprogramming is used as a conceptual framework describing persistent alterations in stromal cell state that extend beyond transient fibroblast activation or fibroblast-to-myofibroblast transition (FMT). These alterations may involve sustained transcriptional programs, altered mechanosensitivity, metabolic or epigenetic adaptation, and incomplete restoration of tissue homeostasis. However, direct evidence demonstrating stable long-term stromal reprogramming in human OA remains limited. Advances in single-cell omics, spatial transcriptomics, and systems biology approaches have revealed substantial heterogeneity among stromal and immune cell populations, providing new insights into fibrosis-associated cellular states and potential opportunities for biomarker-guided patient stratification. Nevertheless, whether these states represent stable biological entities, transitional disease stages, or secondary responses to advanced OA remains unresolved. This review focuses on the unresolved transition from adaptive tissue repair to persistent fibrotic remodeling and proposes a conceptual framework linking stromal reprogramming, inflammatory signaling, ECM remodeling, and mechanobiological feedback during OA progression. Throughout, we distinguish direct evidence from human OA and experimental OA models from mechanistic insights derived from rheumatoid arthritis and other fibrotic diseases. We further discuss emerging precision medicine strategies and future opportunities for biomarker-guided and mechanobiology-informed antifibrotic interventions. Although this Review adopts a whole-joint perspective, current mechanistic evidence remains predominantly synovium-centered, highlighting the need for further investigation of fibrotic remodeling across additional joint compartments.

title: Advances in the Diagnosis and Treatment of Pediatric Sepsis-Associated Acute Kidney Injury.
abstract: Sepsis remains a leading cause of mortality among critically ill children in pediatric intensive care units (PICUs) worldwide. A frequent and severe complication is sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SA-AKI), which increases morbidity and mortality, and contributes to the development of long-term chronic kidney disease. Recent advancements have expanded our understanding of pediatric SA-AKI, revealing a complex pathophysiology driven by systemic inflammation, microcirculatory dysfunction, reprogramming of energy metabolism, and programmed cell death. Besides, the emergence of novel biomarkers and risk stratification models has improved early detection and subphenotype classification. Despite these strides, traditional diagnostic criteria that rely on serum creatinine and urine output often delay diagnosis and exhibit limited ability to capture disease heterogeneity, thereby hindering the timely implementation of targeted, individualized therapies. This review synthesizes the latest evidence on pediatric SA-AKI, focusing on its pathophysiology, evolving diagnostic criteria, and the identification of clinical subtypes. Furthermore, it highlights precision medicine strategies, including novel biomarkers, advanced risk prediction models, and targeted interventions, to provide a theoretical foundation for future clinical research and personalized treatment.

title: Precision medicine for futile recanalization after mechanical thrombectomy in acute ischemic stroke: mechanisms, diagnostics, and tailored therapies.
abstract: Mechanical thrombectomy has substantially improved outcomes in appropriately selected patients with acute ischemic stroke, yet futile recanalization remains a major clinical challenge. Futile recanalization describes poor functional recovery despite technically successful macrovascular reperfusion, underscoring the incomplete relationship between angiographic reperfusion and tissue-level or microvascular perfusion. This narrative review summarizes current clinical, mechanistic, and translational evidence on the determinants of futile recanalization and evaluates emerging precision-medicine approaches to its prevention and management. Precision imaging has established a role in tissue-based patient selection, and recent randomized trials have expanded thrombectomy evidence to selected patients with large-core infarction. In contrast, current randomized evidence does not support routine endovascular treatment for unselected medium-vessel occlusion populations. We further examine bridging therapy versus direct mechanical thrombectomy, individualized periprocedural management, biomarkers, and decision support based on artificial intelligence. Clinical and imaging phenotypes may provide prognostic or mechanistic information, but no phenotype-based strategy has been prospectively validated to select bridging therapy or direct thrombectomy. Biomarkers currently remain primarily prognostic or exploratory. Artificial intelligence applications are largely focused on diagnostic and prognostic support. treatment-benefit prediction, by contrast, requires evidence of treatment-effect modification and prospective validation. Experimental studies of microvascular no-reflow and thrombo-inflammation provide biological rationale for targeted interventions but do not establish clinical efficacy. Future research should integrate multimodal imaging, biological profiling, and validated decision-support tools to move beyond angiographic success toward individualized strategies focused on tissue integrity and meaningful functional recovery.

title: Postpartum Stroke: The Importance of Early Recognition and Multidisciplinary Management.
abstract: Pregnancy and the postpartum period are associated with an increased risk of stroke. We report the case of a 41-year-old para 6 woman with pre-existing hypertension who underwent a category 2 caesarean section at term for fetal distress. A few hours postoperatively, a family member noticed that she was more drowsy than usual. Subsequent clinical assessment revealed left-sided limb weakness and facial drooping. Prompt clinical assessment and multidisciplinary escalation were initiated, followed by transfer to a specialist stroke unit within the potential therapeutic window for reperfusion therapy. Computed tomography (CT) scan of the head and CT angiography showed no obvious thrombus or large-vessel occlusion. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) confirmed an acute ischaemic infarction involving the right basal ganglia and subcortical right frontal lobe. Magnetic resonance venography (MRV) showed no evidence of cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVT). Bilateral carotid Doppler ultrasonography was normal. Intravenous thrombolysis was considered by the stroke team but was not recommended, while mechanical thrombectomy was not indicated because there was no large-vessel occlusion. This case highlights the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for acute neurological deterioration in the immediate postpartum period, particularly in women with underlying vascular risk factors. Early recognition, prompt multidisciplinary escalation, and timely specialist management are essential to optimise outcomes in postpartum patients with suspected stroke.

title: Long-term cost-effectiveness of CKD screening in middle-aged adults.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND HYPOTHESIS: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is common in Finland and frequently remains undiagnosed until advanced stages. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) slow CKD progression and reduce cardio-renal events when used in addition to Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System inhibitor (RAASi) treatment. We hypothesized that a one-time CKD screening program using measurements of estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR), followed by SGLT2i and RAASi treatment for identified CKD, would be cost-effective in Finland. METHODS: We developed a cohort-based Markov model to simulate lifetime CKD progression in a Finnish cohort aged 55 years under two strategies: (1) current practice (no screening) and (2) one-time screening with follow-up and SGLT2i and RAASi treatment for screen-positive CKD (eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m2 and/or UACR ≥3 mg/mmol; confirmed on a repeat sample after ≥ 3 months to establish chronicity). All CKD stages (G1-G5, dialysis, transplant, and death) were included in the model, and screening could detect CKD at any stage, although the incremental detection was concentrated in earlier, previously undiagnosed stages (G1-G3). Outcomes included discounted costs, quality-adjusted life years (QALYs), life years, and clinical outcomes (acute kidney function decline, heart-failure hospital days, dialysis and transplant patient-years, and deaths). Results are reported as means with 95% confidence intervals (CI). RESULTS: Screening increased discounted lifetime costs per person by €907 (95% CI €334-2 553) and QALYs by 0.14 (95% CI 0.07-0.31), yielding an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of €6 478/QALY. Screening increased life years by 0.30. Screening reduced acute kidney function decline (0.88 vs 0.90 events/person), heart-failure hospital days (6.47 vs 6.69 days/person), dialysis exposure (0.29 vs 0.32 patient-years/person) and transplant exposure (0.13 vs 0.14 patient-years/person). CONCLUSIONS: In Finns aged 55 years, one-time CKD screening with eGFR/UACR followed by SGLT2i and RAASi treatment improves long-term outcomes and is likely cost-effective.
journal: Nephrology, dialysis, transplantation : official publication of the European Dialysis and Transplant Association - European Renal Association

title: Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitor Use and Levels of Hemoglobin, Markers of Iron Metabolism, and Erythropoiesis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: In randomized clinical trials, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor use was associated with increased hemoglobin and hematocrit compared with placebo. However, the magnitude and importance of this association remain unclear. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the associations between SGLT2 inhibitor use and levels of hemoglobin, hematocrit, and markers of iron metabolism and erythropoiesis compared with placebo or active comparator. DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) were searched from inception to July 22, 2026. STUDY SELECTION: Randomized, double-masked clinical trials comparing SGLT2 inhibitor use with placebo or active comparators in patients with 1 or more of the following conditions: cardiovascular disease, diabetes, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease. DATA EXTRACTION AND SYNTHESIS: Three reviewers independently extracted data and results were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary outcomes were changes in hemoglobin and hematocrit. Secondary outcomes were changes in red blood cell concentration, erythropoietin (EPO), and iron measures (serum iron, ferritin, transferrin saturation, and hepcidin). RESULTS: A total of 85 randomized clinical trials were analyzed (median [IQR] duration, 24 [12-32] weeks), including 70 543 participants (mean [SD] age, 62.4 [9.4] years; 25 334 female [35.9%]). Mean (SD) baseline hemoglobin was 13.6 (1.5) g/dL; baseline hematocrit was 41.5% (4.9). Seventy-eight clinical trials (67 208 participants) compared SGLT2 inhibitors with placebo, and 7 clinical trials (3335 participants) used active comparators, most commonly sitagliptin (2 trials [1158 participants]). From baseline to follow-up, hemoglobin changed by 0.55 g/dL (95% CI, 0.49 to 0.61 g/dL; P < .001) in the SGLT2 inhibitor group, and -0.08 g/dL (95% CI, -0.13 to -0.03 g/dL; P = .003) in the control group (difference, 0.60 g/dL; 95% CI, 0.55 to 0.66 g/dL; P < .001). From baseline to follow-up, hematocrit changed by 2.17% (95% CI, 1.95% to 2.39%; P < .001) in the SGLT2 inhibitor group and -0.13% (95% CI, -0.28% to 0.01%; P = .07) in the control group (difference, 2.36%; 95% CI, 2.19% to 2.52%; P < .001). Of the 6 secondary outcomes, 4 showed significant associations with SGLT2 inhibitors, including increased EPO (2.35 mIU/mL in SGLT2 inhibitor group vs 0.04 mIU/mL in control group; difference, 2.11 mIU/mL [95% CI, 0.5-3.71 mIU/mL]; P = .01) and decreased transferrin saturation (-2.2% in SGLT2 inhibitor group vs -0.10% in control group; difference, -0.84% [95% CI, -1.21% to -0.47%]; P < .001). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In a meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials, compared with control, SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with small statistically significant increases in hemoglobin and hematocrit levels. The clinical significance of these findings is unclear.

title: Empagliflozin Therapy in Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease: A Feasibility Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: KEY POINTS: Empagliflozin 25 mg once daily for 12 months was safe and well tolerated in adults with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease at high risk of rapid progression. Those randomized to empagliflozin had a greater rate of increase in total kidney volume over 12 months compared with placebo. There was no difference between groups in the chronic rate of change in eGFR, nor in change in vascular stiffness, symptoms, and copeptin. BACKGROUND: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors reduce the risk of diabetic and nondiabetic kidney disease progression; however, their safety and efficacy in patients with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) are undetermined. METHODS: In this pilot and feasibility randomized controlled trial, we assigned 50 participants, 18-55 years of age, with ADPKD, at high risk of progression, not treated with tolvaptan, to receive empagliflozin (25 mg once daily) or placebo in a 1:1 ratio for 12 months. Primary outcomes were medication safety and tolerability. Secondary outcomes were (1) change in height-adjusted total kidney volume; (2) acute and chronic slope of eGFR; and (3) changes in aortic pulse wave velocity, plasma copeptin levels, urine kidney injury molecule-1, and patient-reported outcomes. RESULTS: Mean age was 42±7 years, and eGFR was 70±17 ml/min per 1.73 m2. Frequency of adverse events was similar between the 2 groups. Urinary tract infection occurred in 2 empagliflozin-treated patients versus none in placebo and AKI in 1 placebo-treated patient. In total, 96% of the participants in each group tolerated the full dose of the study drug. Among the secondary outcomes, rate of change in height-adjusted total kidney volume was significantly greater in empagliflozin-treated participants (10.5%/yr; 95% confidence interval, 8.2% to 12.7%) compared with placebo (5.1%/yr; 95% confidence interval, 3.0% to 7.3%; P = 0.001). There was a faster acute decline in eGFR at 1 month among the empagliflozin (-6.2 ml/min per 1.73 m2) versus placebo groups (0.1 ml/min per 1.73 m2; P = 0.01), but no differences in eGFR change from 1 to 12 months (empagliflozin group: -0.77±1.44 ml/min per 1.73 m2 per year versus placebo group: -2.87±1.96 ml/min per 1.73 m2 per year; P = 0.4). No between-group differences were observed in changes in aortic pulse wave velocity, copeptin, urine kidney injury molecule-1, and ADPKD Impact Score. CONCLUSIONS: Empagliflozin at 25 mg once daily was well tolerated by patients with ADPKD. Empagliflozin induced an expected acute decline in eGFR by 1 month, followed by stable eGFR. However, those treated with empagliflozin had a greater increase in kidney volume. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRY NAME AND REGISTRATION NUMBER: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05510115.
journal: Journal of the American Society of Nephrology : JASN

title: Precision medicine approaches in diabetic cardiomyopathy: from molecular mechanisms to personalized therapeutic strategies.
abstract: Diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM) is a distinct myocardial disease defined by the existence of abnormal myocardial structure and performance in diabetes mellitus patients without hypertension and coronary artery disease. DCM has been identified as a major cause of heart failure, hospitalisation and cardiovascular mortality with increasing global burden of diabetes. However, there is a large interindividual variation in disease susceptibility, disease progression and response to therapy, highlighting the limitations of conventional management strategies that are applied uniformly. Precision medicine provides a transformational approach through the integration of genomic, molecular, imaging, clinical and lifestyle data to allow for personalized risk assessment, early diagnosis, prognostication and treatment. This review presents the recent advances in the field of precision medicine for DCM with a focus on the molecular pathological mechanisms including metabolic disorders, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammation, fibrosis and microvascular injury. We discuss the relevance of genomics, pharmacogenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, lipidomics and epigenomics in the context of disease heterogeneity and identification of novel therapeutic targets. Emerging biomarkers including circulating microRNAs, non-coding RNAs, inflammatory mediators, fibrosis-related markers and extracellular vesicles are discussed for their potential in personal diagnosis and prognosis. We also consider the increasing role of advanced cardiac imaging, digital phenotyping, wearable technologies, artificial intelligence, and machine learning in enhancing early detection and clinical decision-making. In this review, the therapeutic advances, including sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, anti-fibrotic therapies, mitochondrial-targeted interventions, regenerative medicine, gene therapy, and RNA-based therapeutics, are discussed, with a focus on the precision medicine approach. Finally, we present current challenges in data integration, clinical validation, cost-effectiveness, and ethical issues, and highlight future directions in digital twins, multi-omics integration, and AI-driven personalized cardiology. The combination of these technologies has the potential to revolutionize the prevention and management of diabetic cardiomyopathy and improve cardiovascular outcomes in patients with diabetes.
journal: Journal of molecular and cellular cardiology

title: Practical Prevention of Heart Failure Across Stages A and B: A Scientific Statement From the Japanese Heart Failure Society.
abstract: Heart failure (HF) is a growing health problem in Japan, associated with substantial morbidity, mortality, recurrent hospitalization, impaired quality of life, and increasing healthcare costs. Early prevention before the onset of signs and symptoms has therefore become a major priority in cardiovascular medicine. This scientific statement from the Japanese Heart Failure Society provides practical prevention strategies for patients with HF Stage A and Stage B in Japan. Particular emphasis is placed on biomarker-guided screening using brain (B-type) natriuretic peptide (BNP) and N-terminal pro-BNP (NT-proBNP) to facilitate earlier detection of Stage B (pre-HF) and identification of patients at increased risk of progression to symptomatic HF. The statement summarizes evidence-based management of major cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic disorders associated with HF development, including hypertension, diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease, obesity, coronary artery disease, left ventricular dysfunction, valvular heart disease, and atrial fibrillation. It also addresses disease-specific approaches for optimizing blood pressure, glycemic control, renal protection, lipid management, and weight reduction. Preventive strategies include lifestyle modification, pharmacological therapy, serial reassessment of natriuretic peptide levels, and appropriate use of cardiovascular imaging and timely specialist referral. Because many patients at risk for HF are managed outside specialized cardiovascular centers, practical pathways for collaboration between cardiologists and non-cardiologist physicians are essential. The importance of timely referral, shared risk recognition, and multidisciplinary care is therefore emphasized. Implementation of clinically applicable prevention strategies may help reduce progression to symptomatic HF, facilitate earlier therapeutic intervention, and improve long-term cardiovascular outcomes.

title: 2026 THS guidelines for the management of hypertension in older adults: Developed by the task force on the management of hypertension of the Taiwan Hypertension Society (THS) and endorsed by the Taiwan Society of Cardiology (TSOC), Taiwan Association of Gerontology and Geriatrics (TAGG), and Taiwan Society of Family Medicine (TSFM).
abstract: The 2026 Taiwan Hypertension Society Guidelines for the Management of Hypertension in Older Adults provide an evidence-based framework tailored to the needs of an aging population. Recommendations were developed using PICO-formulated clinical questions, systematic evidence appraisal, and the GRADE approach, integrating evidence from randomized trials, observational studies, and expert consensus. A total of 63 actionable recommendations address diagnostic evaluation, blood pressure measurement and monitoring, lifestyle modification, blood pressure targets, and pharmacological therapy, with input from a multidisciplinary guideline panel and an external interdisciplinary expert committee. The guidelines emphasize age-related characteristics of hypertension, including arterial stiffness, salt sensitivity, frailty, orthostatic hypotension, cognitive vulnerability, atrial fibrillation, and multimorbidity. Standardized blood pressure measurement using validated oscillometric devices and regular out-of-office monitoring are strongly recommended. Blood pressure targets are specified according to age groups and common comorbid conditions. Non-pharmacological interventions, particularly dietary sodium reduction, potassium-enriched salt substitutes, healthy dietary patterns, and physical activity, are encouraged. Pharmacological treatment prioritizes individualized therapy and avoidance of overtreatment, especially in frail older adults. Endorsed by relevant national societies, these guidelines offer a practical approach to improving hypertension management and cardiovascular outcomes in older adults.
journal: Journal of the Formosan Medical Association = Taiwan yi zhi

title: Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 Inhibitor Use in Kidney Transplant Recipients With Post-Transplantation Diabetes Mellitus - A Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) have proved beneficial effects on cardiovascular risk and preservation of renal function in patients with diabetes mellitus and chronic kidney disease, in addition to their glucose-lowering effects. This study aims to investigate whether SGLT2i was associated with a more favorable metabolic profile in kidney transplant recipients with post-transplantation diabetes mellitus (PTDM). METHODS: In this observational study, patients receiving a kidney transplant between 2007 and 2021 in Norway were identified from the national transplant database. Patients who developed PTDM were identified through new- onset prescription of glucose- lowering treatment after kidney transplantation registered in Norwegian Prescription Database. PTDM patients were categorized whether glucose- lowering treatment included SGLT2i or not during the first 4 years after transplantation. Metabolic parameters at 5 years after transplantation reported to the Norwegian Renal Registry was compared in the 2 patient groups. RESULTS: This observational study included 232 kidney transplant recipients with PTDM. Metabolic parameters at 5 years post-transplantation were compared among the SGLT2i-group (n = 39) and the control group (n = 193); median BMI (27.5 vs. 26.5 kg/m2, p = .22), diastolic blood pressure (80 vs. 79 mm Hg, p = .40), systolic blood pressure (129 vs. 132 mm Hg, p = .42), proteinuria-parameters (u-ACR 4.5 vs. 3.5 mg/mmol, p = .33), (u-PCR 26 vs. 13 mg/mmol, p = .29), HbA1c (52 vs. 49 mmol/mol, p = .11) and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR, 61 vs. 56 mL/min/1.73m2, p = .20). CONCLUSION: Our study could not demonstrate improved metabolic parameters in PTDM patients treated with SGLT2-inhibitors at 5 years post transplantation.

title: Social and behavioral risk factors are associated with age-related differences in sustained attention: A cross-sectional GradCPT analysis of the All of Us dataset.
abstract: Background Attentional control declines with normal aging, yet the role of modifiable lifestyle factors in accelerating this decline remains incompletely characterised in large, diverse populations. We examined associations between four modifiable risk factors (smoking intensity, alcohol binge drinking, social satisfaction and blood pressure) and sustained attention performance in 13,866 adults drawn from the All of Us Research Program. Methods Cognitive performance was assessed using the Gradual-Onset Continuous Performance Task (GradCPT). A composite cognitive efficiency score was derived via principal component analysis of four GradCPT metrics: d' (perceptual sensitivity), response criterion, median reaction time and reaction time variability. Associations between cognitive efficiency and each risk factor were examined using multiple linear regression adjusted for age, sex and race/ethnicity. Effect sizes were expressed as age-equivalent years of cognitive aging (age-equivalent years = regression coefficient for the risk factor divided by the regression coefficient for age) to aid clinical interpretation. Results GradCPT performance declined progressively with age (p < 0.001). Social satisfaction emerged as the strongest lifestyle predictor: low social satisfaction was associated with approximately 5.8 additional age-equivalent years of cognitive aging relative to high social satisfaction. Smoking showed a dose-response pattern, with heavy smokers (> 20 cigarettes/day) exhibiting an approximately 5-year age-equivalent deficit versus never-smokers. Stage 2 hypertension showed a modest, non-significant negative association. Binge drinking showed limited significant associations, likely complicated by survivor and abstainer biases. Bootstrapped analyses of combined exposures showed that combinations of risk factors, particularly those involving low social satisfaction, produced larger cognitive deficits than expected under an additive model. Conclusions These findings support an interactive rather than a purely additive model of lifestyle-related cognitive vulnerability and highlight the GradCPT as a subclinical measure of attention-based cognitive risk in non-clinical populations. Keywords Cognitive aging, Sustained attention, GradCPT, Modifiable risk factors, Social isolation, Smoking, Hypertension, All of Us Research Program.
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences

title: Modifiable health-factor burden and stroke outcomes across three population databases: cross-sectional and longitudinal evidence from NHANES, CHARLS and HRS.
abstract: Background Modifiable vascular and lifestyle factors often cluster in middle-aged and older adults. We examined whether a simple harmonized health profile provides comparable stroke-related information across public population databases. Methods We used NHANES 2007-2018, CHARLS 2018 and HRS 2018 for cross-sectional analyses, and CHARLS 2011-2018 and HRS 2014-2022 for longitudinal validation. The cross-sectional outcome was self-reported physician-diagnosed stroke history. The main exposure was a six-factor burden score covering physical inactivity, hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidemia or high cholesterol, heart disease and current smoking. Database-specific weighted logistic regression estimates were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis. Longitudinal analyses used person-wave discrete-time survival models. Prediction analyses used CHARLS for model development and HRS for external validation. Results The adjusted cross-sectional models included 14,475 NHANES participants, 16,070 CHARLS participants and 8,175 HRS participants. Stroke history increased monotonically across burden categories in all three databases. Each additional unfavorable factor was associated with higher odds of stroke history in NHANES (odds ratio, 1.69; 95% confidence interval, 1.55-1.86), CHARLS (1.67; 1.58-1.77) and HRS (1.63; 1.52-1.76). The pooled odds ratio was 1.66 (95% confidence interval, 1.60-1.73), with little observed heterogeneity. In longitudinal models, each 1-point higher brain-health score was associated with lower hazards of incident self-reported stroke in CHARLS (hazard ratio, 0.740; 95% confidence interval, 0.712-0.769) and HRS (0.830; 0.789-0.874). The brain-health score showed moderate discrimination in CHARLS (area under the curve, 0.645) and HRS (0.648). Conclusions A higher burden of unfavorable modifiable health factors was consistently associated with stroke history across three public datasets. Longitudinal analyses linked a higher brain-health score to lower incident self-reported stroke hazards. These profiles may support low-cost population risk stratification, but they do not support causal or individual-level clinical interpretation.

title: Community Health Worker Coaching, Food Insecurity, and Physical Activity in the Healthy Food First Trial: A Causal Mediation and Longitudinal Analysis.
abstract: To evaluate whether change in food insecurity (ΔFI) mediated the effect of a community health worker (CHW) intervention on physical activity (PA) among food insecure (FI) hypertensive adults, we conducted a secondary analysis of the Healthy Food First randomized clinical trial of food insecure adults with hypertension recruited from 364 North Carolina clinical sites. Participants were randomized to CHW coaching or no coaching within a 2 × 2 × 2 factorial design. FI was measured at baseline and 12 months; total PA (MET-min/week) at 12 and 18 months. Mediation models estimated indirect (ACME), direct (ADE), and total effects (ATE) of CHW assignment on 12-month PA through ΔFI. Generalized estimating equations evaluated repeated PA by CHW assignment. CHW assignment was not associated with PA, and ΔFI did not mediate the relationship. Effects were small (ACME = 16.2; 95% CI -62.6, 121.8; ADE = -214.1; 95% CI -871.7, 484.5; ATE = -197.9; 95% CI -855.6, 500.8 MET-min/week). The proportion mediated was near zero (-8.2%; 95% CI -142%, 124%). GEE analyses similarly showed no association (B = 363.7 MET-min/week; SE = 302.8; P = 0.23). Modest improvements in FI alone may be insufficient to increase PA without additional PA supports. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05048836.

title: Effectiveness of Antenatal Interventions in Preventing Pregnancy-Related Complications: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Gestational diabetes mellitus, preeclampsia, and other adverse pregnancy outcomes continue to contribute substantially to maternal and neonatal morbidity worldwide. The increasing burden of metabolic and hypertensive complications during pregnancy has strengthened the need for effective, targeted preventive strategies. Although pharmacological, lifestyle, dietary, and healthcare system interventions have been widely studied, their effects vary according to the clinical outcome, population risk profile, intervention intensity, timing, adherence, and healthcare setting. Gaps therefore remain in identifying which approaches provide consistent benefit across different maternal and neonatal outcomes. This review synthesized evidence from randomized controlled trials evaluating interventions intended to improve pregnancy-related outcomes. A structured systematic search and study-selection process was undertaken, and eligible trials included pharmacological, lifestyle, dietary, behavioral, and healthcare system interventions. Data were synthesized qualitatively, and methodological quality and risk of bias were assessed using established criteria. The findings indicate that pharmacological interventions, including aspirin, calcium supplementation, and antenatal corticosteroids, showed benefits for selected outcomes in appropriately defined clinical populations and settings. Lifestyle and dietary interventions showed heterogeneous findings, with structured and intensive approaches demonstrating favorable outcomes in some populations, whereas lower-intensity interventions produced less consistent effects on major clinical endpoints. Behavioral and healthcare system interventions improved selected aspects of care delivery and patient-centered outcomes, although effects on major maternal and neonatal clinical outcomes were less consistent. Overall, the evidence supports targeted, context-specific use of preventive interventions rather than direct ranking of intervention categories, while recognizing substantial heterogeneity across populations, interventions, and outcomes.

title: [Acute management of minor ischemic stroke].
abstract: This review summarizes acute-phase treatment for minor ischemic stroke, focusing on the latest evidence for reperfusion therapy and acute antithrombotic treatment. In patients with large vessel occlusion, the benefit of mechanical thrombectomy is not established and the risk of hemorrhage exists; therefore, indications should be judged carefully for each patient. Intravenous thrombolysis provides limited benefit in non-disabling cases, and dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) can be an option. For minor non-cardioembolic stroke, early DAPT is recommended, and the possible role of adding argatroban is promising, especially for suspected branch atheromatous disease. For cardioembolic stroke, early initiation of a direct oral anticoagulant is desirable in mild cases without a large infarct.

title: Association of NMR metabolic signatures of healthy lifestyle with hypertension: a prospective cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Lifestyle factors play a critical role in the prevention and management of hypertension, while metabolomics provides valuable insights into the biological mechanisms underlying disease development. However, the relationships among lifestyle-related metabolic signatures, lifestyle behaviors, and hypertension risk remain incompletely understood. METHODS: This prospective cohort study used data from the UK Biobank. A composite healthy lifestyle score was calculated, and a lifestyle-related metabolic signature was developed using nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR)-based metabolomics and elastic net regression. Multivariable-adjusted Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate the associations between the healthy lifestyle score and the metabolic signature and incident hypertension. Causal mediation analysis based on a counterfactual framework (CMAverse package) was performed to quantify the mediating effect of the metabolic signature on the association between lifestyle and hypertension. Subgroup, interaction, and sensitivity analyses were also conducted. RESULTS: A total of 126,677 eligible participants (mean age, 54.92 ± 8.12 years; 46.47% male; 96.09% White) were included. During a median follow-up of 13.43 years, 18,720 participants developed hypertension. A healthy lifestyle-related metabolic signature comprising 76 metabolites was identified and showed a strong correlation with the healthy lifestyle score. Both a higher healthy lifestyle score (HR: 0.927; 95% CI: 0.913-0.940) and a higher metabolic signature level (HR: 0.675; 95% CI: 0.641-0.711) were independently associated with a significantly lower risk of incident hypertension, with significant inverse dose-response trends. These associations remained generally consistent across subgroups stratified by age, education, and income. Mediation analysis indicated that the metabolic signature explained 57.08% (95% CI: 31.89%-83.15%) of the protective association between a healthy lifestyle and hypertension risk. The primary findings remained robust across multiple sensitivity analyses. CONCLUSION: A healthy lifestyle is associated with a distinct metabolomic profile that substantially mediates its protective association with hypertension. These findings provide new insights into the metabolic mechanisms linking lifestyle behaviors to hypertension risk and highlight the importance of metabolic health in hypertension prevention.

title: Nurses' role in the management of patients living with hypertension in a district hospital in Ghana: a qualitative study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a chronic condition characterised by persistently high blood pressure, increasing the risk of cardiovascular disease, stroke, and kidney failure. Its management remains challenging in low- and middle-income countries due to limited awareness, lifestyle-related risk factors, and restricted access to healthcare. In Ghana, rapid urbanisation and dietary transitions toward processed foods have intensified this burden. This study aims to explore the role of nurses in managing patients with hypertension in Ghana. METHODS: This qualitative, exploratory and descriptive study was conducted between January and September 2025 with 15 participants at Ga West Municipal Hospital in the Greater Accra Region of Ghana. The participants were selected by a purposive sampling method. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews. Data analysis was done using thematic analysis following a systematic process involving data familiarisation, generation of initial codes, categorisation of codes into subthemes, development of overarching themes, and validation of findings to ensure credibility and consistency. RESULTS: Data analysis yielded three main themes and 10 subthemes. The themes included nurses' knowledge of hypertension management, nurses' experiences in managing hypertension and community and follow-up support. Under nurses' knowledge of hypertension management, the sub-themes identified were understanding of hypertension, initial assessment and blood pressure monitoring, pharmacological interventions, and counselling and discharge planning. For nurses' experiences in managing hypertension, the sub-themes comprised the use of clinical guidelines and protocols and challenges encountered in practice. Under community and follow-up support systems, the sub-themes included peer support groups, follow-up via telephone calls, community pharmacies and clinics, and telehealth services. Nurses play a critical role in hypertension management; however, their practice is hindered by limited knowledge, systemic constraints and weak community linkages. Enhancing nurses' competencies through regular professional training, access to updated evidence-based guidelines, adequate staffing and resources, and the integration of digital health tools can strengthen care delivery. CONCLUSIONS: These findings provide valuable insights into the roles and challenges of nurses in hypertension management within a municipal hospital setting. While the results may not be generalisable, they highlight areas for potential improvement, including strengthening professional training, improving access to evidence-based guidelines, and enhancing community follow-up systems. These considerations may inform future research, policy discussions, and practice improvements in similar resource-limited settings.

title: Anxiety Symptoms Assessed by the Goldberg Anxiety and Depression Scale, Lifestyle Habits, and Cardiometabolic Risk in Spanish Workers.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Anxiety has been increasingly recognized as a relevant contributor to cardiometabolic dysfunction through neuroendocrine, inflammatory, and behavioral mechanisms. However, evidence evaluating the relationship between anxiety symptoms, lifestyle habits, and cardiometabolic risk in large occupational populations remains limited. This study aimed to analyze the association between Goldberg Anxiety and Depression Scale (GADS) scores, lifestyle behaviors, and cardiometabolic risk factors in a large cohort of Spanish workers. METHODS: A cross-sectional observational study was conducted in 119,336 Spanish workers undergoing routine occupational health examinations between 2021 and 2023. Anxiety symptoms were assessed using the GADS. Lifestyle variables included smoking status, physical activity assessed with the International Physical Activity Questionnaire (IPAQ), and adherence to the Mediterranean diet evaluated through the Prevention with Mediterranean Diet (PREDIMED) questionnaire. Anthropometric measurements, blood pressure, lipid profile, fasting glucose, obesity, abdominal obesity, and metabolic syndrome were analyzed. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to estimate adjusted odds ratios (ORs) for cardiometabolic abnormalities according to anxiety status and lifestyle factors. RESULTS: Elevated GADS scores were significantly associated with worse cardiometabolic profiles in both sexes, including higher blood pressure, triglycerides, fasting glucose, body mass index, waist circumference, and lower high-density lipoprotein cholesterol concentrations. Workers with elevated anxiety presented markedly higher prevalences of hypertension, hypertriglyceridemia, impaired fasting glucose, abdominal obesity, and metabolic syndrome (all p < 0.001). After multivariable adjustment, elevated anxiety remained independently associated with hypertension (OR 6.48; 95% confidence interval (CI) 5.89-7.09), hypertriglyceridemia (OR 5.31; 95% CI 4.60-6.02), and impaired fasting glucose (OR 5.23; 95% CI 4.64-5.83). Physical inactivity and low adherence to the Mediterranean diet were associated with a less favorable cardiometabolic profile among participants with elevated anxiety scores. Elevated GADS scores were independently associated with all major cardiometabolic outcomes after multivariable adjustment, with the strongest associations observed for hypertension, hypertriglyceridemia, and impaired fasting glucose. CONCLUSIONS: Elevated GADS scores are strongly associated with adverse cardiometabolic profiles in Spanish workers, particularly when combined with unhealthy lifestyle behaviors. These findings support the integration of mental health assessment and lifestyle interventions into occupational cardiometabolic prevention strategies.

title: Circadian-Based Optimization of Pharmacotherapy in Chronic Diseases: Integrating Pharmacokinetics, Pharmacodynamics, and Disease Rhythm.
abstract: Circadian rhythms are endogenous, approximately 24-hour biological cycles that regulate physiological processes, including cardiovascular function, metabolism, immune activity, endocrine signaling, and sleep-wake patterns. These rhythms significantly influence disease pathophysiology and therapeutic responses, making biological time an important determinant of treatment outcomes. Several chronic diseases, including cardiovascular disorders, asthma, rheumatoid arthritis, metabolic syndrome, and psychiatric conditions, exhibit predictable circadian variations in symptom severity and disease activity. Simultaneously, circadian oscillations affect pharmacokinetic processes such as drug absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion, as well as pharmacodynamic mechanisms involving receptor sensitivity and cellular responsiveness. As a result, identical drug doses administered at different times may produce considerable differences in efficacy and toxicity. This review analyzes the role of circadian biology in optimizing pharmacotherapy through the integration of chronopharmacology and chronotherapy. It discusses the molecular basis of circadian regulation and its influence on physiological systems, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics. Disease-specific chronotherapeutic applications in cardiovascular, metabolic, endocrine, respiratory, rheumatologic, psychiatric, and oncologic disorders are highlighted. Clinical examples, including evening statin administration, timed bronchodilator use, and modified-release glucocorticoid therapy, highlight the practical benefits of circadian-based therapies. However, evidence remains variable across therapeutic areas, with some chronotherapeutic strategies, such as bedtime antihypertensive dosing, showing conflicting results in recent clinical trials. Further research is needed to define optimal timing recommendations and facilitate wider clinical adoption. Throughout, the strength of evidence is appraised to distinguish chronotherapeutic strategies with sufficient support for routine clinical use from those that remain experimental. The review also discusses emerging developments in chronopharmacokinetic modeling, advanced drug delivery systems, wearable monitoring devices, and precision chronomedicine. Despite promising evidence, broader implementation remains limited by variability in circadian patterns, lack of awareness, and insufficient standardized guidelines. Integrating circadian principles into pharmacotherapy and, ultimately, combining precision chronotherapy with lifestyle-based strategies may offer a promising direction for improving therapeutic precision, disease prevention, and patient outcomes.

title: Extracellular vesicles in colorectal cancer: M2 polarization, bidirectional regulation of CAFs, metastasis, and treatment.
abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs), as key mediators of intercellular communication, play a critical regulatory role in the pathogenesis and treatment of colorectal cancer (CRC). By carrying diverse bioactive molecules-including miRNAs, lncRNAs, circRNAs, and DNA-EVs influence multiple components of the tumor microenvironment (TME), such as promoting macrophage M2 polarization, reducing T and B Cell activity and proliferation, enabling evasion of natural killer (NK) cell surveillance, and regulating bidirectional fibroblast interactions in CRC. Furthermore, CRC-derived EVs can promote CRC metastasis by stimulating angiogenesis in endothelial cells, facilitating epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), and promoting the formation of pre-metastatic niches. Through an analysis of the role of EVs in the pathogenesis of CRC, numerous studies have found that EVs can augment the efficacy of immunotherapy. At the same time, both mesenchymal stem cell-derived EVs and engineered EVs (such as plant-derived and microorganism-derived EVs) can play significant roles in the treatment of CRC. However, most current research remains in the in vitro and in vivo trial stages. Due to difficulties in purification and engineering, as well as inherent heterogeneity, clinical translation remains challenging; consequently, no related products have yet been brought to market. Most clinical studies remain focused on diagnostic applications, while trials for therapeutic applications are still recruiting participants. Against this backdrop, we highlight the limitations and challenges in EVs research, with the aim of providing better research directions for the clinical translation of CRC treatments.
journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

title: Mechanical Thrombectomy 24 to 72 Hours after Large-Vessel Ischemic Stroke.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Endovascular thrombectomy is an established treatment for acute ischemic stroke. Whether the benefit extends to patients with salvageable brain tissue in the infarct who present more than 24 hours after symptom onset or the time when they were last known to be well is uncertain. METHODS: We conducted an open-label, randomized trial with blinded outcome assessment at comprehensive stroke centers in China. Patients with acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion of the anterior circulation and imaging-identified salvageable brain tissue at 24 to 72 hours were assigned to receive endovascular therapy plus standard medical care (intervention group) or standard medical care alone (control group). The primary outcome was functional status, defined by the score on the modified Rankin scale (range, 0 to 6, with higher scores indicating greater disability and a score of 6 indicating death) at 90 days, with results assessed as the distribution of scores in each group. Secondary outcomes included disability, neurologic impairment, and safety. RESULTS: A total of 336 patients were included in the intention-to-treat population, with 168 assigned to each group. The median time from symptom onset or from the point when the patient was last known to be well to randomization was 38.5 hours. Endovascular therapy resulted in a more favorable distribution of modified Rankin scale scores at 90 days than standard medical care alone (common odds ratio for a better functional outcome, 1.74; 95% confidence interval, 1.19 to 2.55). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 4.8% of the patients in the intervention group and in no patients in the control group, and the 90-day case fatality rate was 6.0% and 1.8%, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients who presented 24 to 72 hours after an acute ischemic stroke from large-vessel occlusion of the anterior circulation and had imaging-identified salvageable tissue, endovascular therapy resulted in better functional outcomes than standard care but led to a higher risk of intracranial hemorrhage and death. (Funded by the National Health Commission Capacity Building and Continuing Education Center and others; LATE-MT ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05326932.).
journal: The New England journal of medicine

title: Colorectal cancers with distinct metastatic potential trigger divergent early T cell responses.
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a leading cause of mortality, with most cases refractory to immunotherapy. Distinguishing tumor-induced from steady-state mucosal T cell responses represents a critical barrier to understanding CRC immunity. Using orthotopic transplantation of CRC organoids with and without metastatic potential, combined with T cell fate-mapping, we show that nonmetastatic tumors elicit early recruitment of CD8αβ+ and CD4+ T cells with cytotoxic and Th1-like programs, whereas pro-metastatic (pro-Met) tumors induce a naïve-like, hypoactivated state. Tumor-infiltrating CD4+ T cells underwent clonal expansion, including clones recognizing microbial and dietary antigens. T cells physically interacting with tumors, identified by universal LIPSTIC, were enriched for expanded and cytotoxic clones. Fate-mapped T cells from nonmetastatic tumors suppressed tumor growth in an IFN-γ-dependent manner. Mechanistically, pro-Met tumors downregulated MHCII, and Ciita targeting in nonmetastatic organoids reduced CD4+ clonal expansion and led to tumor progression. Together, these findings define divergent early T cell trajectories associated with CRC metastasis, indicating that ineffective local immune engagement precedes metastatic dissemination.

title: Real-World Pharmacological Patterns and Residual Cardiometabolic Risk in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes in Romania.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Contemporary management of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) has shifted from a glucose-centered approach toward integrated cardio-renal-metabolic protection. Although sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), and intensive lipid-lowering therapies have demonstrated substantial cardiovascular and renal benefits, implementation in routine outpatient care and the burden of persistent residual risk remain insufficiently characterized in Romania. OBJECTIVES: We aimed to evaluate routine-care pharmacological treatment patterns, identify residual cardio-renal-metabolic risk despite ongoing therapy, determine independent correlates of persistent adverse outcomes, and explore potential therapeutic gaps in adults with T2DM. METHODS: This cross-sectional observational study included 232 unique adults with T2DM attending a specialized outpatient diabetes clinic in Romania between 1 October 2024 and 19 February 2026. One eligible outpatient record per participant was analyzed; when multiple records were available, the earliest eligible record in the exported dataset was used as the index visit. No a priori sample-size calculation was performed. Pharmacological therapies, cardiovascular and renal phenotypes, metabolic biomarkers, and clinical outcomes were extracted from routinely collected electronic medical records. Residual risk was evaluated using glycemic, lipid, renal, obesity, and blood-pressure targets. Multivariable logistic regression analyses identified independent correlates of persistent cardio-metabolic abnormalities. An exploratory cumulative residual-risk count was constructed by summing seven clinically relevant uncontrolled risk factors. RESULTS: Biguanides were the most frequently prescribed glucose-lowering agents (53.0%), followed by SGLT2 inhibitors (44.8%), insulin (32.3% of the total cohort), GLP-1 receptor agonists (15.5%), and DPP-4 inhibitors (14.7%). Statins were prescribed to 48.7% of participants. SGLT2 inhibitor use did not differ significantly according to established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, heart failure, or chronic kidney disease phenotypes, whereas GLP-1 receptor agonists were prescribed more frequently in participants with obesity (22.0% vs. 7.6%, p = 0.003). Clinically important residual risk persisted across all treatment groups. Among SGLT2 inhibitor users, 57.3% had HbA1c ≥ 7%, while 27.9% remained albuminuric. Among insulin-treated participants, 84.0% had HbA1c ≥ 7%; reduced eGFR and albuminuria were also more frequent than among non-users. Despite statin therapy, 33.6% of treated participants continued to exhibit LDL cholesterol ≥ 100 mg/dL. In multivariable logistic regression, insulin therapy was associated with higher odds of HbA1c ≥ 7% (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 7.41, 95% confidence interval [CI] 3.50-15.65), while SGLT2 inhibitor therapy was associated with lower odds of albuminuria (aOR 0.54, 95% CI 0.30-0.95). Absence of statin-containing therapy was associated with higher odds of LDL cholesterol ≥ 100 mg/dL (aOR 6.01, 95% CI 3.38-10.66). Absence of statin-containing therapy was associated with higher odds of residual LDL cholesterol ≥ 100 mg/dL (aOR 4.21, 95% CI 2.34-7.58). Seventy-two percent of participants presented at least three persistent cardio-renal-metabolic abnormalities, while 24.2% exhibited five or more. More than half of participants with established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, heart failure, or chronic kidney disease were not receiving either an SGLT2 inhibitor or a GLP-1 receptor agonist. CONCLUSIONS: Significant residual cardio-renal-metabolic risk persists in adults with T2DM despite use of contemporary pharmacological therapies. Disease severity markers and treatment exposure were associated with persistent adverse outcomes, but the cross-sectional design does not establish causality. The study identified potentially modifiable therapeutic gaps among patients with established cardiovascular and renal disease. Comprehensive and repeatedly reassessed cardio-renal-metabolic management, integrating pharmacological optimization with individualized risk stratification, may improve implementation of guideline-directed therapy and reduce long-term complications in routine clinical practice.

title: Head-to-Head Comparison of FAP Antibody Clones for Tissue Expression Analysis.
abstract: Background: Fibroblast activation protein (FAP) is a promising target for cancer diagnosis and therapy, but the specificity and sensitivity of anti-FAP antibodies used for immunohistochemistry (IHC) vary considerably. A head-to-head comparison of commercially available clones is needed to guide antibody selection, thereby standardizing FAP IHC protocols and ensuring reliable patient stratification for FAP-directed therapies. Methods: We evaluated three anti-FAP clones-FAP/4851 (mouse monoclonal), JA56-11 (recombinant rabbit), and EPR20021 (rabbit monoclonal)-in formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissues from 137 patients with breast (n = 29), colorectal (n = 27), lung (n = 42), and head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (n = 39). FAP expression was assessed by manual semiquantitative scoring (H-score and percentage of positive cells) and, for a validation subset, by QuPath-based digital image analysis. The study included negative (normal liver/skeletal muscle) and positive (WI-38 cell block) controls. Results: Clones JA56-11 and EPR20021 showed specific stromal staining, whereas FAP/4851 exhibited intense non-specific reactivity and was excluded from quantitative analysis. EPR20021 demonstrated significantly higher H-scores than JA56-11 in all four cancer types (Wilcoxon test, p ≤ 0.0179), resulting in a higher overall detection rate under the tested conditions. Aberrant tumor cell expression was detected almost exclusively by EPR20021 in head and neck (59% of cases) and colorectal (59%) cancers. QuPath validation showed good correlation with manual scoring for EPR20021 in the tumor compartment of lung cancer (Spearman's ρ = 0.701, p = 0.024) with small bias (Bland-Altman). Conclusions: Under the conditions tested, EPR20021 (Abcam) demonstrated higher staining intensity and detection rates than JA56-11 across several tumor types. Clone FAP/4851 showed nonspecific staining under the conditions used in this study and was therefore not suitable for quantitative analysis in the present experimental setting. Consequently, careful selection of well-validated antibody clones is essential for ensuring reproducible and reliable FAP immunohistochemical analysis.

title: Olink Platform-Based Identification of Peripheral Blood Biomarkers for irAEs in Advanced NSCLC.
abstract: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Immunotherapy has transformed the treatment landscape for advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, immune-related adverse events (irAEs) represent a major clinical challenge during immunotherapy. These events can affect any organ system, and severe irAEs may necessitate treatment interruption or lead to life-threatening outcomes. We prospectively enrolled 84 advanced NSCLC patients treated with immunotherapy (June 2022-June 2024, followed until February 2025), including 57 who developed grade 1-4 irAEs and 27 who did not. Peripheral blood was collected from 39 patients at baseline for Olink platform-based proteomic screening, complemented by flow cytometric analysis of lymphocyte subsets. Olink profiling revealed IL13 and TRAIL as the most significantly differentially expressed proteins between irAEs and non-irAE groups. These proteins were enriched in biological processes such as negative regulation of lung ciliated cell differentiation and positive regulation of lung goblet cell differentiation, as well as in asthma and inflammatory bowel disease pathways. Moreover, dynamic changes in total T lymphocytes, T helper cells, NK cells, and the CD4/CD8 ratio were strongly associated with irAE occurrence. These markers, readily measurable in peripheral blood, offer potential for early risk stratification and real-time monitoring.

title: Triple Genetic Alterations (EGFR Mutation, ALK Fusion, and MET Polysomy) in Gynecological Metastasis of Lung Adenocarcinoma Patient with Acquired Resistance to Furmonertinib: A Case Report.
abstract: For advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations, targeted therapy is the standard first-line treatment, but acquired resistance and disease progression are inevitable. Identification of resistance mechanisms is crucial for guiding subsequent anti-tumor therapy. We report a 57-year-old female patient with advanced lung adenocarcinoma harboring an EGFR exon 21 L858R mutation. The patient experienced disease progression with rare gynecological metastasis after 16 months of first-line furmonertinib therapy. Next-generation sequencing (NGS) of the uterine metastatic lesion identified concurrence of EGFR mutation and ALK fusion, while fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) confirmed MET polysomy. The patient exhibited intolerance to the combination therapy of glumetinib plus furmonertinib.
