Subsequently, the patient received a combination of furmonertinib and the ALK-TKI ensartinib, which was assessed as a partial response (PR) at the first restaging evaluation (1 month after treatment initiation), with favorable safety and tolerability. Secondary ALK fusion may represent a rare but clinically meaningful resistance mechanism in EGFR-mutant NSCLC. Furthermore, while gynecological metastasis from lung cancer is uncommon, clinicians should be alert to this possibility in patients presenting with relevant symptoms, with pelvic examination conducted as needed.

title: From Dysbiosis to Symbiosis: Using the Gut Microbiome to Improve Cancer Outcomes.
abstract: The gut microbiome has emerged as an important regulator of cancer biology, influencing carcinogenesis, treatment response, and therapy-related toxicity. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on the mechanistic roles of the gut microbiota in gastrointestinal (GI) cancers and evaluates emerging microbiome-based strategies for improving cancer outcomes. Dysbiosis-characterized by altered microbial diversity, depletion of beneficial functions, and enrichment of disease-associated taxa-may contribute to tumorigenesis through interconnected mechanisms involving chronic inflammation, genotoxicity, metabolic dysregulation, epigenetic alterations, and immune evasion. Key cancer-associated bacteria, including Fusobacterium nucleatum, enterotoxigenic Bacteroides fragilis (ETBF), pks+Escherichia coli, and Helicobacter pylori, illustrate the mechanistic diversity of microbiota-associated carcinogenesis. Beyond cancer initiation, the gut microbiome can influence the efficacy and toxicity of anticancer therapies. In immunotherapy, specific microbial taxa and metabolites modulate antitumor immunity and immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) responses, while antibiotic-associated dysbiosis has been linked to poorer outcomes. In chemotherapy, microbial metabolism and microbiota-derived metabolites can alter drug efficacy and toxicity, including modulation of 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) activity. Microbiome-based biomarkers show promise for cancer detection and treatment prediction, with fecal microbial signatures, including F. nucleatum, potentially improving colorectal cancer (CRC) screening when incorporated into multimarker strategies. Therapeutic approaches aimed at restoring microbial symbiosis include fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), which has shown preliminary potential to restore ICI responsiveness in treatment-refractory melanoma, and probiotic interventions, although clinical evidence remains limited. Emerging engineered microbial therapeutics, including tumor-targeting bacteria designed to deliver localized immunostimulatory payloads, are advancing toward clinical translation. Despite substantial progress, important challenges remain, including methodological heterogeneity, lack of standardized protocols, confounding factors, and unresolved safety concerns. Personalized strategies integrating microbial features with host characteristics and treatment context may ultimately enable more effective microbiome-based approaches to improve cancer outcomes.

title: Clinical Course of Four Patients with Mucormycosis Managed Predominantly with Ayurveda-Based Interventions: A Case Series.
abstract: Mucormycosis is a rapidly progressive angioinvasive fungal infection caused by Mucorales, predominantly affecting immunocompromised individuals and associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Despite advances in standard care involving surgical debridement and systemic antifungal therapy, outcomes may remain suboptimal because of recurrence, treatment-related toxicity, including nephrotoxicity associated with amphotericin B, and substantial economic burden. These challenges justify continued investigation of adjunctive therapies and other approaches that may potentially improve outcomes or reduce treatment burden, while established antifungal therapy and surgical management remain the cornerstone of care. Ayurveda, a traditional system of medicine in India, employs comprehensive therapeutic strategies that may include oral formulations, local interventions, dietary regulation, and lifestyle modifications. Ayurveda has been utilised by patients with mucormycosis; however, its evidence base remains limited and largely restricted to adjunctive or isolated case reports. This paper presents a descriptive case series of four patients diagnosed with mucormycosis who were managed predominantly with Ayurveda-based interventions. Three patients opted to receive stand-alone Ayurveda-based treatment after declining recommended standard biomedical treatment. All patients had complex comorbidities, including diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and renal impairment. Serial follow-up imaging documented radiological changes interpreted by the reporting radiologists as improvement in three patients, with no documented recurrence during the available follow-up periods. One patient with suboptimal treatment adherence showed persistent radiological abnormalities at the three-month assessment, although survival was maintained for approximately one year following diagnosis. No treatment-related adverse events were documented in the available follow-up records; one patient with pre-existing renal impairment showed an increase in serum creatinine from 1.48 to 3.3 mg/dL during follow-up. These observations are descriptive and derive from an uncontrolled case series with non-standardised follow-up and outcome assessment. They do not establish treatment effectiveness, safety, non-inferiority, or suitability for clinical application and should not be interpreted as evidence supporting replacement of current standard-of-care management. Rather, these observations advance ongoing hypothesis generation and provide conceptual and methodological insights for the development of future clinical research protocols evaluating predominantly Ayurveda-based interventions for mucormycosis care.

title: Heart and Brain: Linking Obesity-Related Inflammation, Cardiovascular Disease and Cognitive Function.
abstract: The heart and brain are interconnected, and risk factors that impact the heart can negatively affect the brain and cognition. Among the underlying features that foster both poor brain health and poor heart health are obesity, diabetes, physical inactivity and low sleep quality. Obesity and type 2 diabetes are associated with an increased likelihood of cognitive impairment and dementia. Further, obesity is a causal factor in obstructive sleep apnea, leading to intermittent hypoxemia, neuroinflammation and cognitive dysfunction. Cerebrovascular disease with reduced cerebral blood flow brings on stroke and elevates dementia risk. Like cardiovascular disease, cerebrovascular disease is also accelerated in the setting of obesity, likely through the same mechanisms involving endothelial dysfunction and damage to macrovasculature and microvasculature from hypertension, dyslipidemia and inflammation. Obesity is considered a risk factor for recurrent stroke. The protracted low-grade chronic elevation of inflammatory markers found with excess adiposity leads to oxidative stress and promotes both endothelial dysfunction and a pro-thrombotic state. Greater loss of brain volume has been documented in middle-aged and older adults with obesity compared with young adults with obesity. Obesity poses a threat to the cardiovascular and cerebrovascular health and well-being of individuals worldwide. Unfortunately, treatments directed at reducing caloric intake are of limited effectiveness. This review will focus on the latest research into the link between excess adipose tissue and cardiac and brain health, with attention to dietary and lifestyle interventions that may be protective of the integrity and function of the vasculature and brain.
journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease

title: Thrombophilic Variants and Clinical Outcomes in Young Ischaemic Stroke Patients Undergoing Mechanical Thrombectomy: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to characterise thrombophilic variants in young patients (≤50 years) undergoing mechanical thrombectomy (MT) for acute ischaemic stroke and to determine their clinical relevance. In addition, outcomes in young patients were compared with those in older patients to provide clinical context for age-related differences in presentation and recovery. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients with large-vessel occlusion stroke who achieved successful recanalisation (TICI ≥ 2b) after MT at a comprehensive stroke centre. Patients were stratified into young (≤50 years) and non-young (>50 years) groups. Clinical variables, thrombophilia markers, and functional outcomes were analysed. RESULTS: Among 679 included patients, 76 (11.2%) were classified as young (mean age 39.2 ± 7.4 vs. 72.0 ± 11.4 years in older patients). Young patients had lower baseline NIHSS scores (14.6 ± 7.9 vs. 17.7 ± 4.7; mean difference -3.1 points) and markedly lower 1-month NIHSS scores (2.4 ± 2.3 vs. 9.5 ± 5.6; mean difference -7.1 points; both p < 0.001). Three-month mortality was 11.8% in young patients and 17.6% in older patients; however, this difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.2565). The MTHFR C677T variant was associated with lower post-procedural NIHSS scores (p = 0.021), while the distribution of hereditary thrombophilia markers did not differ significantly across vascular territories. Elevated homocysteine levels were associated with poorer 3-month outcomes (p = 0.0156). CONCLUSIONS: Young stroke patients undergoing MT demonstrated markedly better neurological and functional outcomes than older patients; however, three-month mortality did not differ significantly between the groups. Although several inherited thrombophilic variants were identified in the young cohort, most showed no consistent association with clinical outcomes.
journal: Journal of cardiovascular development and disease

title: Rethinking Evidence Generation for Vaccine Safety in Pregnancy: Beyond Randomized Trials Across the Immunization Lifecycle.
abstract: Maternal immunization protects pregnant individuals and infants. However, evidence on vaccine safety during pregnancy remains variable across vaccine products and maternal, fetal, neonatal, and infant outcomes. Debate has often focused on whether pregnant individuals should be included in randomized controlled trials, overlooking the complementary roles of other study designs. Trials are indispensable for assessing immunogenicity, reactogenicity, efficacy, and common short-term outcomes, but are rarely powered to exclude modest increases in uncommon obstetric, congenital, neonatal, or delayed childhood outcomes. This Perspective examines a coordinated approach to maternal vaccine safety assessment before and after authorization, including randomized trials, spontaneous reporting, pregnancy vaccine exposure registries, linked maternal-infant databases, near-real-time surveillance, and international research networks. Lessons from influenza, pertussis, COVID-19, and maternal respiratory syncytial virus vaccination show why authorization should initiate sustained pregnancy-specific safety monitoring. We discuss the limitations of real-world evidence, including confounding, healthy-vaccinee effects, gestational timing, conditioning on live birth, outcome misclassification, and background rate estimation, as well as methods to strengthen causal interpretation. Regulators and vaccine developers should prespecify pregnancy-specific post-authorization studies, harmonize outcome definitions and exposure windows, and distinguish the absence of a detected signal from the exclusion of a clinically relevant risk. Coordinated surveillance is essential to provide timely, precise, and clinically meaningful evidence for pregnant individuals and their children.

title: Five-Year Effectiveness and Adherence Outcomes of SARS-CoV-2 Vaccination in Immunocompromised Patients Since the Launch of the Vaccination Campaign.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Immunocompromised patients are at heightened risk for severe COVID-19 and its complications. While vaccination is critical for this population, long-term adherence and the durability of vaccine-induced immunity remain significant public health concerns. This study aimed to evaluate the longitudinal serological response associated with hybrid immunity and to assess temporal trends in SARS-CoV-2 vaccination adherence among immunocompromised patients. METHODS: A prospective observational cohort study was conducted on 170 immunocompromised patients followed longitudinally for five years at an Italian Teaching Hospital. Humoral response was assessed by quantifying IgG antibodies against the spike receptor-binding domain (RBD) of SARS-CoV-2 (anti-RBD IgG titers) at multiple time points, from baseline through the first booster dose. Vaccination uptake and reasons for vaccine refusal were monitored throughout the study period. RESULTS: Of the 170 enrolled patients, 159 (94.1%) completed the primary three-dose schedule. Following the initial two-dose regimen, 88% of patients were classified as non- or low-responders (mean anti-RBD IgG: 84.9 BAU/mL). Administration of an additional third dose and subsequent booster markedly enhanced immunogenicity, increasing the mean anti-RBD IgG titer to 3447.5 BAU/mL, with 87.7% of patients classified as high responders post-booster. Despite favorable clinical outcomes, with no COVID-19-related deaths recorded, vaccination uptake demonstrated a significant and continuous decline, dropping from 97% during the pandemic phase to 8.3% during the 2025-2026 campaign. Primary reasons for refusal included doubts regarding vaccine efficacy (55%) and weak indications or contraindications provided by healthcare professionals (22%). CONCLUSIONS: Repeated SARS-CoV-2 vaccine doses significantly improve humoral immunity and clinical outcomes in immunocompromised individuals. However, the progressive decline in long-term vaccine uptake, driven largely by efficacy concerns and insufficient provider recommendations, poses a major public health challenge.

title: Navigating the Transition to RNA-Based Influenza Vaccines: A State-of-the-Art Review.
abstract: Seasonal influenza and the ongoing emergence of zoonotic influenza viruses, including highly pathogenic avian influenza A (H5N1), remain substantial global public health threats, underscoring the need for rapidly adaptable vaccine platforms. This state-of-the-art review critically evaluates the clinical development of RNA-based influenza vaccines through a comprehensive assessment of ClinicalTrials.gov records and peer-reviewed literature. Candidates were examined across four domains: seasonal influenza vaccines, pre-pandemic influenza vaccines, combination respiratory vaccines, and self-amplifying RNA (saRNA) platforms. Clinical evidence indicates that mRNA influenza vaccines consistently elicit robust humoral immune responses and, in late-stage trials, have demonstrated improved relative efficacy against influenza A compared with conventional influenza vaccines. Reactogenicity is generally more frequent with mRNA vaccines, particularly with respect to transient mild-to-moderate systemic adverse events. However, serious adverse events remain uncommon and broadly comparable to those observed with licensed comparator vaccines. Pre-pandemic and multicomponent mRNA vaccine candidates similarly demonstrate strong immunogenicity, supporting the potential of RNA platforms for both seasonal vaccination and pandemic preparedness. Clinical development of saRNA influenza vaccines has progressed through early-phase trials, although publicly available clinical data remain limited. Regulatory milestones in 2026, including U.S. approval of mRNA-1010 (mFlusiva), the first approved mRNA-based seasonal influenza vaccine, and European Union authorization of mRNA-1083 (mCOMBRIAX), an mRNA-based influenza-COVID-19 combination vaccine, represent important steps in the clinical transition and implementation of RNA-based influenza vaccination.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Live Attenuated COVID-19 Vaccine Candidate Based on Omicron-like Temperature-Sensitive Mutant in Preclinical Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Although the COVID-19 pandemic has ended, emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants remain a future threat. This study evaluated the safety and efficacy of an intranasal live attenuated vaccine (LAV) prototype based on a temperature-sensitive (ts) Omicron-like SARS-CoV-2 mutant in a Syrian hamster COVID-19 model. Methods: SARS-CoV-2 Dubrovka (Wuhan-like), Otradnoe (BA.1.1) and FEB2 (BA.5.2) strains and the ts F-F3 mutant derived from FEB2 were characterized by electron microscopy, nanopore sequencing, cytopathic effect titration, and RT-PCR. In vitro studies used Vero CCL-81 cells; in vivo transmissibility and efficacy studies were assessed in female Syrian hamsters. Serum antibody titers were measured by ELISA and neutralization assays. Immunization efficacy was assessed by weight change; viral loads in the lungs, nasal passages, and brain; and histological examination of the lungs at day 4 post-challenge. Safety criteria included evaluation of pathogenicity and transmissibility in hamsters and ts phenotype stability during prolonged in vitro cultivation. Results: The F-F3 strain displayed a stable ts phenotype in vitro, did not infect hamster lungs or brain, and showed no transmission from immunized to naïve co-housed animals. A single intranasal immunization by F-F3 induced seroconversion, reduced pneumonia severity by 76.2% and 79.5% in two independent experiments (p < 0.01), protected the lungs against productive infection while reducing viral load in the nasal passages, and resulted in no detectable viral transmission after homologous BA.5.2 challenge. Following heterologous Wuhan-like challenge, immunization prevented weight loss and significantly reduced viral loads in the lungs, nasal passages, and brain; however, protection against pneumonia was only modest (18.6%; p < 0.05). Conclusions: Preclinical evaluation of the F-F3-based LAV prototype demonstrated a favorable balance between safety and efficacy. These characteristics support its further consideration as a candidate strain for COVID-19 LAV development.

title: Preprocedural CT Radiomic Features of the Basal Ganglia Are Associated with Post-Thrombectomy Hyperdense Transformation: A LASSO-Based Logistic Regression Analysis.
abstract: Purpose: To investigate whether radiomic characteristics of visually unremarkable basal ganglia on preprocedural non-contrast computed tomography (CT) are associated with subsequent post-thrombectomy hyperdense transformation (HT) in patients with acute ischemic stroke. Materials and Methods: This retrospective single-center study included a derivation cohort of 84 patients with preserved Alberta Stroke Programme Early CT Scores (ASPECTS ≥ 8), no visually appreciable basal ganglia abnormality, anterior circulation large-vessel occlusion, and complete reperfusion after mechanical thrombectomy between January 2022 and July 2023. An independent temporal validation cohort comprised 31 consecutive eligible patients treated between August and November 2023. The ipsilateral basal ganglia were manually segmented on preprocedural non-contrast CT, and radiomic features were extracted using LIFEx. Candidate features underwent interobserver reproducibility assessment and correlation filtering before least absolute shrinkage and selection operator logistic regression with 10-fold cross-validation. The final model was applied without modification to the temporal validation cohort. Nested cross-validation and learning-curve analysis were additionally performed to assess model-development optimism and stability. Results: The final model retained two texture features, Gray-Level Run Length Matrix Short Runs Emphasis and Gray-Level Size Zone Matrix Grey Level Variance. In the derivation cohort, the model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.760 (95% CI, 0.652-0.855), with 48.8% sensitivity, 95.3% specificity, and 72.6% accuracy. When applied without modification to the independent temporal validation cohort, the AUC was 0.677 (95% CI, 0.475-0.858), with 33.3% sensitivity, 93.8% specificity, and 64.5% accuracy. Nested cross-validation yielded a mean AUC of 0.673 ± 0.037, with variability in feature selection across resampling iterations. Learning-curve analysis showed an early plateau, with little improvement in cross-validated discrimination as the training sample increased within the evaluated range. Conclusions: Radiomic analysis of visually unremarkable basal ganglia on preprocedural non-contrast CT identified an exploratory two-feature imaging signature associated with subsequent post-thrombectomy HT. The model retained modest discriminatory ability in temporal validation, although internal resampling demonstrated model-development optimism and limited feature-selection stability. These findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and warrant further evaluation using larger datasets, alternative modeling approaches, and independent multicenter validation.

title: Skeletal Muscle in Vulnerable Populations Receiving Cardiorenal-Metabolic Therapies: SGLT2 Inhibitors, Incretin-Based Therapies, and the Challenge of Precision Medicine.
abstract: The introduction of sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors and incretin-based therapies has transformed the management of obesity, type 2 diabetes, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease by delivering substantial metabolic, cardiovascular, and renal benefits. However, their effects on skeletal muscle have become a growing area of interest. While SGLT2 inhibitors induce modest weight loss, their catabolic metabolic effects have prompted questions regarding skeletal muscle preservation, particularly in individuals with limited physiological reserve. Conversely, the profound weight loss achieved with incretin-based therapies has raised concerns about accompanying reductions in lean tissue and their potential functional consequences. In this narrative review, we critically evaluate the available evidence regarding the effects of these therapeutic classes on skeletal muscle, integrating findings from randomized controlled trials, observational studies, systematic reviews, and mechanistic investigations. We compare their distinct biological mechanisms; summarize clinical evidence on changes in muscle quantity, quality, strength, and physical performance; and discuss their implications for older adults; individuals with frailty, sarcopenia, or sarcopenic obesity; and patients with heart failure or chronic kidney disease. Overall, current evidence indicates that both SGLT2 inhibitors and incretin-based therapies preferentially reduce adipose tissue, whereas the accompanying reductions in lean tissue are generally proportional to the magnitude of weight loss. Importantly, reductions in lean tissue should not be equated with treatment-induced sarcopenia, as current evidence does not consistently demonstrate clinically meaningful impairment in muscle strength or physical performance. Nevertheless, the populations most susceptible to skeletal muscle dysfunction remain underrepresented in clinical trials. We discuss a phenotype-based approach that integrates skeletal muscle health into therapeutic decision-making and outline practical strategies-including resistance exercise, adequate protein intake, and individualized monitoring-to preserve muscle function during treatment. Future research should prioritize standardized functional outcomes and dedicated studies in vulnerable populations to enable precision cardiorenal-metabolic medicine.

title: Nanozyme-Amplified Closed Bipolar Electrochemical Colorimetric Platform for Multiplexed Visual Detection of Sepsis Biomarkers.
abstract: Early diagnosis of sepsis urgently requires the development of novel electrochemical sensing platforms for rapid, sensitive, and multiplexed measurement of inflammatory biomarkers at the point of care. Herein, we report a closed bipolar electrochemical (cBPE) colorimetric platform that couples nanozyme-catalyzed redox cycling at the sensing pole with Prussian blue (PB) electrodeposition at the signal pole. Bimetallic Au@Pt nanozymes (Au core, porous Pt shell) catalyze the reduction of [Fe(CN)6]3- by ammonia borane (NH3·BH3) with a specific activity of 310 U mg-1, which is 12-fold higher than that of the Au core, and an apparent catalytic efficiency (kcat/Km) of 2.7 ×107 M-1 s-1, determined under the first-order kinetic regime. Sepsis biomarkers captured on immunomagnetic beads and labeled with detection antibody-conjugated Au@Pt nanozymes were magnetically enriched at the cBPE anode, where the nanozyme-generated [Fe(CN)6]4- was re-oxidized to [Fe(CN)6]3-, sustaining a redox cycle that amplifies the Faradaic current. Charge conservation across the cBPE converts this current into an equivalent cathodic flux in a physically separated signal chamber, where Fe3+ reduction drives deposition of a blue PB film whose grayscale intensity increases monotonically with target concentration and is read by the naked eye. The spatially addressable cBPE array allows interleukin-6 (IL-6), C-reactive protein (CRP), and serum amyloid A (SAA) to be assayed in parallel, with the limits of detection of 0.83, 2.69, and 1.82 ng mL-1, respectively. In clinical serum samples from healthy controls (n = 11) and sepsis patients (n = 11), all three biomarkers were significantly elevated in the sepsis patients, with an area under the ROC curve of 0.82-1.00, demonstrating discriminative performance in real samples. The proposed cBPE-based electrochemical colorimetric platform integrates catalytic signal amplification, wireless multiplexing, and visual readout, offering a practical route toward point-of-care detection of sepsis-associated biomarkers.

title: Dual VEGF and PD-(L)1 Blockade: Facts and Hopes.
abstract: VEGF-A/VEGF-R axis is well recognized for its role in tumor angiogenesis as well as tumor-induced immunosuppressive mechanisms. Targeting this pathway can help to switch tumor microenvironment toward a more immune-permissive state. Inhibition of VEGF-A/VEGFR has emerged as a strategy to enhance the efficacy of immunotherapy in some cancers leading to the approval of anti-VEGF-A/anti-PD(L)1 combinations in advanced renal cell cancer, hepatocellular carcinoma, non-small cell lung cancer, and endometrial cancer. However, in other tumor types, and particularly in colorectal cancer or glioblastoma, results remain limited. In this review, we discuss the biological rationale underlying anti-VEGF-A/PD-(L)1 combinations, summarize the clinical evidence supporting their use across tumor types, discuss the disappointing results in colorectal cancer and glioblastoma, and highlight emerging strategies to improve their therapeutic efficacy.
journal: Clinical cancer research : an official journal of the American Association for Cancer Research

title: Using rare coding variants in SLC5A2 to explore the impact of SGLT2 inhibitors on cardiorenal outcomes.
abstract: AIMS: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors are agents originally developed as glucose-lowering drugs but now widely used to improve cardiorenal outcomes, including in patients with heart failure and chronic kidney disease regardless of diabetes status. However, their exact mode of action remains unclear. Here, we investigated the association of loss-of-function (LoF) and other rare coding variants in the SLC5A2 gene, as a genetic model of altered SGLT2 function, with 13 cardiometabolic and renal traits and clinical outcomes. METHODS AND RESULTS: A total of 442 570 European ancestry participants from the UK Biobank with exome sequence and phenotype data were included. We applied SAIGE-GENE+ for gene-based and single-variant association tests in the full study population and in individuals with heart failure, renal failure, and type 2 diabetes (T2D). A total of 52 LoF variants in SLC5A2 were identified. Rare variants in SLC5A2 were associated with decreased uric acid (PCauchy = 4.98 × 10-13) and with increased haematocrit (PCauchy = 1.67 × 10-5), haemoglobin (PCauchy = 1.60 × 10-5), and estimated glomerular filtration rate (PCauchy = 9.88 × 10-4). One frameshift variant (rs267607067) was significantly associated with increased haemoglobin (β = 0.33 [95% CI 0.15-0.51]; P-value = 2.40 × 10-4) and another (rs768095044) with decreased uric acid (β = -0.31 [95% CI -0.49 to -0.13]; P-value = 4.22 × 10-4). In patients with T2D, the rare variants within SLC5A2 were also associated with a lower probability of having heart failure (PCauchy = 4.00 × 10-4). CONCLUSION: Rare genetic variants in SLC5A2 were associated with increased haemoglobin and decreased uric acid. These variants were also associated with a lower probability of heart failure among participants with T2D, providing tentative genetic support for a cardioprotective effect of SGLT2 inhibition.

title: Effects of Stellate Ganglion Blockade on Pulmonary Artery Pressure and Sympathetic Baroreflex Function at High Altitude: A Case Study in Treated Hypertension.
abstract: In this case study, we explored whether transient inhibition of sympathetic outflow with stellate ganglion blockade (SGB) modifies pulmonary artery pressure and sympathetic arterial baroreflex regulation during high-altitude (HA) exposure in an individual with treated hypertension. Methods: A 44-year-old man with treated hypertension underwent physiological assessments at sea level (220 m) and after 5 to 8 days of exposure to HA (3,800 m). Pulmonary artery systolic pressure (PASP), muscle sympathetic nerve activity (MSNA), beat-by-beat blood pressure (BP), carotid artery diameter, and spontaneous sympathetic baroreflex function (integrative and mechanical components) were assessed at sea level and during HA exposure. During HA exposure, these measurements were obtained following right ultrasound-guided SGB and compared with subsequent time-control visits. Results: HA exposure increased PASP, MSNA, BP, and BP variability compared with sea level. SGB reduced PASP, whereas no meaningful change occurred during the time-control visit. BP variability was lower following SGB than during the control visit. The integrative sympathetic arterial baroreflex relationship appeared steeper following SGB, and the mechanical component demonstrated a greater slope than during the time-control visit, consistent with altered mechanical baroreceptor transduction. Conclusions: These observations suggest that regional sympathetic inhibition may exert distinct influences on pulmonary artery pressure and sympathetic baroreflex regulation during sustained high-altitude exposure in treated hypertension.

title: From single to dual targeting: Recent advances in EGFR-based dual inhibitors for cancer therapy.
abstract: The epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) is a receptor tyrosine kinase whose overexpression and activating mutations drive the pathogenesis of solid tumors, particularly non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). ATP-competitive EGFR inhibitors have progressed through four generations with considerable clinical success, yet their durability is limited by acquired mutations such as T790 M and C797S and by activation of compensatory signaling pathways. Dual-targeting inhibitors are single chemical entities designed to engage two distinct molecular targets simultaneously, generally constructed by conjugating, fusing or merging the pharmacophores of two established ligands. Conjugation offers synthetic flexibility but increases molecular size; fusion reduces molecular size at the cost of potential affinity loss; merging yields the most drug-like molecules but requires substantial pharmacophore overlap. EGFR-based dual inhibitors retain EGFR as the primary target and add a second oncogenic node such as HER2, VEGFR-2 or microtubules. The structural plasticity of the EGFR kinase domain, together with its well-characterized hinge, back-pocket and solvent-exposed regions, tolerates side-chain and linker modification and has made EGFR a favored scaffold for this approach. Clinically approved multi-targeting agents including vandetanib and neratinib provide proof of principle. Such molecules can simplify pharmacokinetics relative to drug combinations, although a single emergent mutation may abolish both activities and broader target coverage can reduce selectivity, so clinical superiority over combination regimens has to be demonstrated for each target pair. This review examines studies published between 2020 and 2026 on EGFR-based dual inhibitors spanning 26 secondary targets, addressing rational design, structure-activity relationships, receptor-ligand interaction profiles, and preclinical and clinical efficacy, and identifies the strategies most likely to resolve the current limitations of EGFR-centered multi-target therapy.

title: Predictors of treatment response in rheumatoid arthritis: a narrative review.
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a common autoimmune disease having diverse responses to disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs. Although treat-to-target strategies have improved disease management, therapeutic selection remains largely empirical and a substantial proportion of patients fail to achieve adequate clinical response to their therapies. Therefore, reliable biomarkers capable of predicting treatment response before therapy initiation are urgently needed to guide personalised treatment decisions. Current evidence suggests that multiple categories of biomarkers may contribute to the prediction of treatment responses across different therapeutic agents in RA, including clinical characteristics, serological markers, cytokine profiles, genetic and transcriptomic signatures, immune-cell phenotypes, synovial pathotypes and microbiome features. This review summarises current biomarker strategies for predicting therapeutic response in RA and discusses their potential utility in improving precision medicine. However, most individual biomarkers show limited predictive power, partly due to the complex and dynamic nature of RA pathogenesis. Combining biomarkers from multiple biological dimensions, together with the continued exploration of novel predictive markers, may improve the robustness and accuracy of treatment response prediction in RA.

title: Recent research on vaccines for older adults.
abstract: Vaccination is increasingly recognised as a cornerstone of healthy ageing and geriatric care, extending beyond the prevention of infectious disease to potentially influence broader health outcomes. This Commentary article commemorates the launch of Age and Ageing's vaccines collection by highlighting key vaccine-related research published in the journal. It focuses on vaccine uptake, effectiveness and emerging research priorities for older adults. Uptake of recommended vaccines, including influenza, COVID-19, respiratory syncytial virus and pneumococcal vaccines, remains variable internationally and is challenged by vaccine hesitancy. Successful vaccination programmes combine healthcare professional education, centralised reminder systems and easy access to vaccination services. Studies involving care-home residents demonstrated that COVID-19 vaccines provided substantial protection against infection and, particularly, mortality, although effectiveness declines over time and is influenced by immunosenescence. Immunological studies reveal weaker vaccine responses among infection-naïve older adults, supporting the importance of booster programmes and strategies to enhance immunity. Emerging evidence also suggests that interventions such as probiotics may improve vaccine immunogenicity, although further high-quality trials are required. Beyond infection prevention, observational data indicate that several vaccines, may be associated with a reduced risk of dementia, particularly vascular dementia, though causal relationships remain unproven. Looking forward, greater inclusion of frail older adults and care home residents in vaccine trials is essential to strengthen the evidence base. Future research should support the development of novel vaccines, improve preparedness for future pandemics and optimise vaccination strategies to maximise healthy ageing and preserve function in later life.

title: Neoadjuvant durvalumab plus chemotherapy in resectable or borderline resectable non-small-cell lung cancer: the phase 2 MDT-BRIDGE trial.
abstract: The phase 2 MDT-BRIDGE study is investigating perioperative durvalumab plus neoadjuvant chemotherapy (AEGEAN regimen) in resectable and borderline resectable non-small-cell lung cancer and chemoradiotherapy (CRT) followed by consolidation durvalumab (PACIFIC regimen) in patients who become unresectable after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy guided by multidisciplinary team assessments during the neoadjuvant period. The primary endpoint was the overall resection rate (descriptive with no formal hypothesis testing). Secondary endpoints included event-free survival, progression-free survival, pathological complete response rate (resectable patients cohort), circulating tumor DNA clearance between baseline and presurgery/pre-CRT and safety. Overall, 142 patients received neoadjuvant treatment; 64.8% and 35.2% were deemed resectable and borderline resectable at baseline, respectively. The overall resection rate (95% confidence interval) was 74.6% (66.7‒81.6) in a population that included more than one-third of patients with borderline resectable disease. R0 resection rate was 96.2% (90.6‒99.0) in those who underwent surgery. Overall, 131 (92.3%) patients had surgery (n = 106) or CRT (n = 25) after neoadjuvant treatment, and 117 (82.4%) patients received adjuvant (n = 94) or consolidation (n = 23) durvalumab. During adjuvant or consolidation durvalumab, maximum grade 3/4 adverse events occurred in 7.4% of resected patients and 17.4% of CRT-treated patients, with 8.5% and 13.0% discontinuing treatment due to adverse events. This multidisciplinary team-guided approach was feasible and enabled delivery of curative-intent treatment (surgery or CRT), followed by durvalumab in most patients, and demonstrated encouraging preliminary efficacy with a manageable adjuvant or consolidation safety profile that was consistent with prior studies. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05925530 .

title: CD4+ T cell-licensed CD8+ T cells are required for immunotherapy response in MHC-I negative MMRd cancer.
abstract: DNA mismatch repair deficiency (MMRd) causes hypermutation and increased T cell response in multiple tumor types. MMRd colorectal cancers (CRC) display frequent immune evasion, but respond to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB), through uncertain mechanisms. We generated mouse models of MMRd CRC, and found that accelerated tumorigenesis was accompanied by loss of major histocompatibility class I (MHC-I) expression and exclusion of cytotoxic CD8+ T cells, but not helper CD4+ T cells. MHC-I deletion (MHC-IKO) in a syngeneic MMRd CRC model reduced tumor CD8+ but not CD4+ cell infiltrate, and accelerated tumor growth. MMRd MHC-IKO tumors were resistant to anti-PD1 ICB, but sensitive to anti-PD1 and anti-CTLA4 combination ICB (cICB) with response dependent on both CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, but not γδ-T cells. CD4+ cell depletion-induced cICB resistance was reversed by CD40 agonism, suggesting that CD4+ cells directly or indirectly license CD8+ cell for MHC-I-independent cytotoxicity. Investigation of MHC-I status as predictor of cICB vs ICB monotherapy appears worthwhile.

title: Effectiveness of NKG2D CAR-NK92 cells in targeting solid tumors: novel dynamic cytotoxicity analysis via real-time cell analysis.
abstract: Lung, colorectal, and liver cancers are among the most prevalent and lethal solid tumors globally. However, traditional therapeutic modalities and even current immunotherapeutic strategies such as chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy have failed to deliver durable clinical benefits. This limitation is primarily attributed to the challenges posed by tumor heterogeneity, off-target toxicity, and, critically, to the inadequate assessment of the dynamic anti-tumor efficacy of these treatments. A major bottleneck in the preclinical evaluation of CAR-based immunotherapies for solid tumors is the overreliance on static endpoint cytotoxicity assays, including lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) release and chromium-51 (51Cr) release assays. These conventional methods merely quantify the final extent of tumor cell lysis and are unable to capture critical kinetic parameters-such as response latency, cytotoxicity rate, and the capacity for complete tumor elimination in vitro-all of which are pivotal for predicting clinical applicability. To address this gap, we employed real-time cell analysis (RTCA), a label-free and continuous monitoring technology, to systematically evaluate the anti-tumor potency of NKG2D CAR-engineered NK92 cells against lung (H1299), colorectal (HCT116), and liver (Hep3B) cancer cell lines. RTCA's unique capability to track tumor cell viability at 15-min intervals revealed that NKG2D CAR-engineered NK92 cells initiated cytotoxicity immediately without a lag phase, exhibited steeper cytotoxicity slopes, and achieved complete target cell eradication at an effector-to-target (E:T) ratio of 5:1-dynamic insights that remained undetectable with static assays. Notably, using this advanced cell killing detection method, we found that NKG2D CAR-engineered natural killer (NK) cells displayed cytotoxicity kinetics comparable to those of five times the number of unmodified NK cells against H1299, HCT116 and Hep3B cell lines. At E:T ratios of 5:1, the engineered cells also secreted significantly higher levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IFN-γ and TNF-α) compared to unmodified NK92 cells. This confirmed robust immune activation that coincided with real-time tumor killing. These findings not only demonstrate that NKG2D CAR-engineered NK92 cells represent a promising immunotherapeutic candidate for solid tumors, but also highlight RTCA as a useful and informative platform for monitoring cytotoxicity kinetics in real time and advancing the translational development of solid tumor immunotherapies.

title: Clinical risk factors associated with coronary slow flow: a meta-analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To investigate factors associated with coronary slow flow (CSF) using a meta-analysis and to provide evidence-based support for the prevention and management of coronary artery disease. METHODS: Relevant studies published between January 1, 2015, and December 31, 2025, were retrieved from CNKI, CBM, Wanfang, VIP, PubMed, and Embase using the search terms "coronary slow flow," "coronary slow flow phenomenon," "coronary slow flow syndrome," "related factors," "influencing factors," and "risk factors." Case-control studies that met the predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria were included. Study quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS), with studies scoring ≥ 7 considered high quality. Meta-analysis was performed using RevMan version 5.3. This study was registered with PROSPERO (ID: CRD420261334323). RESULTS: A total of 41 studies were included in the systematic review. Quantitative meta-analysis was performed only for risk factors reported in a sufficient number of studies with comparable definitions and extractable data. The meta-analysis suggested that smoking (OR = 1.21, 95% CI: 1.13-1.29), higher body mass index (OR = 1.20, 95% CI: 1.06-1.36), male sex (OR = 1.51, 95% CI: 1.26-1.81), hypertension (OR = 2.32, 95% CI: 1.27-4.26), elevated homocysteine (OR = 1.55, 95% CI: 1.13-2.13), elevated high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (OR = 1.62, 95% CI: 1.36-1.94), and higher uric acid levels (OR = 1.90, 95% CI: 1.47-2.46) were associated with higher odds of CSF. In contrast, higher high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) levels were associated with lower odds of CSF (OR = 0.45, 95% CI: 0.38-0.55). CONCLUSION: Coronary slow flow (CSF) may be associated with multiple clinical and biochemical factors. Smoking, increased body mass index, male sex, hypertension, and elevated levels of homocysteine, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, and uric acid were associated with higher odds of CSF, whereas higher HDL-C levels were associated with lower odds of CSF. These findings suggest that unhealthy lifestyle behaviors, metabolic abnormalities, and inflammatory responses may contribute to the development of CSF. Although many CSF-associated factors are potentially modifiable, early interventions-particularly smoking cessation, blood pressure and weight control, and improvement of metabolic and inflammatory status-may help reduce the likelihood of CSF. However, these associations should be interpreted cautiously because moderate-to-high heterogeneity remained in several pooled analyses. Future high-quality prospective studies are needed to clarify the relative importance of these factors, examine potential causal relationships, and evaluate targeted interventions.

title: Effect of dapagliflozin on left ventricular longitudinal strain and atrioventricular coupling in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and chronic kidney disease.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i), including dapagliflozin, were initially developed for type 2 diabetes mellitus. Despite the established benefits of SGLT2i in heart failure (HF) with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), their effects on myocardial deformation (assessed by global longitudinal strain, GLS) and left atrioventricular coupling (quantified by the left atrioventricular coupling index, LACI) in HFpEF patients with concomitant chronic kidney disease (CKD)-hereafter referred to as HFpEF-CKD-remain unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of dapagliflozin on GLS and LACI in this high-risk comorbid population. METHODS: This prospective cohort study enrolled 259 patients with HFpEF-CKD from September 2023 to October 2024. Participants were assigned to two groups: the dapagliflozin group (dapagliflozin 10 mg/day added to conventional HF and CKD therapy without SGLT2i, n = 138) and the control group (conventional HF and CKD therapy without SGLT2i, n = 121). Conventional and speckle-tracking echocardiography were performed at baseline and 6-month follow-up to assess GLS, LACI, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and left atrial volume (LAV) parameters, including minimal LAV (LAVmin) and LAV index (LAVI). RESULTS: Compared with controls, dapagliflozin decreased GLS (between-group Δ: -1.34%, 95% CI: -1.72 to -0.97; Cohen's d = 0.875) and reduced LACI (Δ: -0.07, 95% CI: -0.09 to -0.05; Cohen's d = 0.855), both p < 0.001. The dapagliflozin group showed greater reductions in LAV parameters (ΔLAVmin: -6.38 ± 9.06 mL vs. -1.25 ± 3.78 mL, p < 0.001; ΔLAVI: -0.82 ± 1.79 mL/m2 vs. -0.43 ± 1.57 mL/m2, p = 0.075). LVEF remained stable in both groups (p = 0.264). Multivariable regression analysis confirmed dapagliflozin as an independent predictor for both GLS reduction (B = -1.335, 95% CI: -1.686 to -1.006, p < 0.001) and LACI reduction (B = -0.057, 95% CI: -0.074 to -0.040, p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: In patients with HFpEF-CKD, dapagliflozin improves left ventricular longitudinal function and atrioventricular coupling. The superior sensitivity of novel echocardiographic parameters-GLS, LACI, and LAVmin-supports their clinical utility for monitoring early cardiac functional recovery during treatment.

title: Rethinking evidence generation in gastrointestinal cancer treatment research: the need for both high-quality interventional and observational evidence.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The current research ecosystem on gastrointestinal (GI) cancers-including anal, colorectal, esogastric, pancreatic, hepatocellular, and biliary tract cancers-relies heavily on randomized controlled trials (RCTs), which involve high costs and limited transportability. MAIN BODY: Fewer than 10% of therapeutic recommendations for pancreatic adenocarcinoma are based on high-level evidence, a proportion that has not improved between 2011 and 2022. Furthermore, substantial research waste undermines interventional research in GI cancer: 30-37% of completed GI cancer trials lack publicly available results, and only 59% of gastric cancer trials are published as full-text articles. Such waste in research negatively impacts evidence synthesis and guidelines recommendations. While interventional research is the only way to assess the efficacy of a new drug, observational studies and real-world evidence (RWE), using health records, cohorts, registries and/or administrative databases, may offer complementary insights, especially for research questions that cannot be studied by RCTs. In particular, RWE can evaluate treatments in elderly or comorbid patients often excluded from trials, inform decisions for rare tumors such as digestive neuroendocrine neoplasms, and evaluate real-world effectiveness of treatments such as targeted therapies or immunotherapy. While historically RWE reliability was often criticized for biases and data quality issues, methodological advances, such as target trial emulation and data standardization, have enhanced its validity, and it is now increasingly used to support regulatory decisions by agencies like the Food and Drug Administration and the European Medicines Agency. CONCLUSIONS: Better integration of high quality interventional and observational approaches is essential in GI cancer research. Guidance on when to use interventional versus observational studies, depending on the clinical question, may help put this integration into practice. This synergy could reduce research waste, accelerate evidence generation, and help identify more effective personalized treatments for GI cancer patients.

title: Blocking aryl hydrocarbon receptor remodels myeloid-T cell crosstalk and enhances anti-PD-1 response in the tumor microenvironment.
abstract: PURPOSE: Cancer metabolism-associated immune suppression remains a major barrier to durable therapeutic responses. Indoleamine-2,3-dioxygenase 1 has been pursued as a therapeutic target, but incomplete pathway suppression has limited clinical success. As the aryl hydrocarbon receptor is a ligand-activated transcription factor and downstream effector of tryptophan metabolism, we investigated how myeloid-cell aryl hydrocarbon receptor signaling shapes the tumor immune microenvironment and whether its inhibition can restore antitumor immunity. METHODS: Conditional aryl hydrocarbon receptor knockout mice targeting dendritic cells or macrophages were used to evaluate the effects of genetic aryl hydrocarbon receptor ablation. Pharmacologic inhibition was assessed using DA-4505 across syngeneic lung, colorectal, and breast cancer models and an immune checkpoint inhibitor-refractory humanized patient-derived xenograft model. Therapeutic efficacy was evaluated alone or in combination with anti-programmed cell death protein 1 therapy, chemotherapy, or surgery. Tumor growth, survival, metastasis, and immune remodeling were analyzed by flow cytometry, multiplex immunohistochemistry, single-cell RNA sequencing, cytokine profiling, and human tumor datasets. RESULTS: Conditional aryl hydrocarbon receptor depletion in macrophages and dendritic cells enhanced innate and adaptive immune activation, increased interferon-γ-producing T cells, and strengthened antitumor immunity. In mouse tumor models, pharmacologic aryl hydrocarbon receptor blockade enhanced macrophage chemotaxis and activation programs, promoted M1-like macrophage polarization, increased interferon-γ-producing CD8+ T cells, and reduced regulatory T cells and polymorphonuclear myeloid-derived suppressor cells. These changes promoted robust T-cell activation and durable tumor control. Aryl hydrocarbon receptor inhibition further synergized with chemotherapy, surgery, and immune checkpoint blockade, leading to expansion of effector and memory T-cell populations and sustained antitumor responses. In a humanized lung cancer model, aryl hydrocarbon receptor blockade increased intratumoral CD8+ T-cell infiltration and cytotoxic-memory programs while reducing regulatory T-cell enrichment. In human tumor datasets, aryl hydrocarbon receptor-positive macrophages correlated with FOXP3+ T-cell infiltration, and higher aryl hydrocarbon receptor inhibition-associated T-cell signatures were associated with improved patient survival.

title: Characterization and treatment of ischemic stroke in patients with infective endocarditis: a meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke is a common and serious complication of infective bacterial endocarditis. This study aimed to characterize the frequency, clinical and pathological features, treatment strategies, and outcomes of patients with stroke due to infective endocarditis. METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed from database inception to October 2022 for studies reporting on stroke in patients with infective endocarditis and performed a meta-analysis. RESULTS: A total of 122 studies comprising 270,211 patients with infective endocarditis were included. Ischemic stroke occurred in 21% and hemorrhagic stroke in 5% of patients. Stroke was observed in 32% of patients with mitral valve endocarditis, 25% with aortic valve, and 11% with tricuspid valve endocarditis. Stroke was associated with significantly higher mortality (OR 2.35; 95%CI 1.74-3.16). Staphylococcus and Streptococcus species were most frequently associated with stroke (33% and 25%, respectively). The risk of stroke did not differ significantly between patients with and without pre-existing antithrombotic therapy (37% vs. 24%; OR 1.24, 95%CI 0.75-2.06). Successful reperfusion was achieved in 80% of patients undergoing mechanical thrombectomy, although mortality remained high at 49%. CONCLUSIONS: Stroke is a common complication of infective bacterial endocarditis and has a substantial impact on patient outcomes. It occurs most frequently in patients with mitral valve endocarditis and in those with infections caused by staphylococcal pathogens. Stroke risk was not reduced in patients with pre-existing antithrombotic therapy, supporting discontinuation where no other indication exists. Mechanical thrombectomy in patients with endocarditis-related large vessel occlusion achieves high recanalization rates; however, overall clinical outcomes remain poor in this population.

title: Impact of anatomical changes on simulated proton arc therapy and intensity-modulated proton therapy for lung cancer.
abstract: PURPOSE: During lung cancer radiotherapy, inter-fractional anatomical changes may cause the delivered dose to deviate from the primary plan, affecting tumor control and increasing the risk of normal tissue damage. This study aims to evaluate the impact of anatomical changes on the dosimetric and radiobiological performance of simulated proton arc therapy (sPAT) versus intensity-modulated proton therapy (IMPT) for lung cancer patients under patient-specific anatomical changes. METHODS: Data from 21 lung cancer patients were retrospectively analyzed. The prescribed dose for all patients was 6000 cGy (relative biological effectiveness, RBE). Each patient with a primary planning computed tomography (pCT) and a mid-treatment adaptive-planning CT (aCT) acquired at a median of 29 days into treatment due to notable tumor volume changes. Primary plans for sPAT and IMPT were designed on the pCT. After rigid registration of the pCT and aCT, non-adaptive plans (sPATp-a, IMPTp-a) were generated by directly recalculating the doses of the primary plans on the aCT. The comparison evaluated the dosimetric impact of anatomical changes by comparing non-adaptive plans (sPATp-a vs. IMPTp-a). Dose-volume histogram (DVH) parameters for targets and organs at risk (OARs) and tumor control probability (TCP) and normal tissue complication probability (NTCP) were evaluated. RESULTS: For the primary plans, sPAT and IMPT achieved similar target coverage, while the doses to OARs were generally lower in sPATp. Under anatomical changes, both non-adaptive plans exhibited a decrease in target coverage, sPATp-a achieved a D95% of 5567.57 cGy[RBE] compared with 5423.33 cGy[RBE] for IMPTp-a (p < 0.001), indicating that sPAT better preserved target coverage. Compared with the primary plans, sPATp-a and IMPTp-a exhibited TCP reductions of 5.83% and 8.07%, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Compared with IMPT, sPAT exhibits enhanced robustness against inter-fractional anatomical changes occurring in lung-cancer radiotherapy.
journal: Journal of applied clinical medical physics

title: Use of SGLT2 Inhibitors, GLP-1 Receptor Agonists, and DPP-4 Inhibitors in Incident Hyponatremia in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes: Multicenter Target Trial Emulations.
abstract: Hyponatremia poses risks in type 2 diabetes, yet comparative electrolyte safety across glucose-lowering therapies remains unclear. We evaluated the risk of incident hyponatremia associated with sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), and dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitors in real-world practice. Using electronic health records from 155 healthcare organizations in the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network, we conducted multicenter active-comparator, new-user target trial emulations with 1:1 propensity score matching. For each pairwise comparison, adults with type 2 diabetes initiating either drug class, with no record of either class during the preceding 365 days, were included. The primary outcome was incident hyponatremia (ICD-10-CM E87.1 or serum sodium ≤ 135 mmol/L); sensitivity outcomes included diagnosis-only, laboratory-only, and stricter laboratory thresholds. Among more than 300,000 matched pairs per comparison, SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 RAs were each associated with a 15% lower hazard of hyponatremia than DPP-4 inhibitors (hazard ratio [HR], 0.850; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.842-0.858 and HR, 0.847; 95% CI: 0.838-0.856). The lower risk persisted at stricter sodium thresholds and across clinically relevant subgroups, including patients with heart failure, chronic kidney disease, or high-risk medications use. SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 RAs were broadly comparable (HR, 0.962; 95% CI: 0.952-0.971). Positive and negative control outcomes were consistent with expectations. Overall, SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 RAs were associated with a lower risk of incident hyponatremia than DPP-4 inhibitors. These real-world findings provide reassurance regarding the electrolyte safety of SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 RAs, complementing their established cardiorenal benefits.

title: EGFR-TKI-associated colitis in non-small cell lung cancer: a retrospective characterization of clinical, radiographic, endoscopic, and histopathologic features.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKIs) are standard targeted therapies for EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but clinically documented EGFR-TKI-associated colitis remains incompletely characterized. We aimed to describe its clinical, radiographic, endoscopic, histopathologic, management, and exploratory survival features. METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective case-control analysis nested within an institutional cohort of 3,285 patients with NSCLC treated with EGFR-TKIs between January 2018 and July 2025. The analysis included 43 patients with documented radiographic and/or endoscopic colitis and 223 selected asymptomatic controls. Clinical, imaging, colonoscopic, histopathologic, treatment, and survival data were reviewed. Ever-smoking was examined in an exploratory univariable logistic analysis. Drug-specific EGFR-TKI odds were not estimated because a common time-aligned exposure definition for cases and controls could not be reconstructed, and overall survival was examined exploratorily. RESULTS: Clinically documented EGFR-TKI-associated colitis occurred in 43/3,285 treated patients (1.3%). Ever-smoking was more frequent among cases than selected controls (39.5% vs. 20.2%; univariable odds ratio = 2.586, 95% confidence interval: 1.293-5.173, P = 0.007). Drug-specific odds were not estimated because a common time-aligned exposure definition could not be reconstructed. Median symptom onset was 3 months. Diarrhea occurred in 40/43 patients (93.0%); three patients had grade 0 diarrhea. Among 39 patients undergoing colonoscopy, 14 had normal-appearing mucosa; 11 of these patients underwent biopsy and showed histologic inflammation. Of 35 classifiable biopsies, 10 (28.6%) showed a microscopic pattern, 14 (40.0%) an inflammatory/IBD-like pattern, and 11 (31.4%) an ischemic-like pattern. In exploratory survival analysis, no statistically significant association between documented colitis and overall survival was detected (log-rank P = 0.538; adjusted HR = 1.184, 95% CI: 0.782-1.793, P = 0.426). CONCLUSION: Clinically documented EGFR-TKI-associated colitis showed heterogeneous radiographic, endoscopic, and histopathologic patterns. Normal-appearing mucosa did not exclude histologic inflammation in biopsied patients. The 1.3% value represents documented cases in this institutional cohort rather than population incidence. The recorded smoking difference, severity-stratified findings, treatment outcomes, and survival estimates should be interpreted as exploratory; no drug-specific colitis association is inferred.

title: Chinese medicine combined with EGFR-TKIs in EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC: a meta-analysis of efficacy and safety.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: For advanced EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKI) therapy is the primary treatment, but drug resistance and side effects reduce its effectiveness. Integrating Chinese and Western medicine is a key focus in cancer treatment. This study evaluates the clinical benefits of combining traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) with EGFR-TKI, summarizing TCM syndromes and medication traits. METHODS: We searched six databases for relevant clinical studies. A meta-analysis assessed progression-free survival (PFS), disease control rate (DCR), and adverse reactions, with subgroup analysis by EGFR mutation type. A TCM syndrome network was created to examine syndrome distribution and core prescription patterns. RESULTS: TCM combined with EGFR-TKIs significantly improved PFS (HR = 0.70, 95%CI 0.65-0.76, p < 0.00001, I2 = 0%), benefiting patients with Exon 19 deletion or L858R mutation equally (p = 0.75). The combination therapy increased DCR (RR = 1.19, 95% CI 1.01-1.40, p = 0.04), with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 89%), and reduced targeted-agent-related adverse reactions. Qi-Yin and Lung-Spleen deficiency were the dominant TCM syndromes, managed via Qi-tonifying, Yin-nourishing and spleen-strengthening regimens. CONCLUSION: Integrating TCM with EGFR-TKI enhances tumor control and treatment safety in advanced NSCLC patients with EGFR mutations, showing consistent efficacy across various mutation types. This approach, which considers clinical syndrome differentiation and medication patterns in Chinese medicine, offers evidence-based guidance for personalized treatment. This review was performed following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261398486, identifier CRD420261398486.

title: Perception of virus effects and vaccination among people with multiple sclerosis in Saudi Arabia.
abstract: BACKGROUND: People with multiple sclerosis (pwMS) are at increased risk of infection due to immune dysregulation and exposure to disease-modifying therapies (DMTs). Despite this risk, real-world vaccine uptake remains inconsistent. This study evaluated vaccination readiness, counseling practices, and infection-related perceptions among pwMS in Saudi Arabia. METHODS: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among adults with MS (n = 204) recruited using non-probability (convenience) sampling from tertiary-care clinical and community-based sources. The survey assessed demographic characteristics, vaccination attitudes and uptake, counseling experiences, perceptions of infection risk related to MS and DMTs, and awareness of Epstein-Barr virus (EBV). Internal consistency of multi-item measures was acceptable (Cronbach's α = 0.72). Descriptive statistics were used to summarize outcomes. RESULTS: The cohort was relatively young (mean age 35.7 years), with two-thirds aged 25-44 years (25-34 years: 38.2%; 35-44 years: 36.8%). Most participants held a bachelor's degree (66.7%). Attitudes toward routine vaccination were frequently non-committal: 47.6% were somewhat or very likely to vaccinate, 33.8% were neutral, and 18.6% were somewhat or very unlikely; separately, 60.8% agreed or somewhat agreed that routine vaccines might be harmful for pwMS. COVID-19 vaccination uptake was high (72.5%), whereas influenza vaccination was low (30.9%). Uptake of other adult vaccines, including hepatitis B, meningococcal, herpes zoster, and human papillomavirus vaccines, was < 10% for each. Perceived infection vulnerability was substantial, with 62.7% expressing concern about viral infections due to MS and 71.1% believing that DMTs increased susceptibility, consistent with 59.4% receiving high-efficacy DMTs. Awareness of EBV was limited: 26.5% had heard of EBV, 16.6% perceived an MS-EBV association, and 21.1% were aware of possible causality. Nearly half of participants (49.0%) were undecided about a hypothetical EBV vaccine, while approximately 44% expressed willingness to receive it. Counseling gaps were evident, as only 32.8% reported any discussion about vaccination with clinicians; counseling prior to DMT initiation and during ongoing treatment was reported by 16.2% and 19.1%, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: In a young and highly educated cohort of pwMS in Saudi Arabia, vaccine hesitancy and counseling gaps persist despite high perceived infection risk. These findings highlight the need for structured and routine vaccine counseling, particularly at MS diagnosis and before initiating high-efficacy DMTs, to improve uptake of influenza and other recommended adult vaccines in MS clinics.

title: The Role and Mechanism of SGLT2 Inhibitors in Chronic Kidney Disease.
abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) refers to structural or functional abnormalities of the kidneys caused by various factors lasting ≥3 months, or a decline in glomerular filtration rate (GFR) of <60 mL/min of unknown cause lasting ≥3 months. Its primary causes include diabetic kidney disease, hypertensive nephropathy, IgA nephropathy, membranous nephropathy, and lupus nephritis, among others. As a new class of antidiabetic drugs, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) have been shown in numerous clinical studies and animal experiments to be effective in treating CKD of various etiologies. The renoprotective effects of SGLT2 inhibitors are independent of their glucose-lowering effects. Through mechanisms such as hemodynamics, oxidative stress, and anti-fibrosis, they reduce serum creatinine and urinary protein levels, thereby slowing the progression of CKD. This review primarily summarizes clinical and basic research on SGLT2i in the treatment of CKD and analyzes the signaling pathways through which SGLT2i exerts its effects on CKD. This demonstrates that SGLT2 inhibitors can delay the progression of kidney function decline and improve outcomes in patients across various subtypes through multiple mechanisms. They are suitable for patients with CKD of different etiologies and across different estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) categories, indicating the significant potential and promising prospects for the widespread use of SGLT2 inhibitors in patients with CKD.

title: Diabetic Retinopathy Risk in SGLT2i vs GLP1RA Initiators With CKD Stages 3-4 and Type 2 Diabetes.
abstract: RATIONALE & OBJECTIVE: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP1RA) have demonstrated renal and cardiovascular benefits among patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) and type 2 diabetes (T2D). However, their comparative effects on diabetic retinopathy (DR) outcomes in patients with CKD stages 3-4 and T2D remain unclear. This study aimed to demonstrate the effect of SGLT2i vs GLP1RA in this population. STUDY DESIGN: Population-based, new-user, active comparator cohort study comparing SGLT2i versus GLP1RA initiators. Subjects were divided into 2 cohorts: (1) incident nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy (NPDR) and (2) DR progression cohort. SETTING & STUDY POPULATION: Patients with CKD stages 3-4 and T2D across 3 US health care databases: Optum's de-identified Clinformatics Data Mart Database (2014-2024), Merative MarketScan (2014-2022), and Medicare Fee-for-Service (2014-2020). SELECTION CRITERIA FOR STUDIES: Adults with a new prescription for either SGLT2i or GLP1RA without prior use in the preceding 365 days. The primary outcomes were incident NPDR and DR progression, identified through ICD-9/10 diagnosis codes and procedural codes for retinopathy treatments. DATA EXTRACTION: Exposures, covariates, and outcomes were obtained from structured claims fields. ANALYTICAL APPROACH: Both cohorts were analyzed using propensity score matching (1:1) to control for confounding. Incidence rates (IRs), rate differences, and hazard ratios (HRs) were calculated. RESULTS: After 1:1 propensity score matching, the study included 20,135 matched patient pairs in the incident NPDR cohort and 7,763 matched pairs in the DR progression cohort. For incident NPDR, there was no difference between SGLT2i and GLP1RA groups (IR 29.55 vs 30.38 per 1,000 person-years, respectively; HR 0.98 [95% CI, 0.87-1.10]). Similarly, DR progression was not different between groups (IR 32.73 vs 35.24 per 1,000 person-years; HR 0.92 [95% CI, 0.76-1.12]). Subgroup analyses showed no differences in HRs for both incident NPDR and DR progression across multiple predefined subgroups. LIMITATIONS: Potential for residual confounding, outcome misclassification, and limited generalizability to non-U.S. populations. CONCLUSIONS: Initiation of SGLT2i was not associated with a different risk of incident NPDR or DR progression compared with GLP1RA among patients with CKD stages 3-4 and T2D. Additional studies with extended follow-up are needed to better characterize long-term retinal safety profiles of these therapies.

title: SGLT2 Inhibitors for the Primary Prevention of CKD in Type 2 Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors slow the progression of chronic kidney disease (CKD), although their potential to prevent the development of CKD in type 2 diabetes needs to be examined. PURPOSE: To evaluate SGLT2 inhibitors for the primary prevention of CKD in people with type 2 diabetes. DATA SOURCES: PubMed and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) were searched through October 2025. DATA SYNTHESIS: Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of SGLT2 inhibitors compared with placebo or other glucose-lowering agents in people with type 2 diabetes without baseline CKD were included. Outcomes were estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) decline and incident albuminuria (i.e., urine albumin-to-creatine ratio [UACR] ≥30 mg/g). Random-effects meta-analyses were performed, and heterogeneity was assessed with I 2. Certainty of evidence was evaluated with Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE). RESULTS: Eight RCTs were included: five cardiovascular outcomes trials comparing SGLT2 inhibitors and placebo (24,072 participants) and three trials comparing SGLT2 inhibitors and sulfonylureas (2,889 participants). Compared with placebo, SGLT2 inhibitors reduced the risk of incident albuminuria (three trials; hazard ratio 0.82; 95% CI 0.77-0.88; I 2 = 0%, high certainty) and slowed eGFR decline based on the chronic eGFR slope (five trials; mean difference [MD] 0.95 [95% CI 0.84-1.07] mL/min/1.73 m2/year; I 2 = 19%, high certainty) and total eGFR slope (four trials; MD 0.76 [0.50-1.03] mL/min/1.73 m2/year; I 2 = 88%, moderate certainty). Compared with sulfonylureas, SGLT2 inhibitors slowed eGFR decline based on the chronic eGFR slope (three trials; MD 2.43 [1.72-3.13] mL/min/1.73 m2/year; I 2 = 55%, moderate certainty). CONCLUSIONS: In people with type 2 diabetes without CKD, SGLT2 inhibitors slow eGFR decline compared with both placebo and sulfonylureas and prevent incident albuminuria compared with placebo. title: The relationship between cardiometabolic disease and vertebral bone strength, mineral density, and mass in US adults.
abstract: CONTEXT: Cardiometabolic disease (CMD) may increase vertebral fracture risk through deterioration in bone structure and/or tissue properties, compromising bone strength. OBJECTIVE: Evaluate the relationship between CMD and vertebral bone measures. DESIGN: Cross-sectional. PARTICIPANTS: Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults (CARDIA) study participants with year 25 (2010-2011) abdominal computed tomography (CT) scans (n = 2728). EXPOSURE: CMD (abdominal obesity, diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, or hypertension) status (≥1 vs 0) and burden (0, 1, 2, ≥3). OUTCOME MEASURES: Vertebral strength, volumetric bone mineral density (vBMD), and bone mass, obtained via biomechanical CT analysis. METHODS: Multivariable linear regression evaluated the association between CMD and vertebral bone measures. Sex-specific models were adjusted for age, race, height, weight, and additional social determinants of health, lifestyle factors, and comorbidities. Effect modification by race, age, and menopausal status was evaluated. RESULTS: Overall, at least 1 CMD was identified in 72.3% of men and 70.5% of women. In the fully adjusted model, CMD status was significantly associated with lower total (β = -6.32 mg/cm3; P = .018), trabecular (β = -4.53 mg/cm3; P = .048), and cortical (β = -6.63 mg/cm3; P = .034) vBMD in men. Greater CMD burden was associated with lower total and trabecular vBMD. The negative association between CMD and vBMD was stronger in men ≤50 years. There was no association in women. CONCLUSION: In this biracial cohort of Black and White adults from the United States, CMD was associated with significantly lower total and subcompartment vertebral vBMD in men.

title: Low-affinity anti-HER2-CAR T cells efficiently eradicate HER2+ and HER2low cancer cells with reduced toxicity on healthy tissue.
abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy is considered a therapeutic breakthrough in hematological malignancies. However, its translation to metastasized solid tumors remains limited by the paucity of "druggable" targets and the limited therapeutic potency of the cell therapeutics in solid cancers. Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2), a promising target for treatment of metastasized solid cancers, is amplified in around 3% (HER2+ cancer) and overexpressed without amplification in ∼40% (HER2low cancer) of all carcinomas, yet the physiological expression of HER2 on healthy tissues poses the risk of on-target off-tumor effects. To address this, we utilized low-affinity (LA) Anti-HER2-CAR T cells. These CAR T cells exhibited efficient lysis of HER2+ SKOV3 ovarian cancer cells even at low effector-to-target ratios. Following stimulation through cancer cells, LA Anti-HER2-CAR T cells showed rapid proliferation and elevation of pro-inflammatory cytokines markers. Low numbers of CAR T cells were sufficient to induce durable complete remissions of systemically seeded ovarian cancer in NOD-Prkdc scid -IL2rg Tm1 /Rj mice. LA Anti-HER2 CAR T cells also exhibited tumor regression and lasting tumor control in a subcutaneous in vivo model of HER2low LS174T cells. Additionally, the LA and high-affinity (HA) CAR T cells could effectively combat HER2low human colorectal cancer (CRC) cell lines and primary CRC organoids, while LA Anti-HER2-CAR T cells showed a trend-wise reduced lysis of healthy colon organoids. Our results suggest that LA Anti-HER2-CAR T cells provide a novel treatment option for HER2-overexpressing advanced systemic tumors. Importantly, they effectively distinguished between healthy colon tissue and HER2low cancer, broadening the scope of HER2-directed CAR T cells to this frequent cancer subset.

title: Short-term effects of an SGLT2 inhibitor on divalent ions in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease: a randomized crossover trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors are a cornerstone of chronic kidney disease therapy, reducing disease progression, cardiovascular events, and mortality. Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) patients were excluded from major trials, and data on electrolyte handling with SGLT2 inhibitors, in combination with tolvaptan, are lacking. METHODS: SIDIA was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, two-period crossover trial in 15 adults with ADPKD (mean estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) 68 ml/min/1.73 m2; median age 43 years). Participants received empagliflozin 10 mg or placebo for 14 days, separated by a 2-week washout. The primary endpoint was 24 h urinary and fractional excretion of phosphate, calcium, and magnesium. Exploratory secondary endpoints included markers of kidney stone propensity, inflammation, vitamin D metabolism, and tolerability. Treatment effects were estimated using generalized linear mixed models. Given the small sample size, analyses were exploratory and focused on effect estimation. RESULTS: For the primary endpoint, neither 24 h urinary nor fractional excretion of phosphate, calcium, or magnesium differed between empagliflozin and placebo. Empagliflozin lowered serum uric acid (-26%), increased serum magnesium (+5.7%) and urinary citrate (+78.6%), and reduced blood pressure (-4/-7 mmHg). An expected decline in eGFR (-7.1%) was observed, with no major short-term safety signals observed. Copeptin levels increased with empagliflozin (+26%). CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory mechanistic trial, no substantial short-term difference in urinary or fractional excretion of divalent ions were detected with empagliflozin. The observed changes in serum magnesium, urinary citrate, uric acid, and copeptin are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in larger, longer-term studies.

title: From macrofungal polysaccharides to precision microbial immunotherapy: reprogramming the tumor microenvironment through immunometabolic and gene-regulatory pathways.
abstract: Engineered microbial immunotherapies can localize immune-modulating signals within solid tumors, where hypoxia, suppressive myeloid cells, deficient antigen presentation, and dysfunctional T-cell trafficking often limit immunotherapy. Macrofungal polysaccharides, especially structurally defined β-glucans, offer mechanistic templates rather than interchangeable drug substances for source-specific, structure-controlled immune engineering programs. Their activity depends on linkage, branching, molecular mass, conformation, solubility, aggregation, and physical presentation. Critically, the strongest Dectin-1 and trained-immunity evidence discussed here uses particulate β-glucans from Saccharomyces cerevisiae; those findings cannot be assigned directly to macrofungal β-glucans without material-specific comparison.
