We therefore distinguish four engineering architectures: de novo microbial biosynthesis of a defined β-glucan, microbial surface display, delivery of a pre-characterized β-glucan cargo, and delivery of non-glycan payloads that mimic the desired downstream immune program. Because therapeutic bacteria have not yet been shown to reproduce a macrofungal β-glucan with controlled linkage, branching, conformation, and presentation, near-term development should prioritize standardized cargo delivery or pathway mimicry. In pancreatic and colorectal cancer models, yeast whole-glucan particles have altered myeloid trafficking or generated epigenetically and metabolically trained macrophages linked to CXCL9/CXCL10 production, natural killer-cell recruitment, conventional type 1 dendritic-cell accumulation, and stronger CD8 T-cell responses. Human evidence remains preliminary and cannot establish β-glucan-specific efficacy in uncontrolled combination studies. This Perspective proposes source-resolved material characterization, receptor and cell-state testing, multidimensional pharmacodynamic biomarkers, and microbial safety controls as prerequisites for translating fungal-inspired immune programs into precision cancer therapeutics.

title: Tumor antigens across cancer progression: from immune recognition and selection to precision cancer immunotherapy.
abstract: Tumor antigens provide the molecular interface between malignant transformation and host immunity, but their biological significance is determined by more than their molecular existence. Antigen clonality, abundance, processing, human leukocyte antigen (HLA) presentation, dendritic-cell function, T-cell recognition, spatial immune organization, and the surrounding tumor microenvironment (TME) collectively determine whether an antigen becomes immunologically visible and therapeutically actionable. Across cancer progression, tumor-cell antigenic states and the TME undergo reciprocal selection: immune pressure can eliminate highly visible clones while favoring antigen-loss variants, HLA defects, immune exclusion, suppressive myeloid and stromal states, and treatment-resistant populations. Recent single-cell, spatial and three-dimensional imaging, as well as immunopeptidomic studies show that this evolution is heterogeneous across tumor regions and anatomical compartments rather than a uniform linear process. This review therefore advances an antigen-TME co-evolution framework linking primary tumors, lymphatic and nodal immune compartments, systemic dissemination, distant metastatic niches, therapy, minimal residual disease, and recurrence. It critically evaluates the strengths and limitations of the classical immunoediting model; compares melanoma, breast, colorectal, lung, prostate, sarcoma, and virus-associated cancers according to antigen source, clonality, presentation competence, immune architecture, and dominant therapeutic bottleneck; and examines clinical translation through checkpoint blockade, cellular therapy, vaccines, antibodies, antibody-drug conjugates, immunopeptidomics, and computational antigen prediction. Particular attention is given to the gap between predicted peptide binding and verified presentation or immunogenicity, the need for longitudinal rather than single-biopsy profiling, and the requirement for prospective validation of artificial-intelligence models. The central conclusion is that tumor antigens become clinically meaningful only when antigenic state and microenvironmental context are assessed together, providing a more rigorous foundation for precision cancer immunotherapy.

title: Uncovering KRAS-mutant allele-specific biology and vulnerabilities in non-small cell lung cancer.
abstract: KRAS (Kirsten-Ras) mutations are the most commonly occurring oncogenic drivers in non-small cell lung cancer. Despite the discovery of KRAS inhibitors representing a translational breakthrough for KRAS-driven cancers, resistance remains a major clinical challenge. We believe that to circumvent resistance, an in-depth understanding of the biological differences and therapeutic vulnerabilities specific to KRAS mutations is critical to inform rational combination partners with either mutant-selective or broad-spectrum (K)RAS inhibitors. The present review draws upon insights from both preclinical and clinical studies exploring KRAS-mutant allele-specific behaviours and therapeutic vulnerabilities. We will also highlight studies in which targeting of these vulnerabilities was combined with (K)RAS inhibitors, offering contextual examples of KRAS-mutant allele-tailored therapeutic strategies.

title: Hypoxia-inducible CEA-targeted CAR T-cell therapy for relapsed stage IV non-small cell lung cancer.
abstract: Mitigating on-target off-tumor toxicity remains a central challenge for chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy for solid tumors. We developed a hypoxia-inducible CAR-T-cell product targeting carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) that restricts CAR activation to hypoxic tumor niches via oxygen-dependent expression control. In this first-in-human, phase I trial enrolling heavily pretreated patients with relapsed stage IV non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), a single infusion of the investigational product achieved an objective response rate of 47% and a disease control rate of 87%, with a manageable safety profile. Exploratory analyses showed that clinical outcomes were associated with baseline factors. Deep single-cell profiling indicated that the clinical response was associated with the expansion of hypoxia-adapted, tumor-reactive-like CD8+ T cells alongside coordinated functional maturation of natural killer (NK) cells. Collectively, these data provide clinical proof-of-concept for hypoxia-inducible CAR design and inform the rational development of strategies leveraging tumor microenvironmental features in solid tumor cellular immunotherapy.

title: Drug-Loaded Bacterial Outer Membrane Vesicles Eradicate Intratumoral Fusobacterium nucleatum to Enhance Colorectal Cancer Treatment.
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) represents one of the most commonly diagnosed malignancies in which Fusobacterium nucleatum (Fn) infiltration critically drives tumor progression by fostering an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) that compromises immunotherapy efficacy. Outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) originating from Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 offer an attractive tumor-targeting drug delivery system, combining intrinsic immunostimulatory properties with drug-loading capacity. We therefore developed an OMV-based dual-function system coencapsulating 5-fluorouracil (5-Fu) and metronidazole (MTZ), designated 5-Fu/MTZ@OMVs. In vitro, this system effectively eliminated both CT26 cells and Fn while promoting DC maturation and driving repolarization of M2 macrophages toward M1 as well as N2 neutrophils toward N1. In vivo, upon administration to an Fn-colonized CT26 model, the system homed to tumors, reduced the Fn burden, and inhibited tumor growth, demonstrating its bactericidal and antitumor efficacy. Notably, it reversed immunosuppressive TME by promoting DC maturation, M1 macrophage, and N1 neutrophil polarization, which enhanced the recruitment and functional activation of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells within the tumor. Thus, by integrating bactericidal, antitumor, and immune remodeling activities into a single OMV platform, our strategy constitutes a viable therapeutic approach for Fn-associated CRC.

title: Efficacy Augmentation of Ferroptosis-Inducing Nanomedicine for Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor-Resistant Lung Cancer Brain Metastasis.
abstract: Acquired resistance to epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) poses a major clinical challenge for EGFR-mutant non-small-cell lung cancer patients with brain metastasis. A key unresolved question is whether the adaptive mechanisms driving TKI resistance also confer new therapeutic vulnerabilities. Here, we reveal that TKI-resistant lung cancer brain metastatic cells develop a redox perturbation state, characterized by elevated oxidative stress and diminished antioxidant capacity, which confers a latent sensitivity to ferroptosis induction. To exploit this vulnerability, we developed MIL-S@M, a brain-targeted nanoplatform capable of efficient blood-brain barrier penetration and glutathione-responsive drug release. MIL-S@M potently induces ferroptosis through the synergistic effects of iron overload, glutathione depletion, and glutathione peroxidase 4 inactivation. In mouse models of osimertinib-resistant brain metastasis, MIL-S@M significantly suppressed tumor growth and extended survival, both as a monotherapy and in combination with osimertinib, without inducing systemic or neurotoxic effects. This work unveils a targetable adaptation in TKI-resistant brain metastasis and presents a translatable nanotherapeutic strategy.

title: Membrane-Anchored Dual-Targeting Aptamer Engagers for Programmable T Cell Redirection in Solid and Hematological Cancers.
abstract: Inefficient immune synapse formation limits the therapeutic efficacy of T cell-based immunotherapy in both solid tumors and hematological malignancies. Here, we report a fully synthetic, membrane-anchored dual-targeting aptamer engager, AptE 2, that acts as a programmable artificial immunological interface to redirect cytotoxic T cells toward cancer cells without genetic engineering. Constructed entirely from DNA aptamers through optimized bioorthogonal conjugation and enzyme-mediated ligation, AptE 2 integrates multivalent tumor recognition, T cell binding, enhanced nuclease resistance, and prolonged membrane anchoring within a single modular scaffold. In colorectal cancer models, AptE 2 promoted stable T cell-tumor cell engagement, enhanced cytotoxicity and cytokine secretion, and drove pronounced tumor regression with increased intratumoral CD8+ T cell infiltration and minimal systemic toxicity. Importantly, AptE 2 also demonstrated broad applicability in leukemia. In CCRF-CEM cells, AptE 2 exhibited strong surface binding, sustained membrane retention for up to 6 h, and superior resistance to wash-off compared with monovalent aptamers and bivalent controls. AptE 2-prearmed TALL-104 cells markedly enhanced leukemia cell clustering, increased cell lysis to over 90% under optimized coculture conditions, and amplified IFN-γ secretion. In a disseminated CCRF-CEM-Luc leukemia mouse model, AptE 2-mediated T cell therapy suppressed systemic leukemia progression, improved peripheral hematological profiles, and showed favorable tolerability without detectable major organ injury. These findings establish AptE 2 as a generalizable, nonprotein-based and nonviral immune engager platform for programmable T cell redirection across both solid and hematological cancers.

title: Central retinal artery occlusion preceding hemispheric ischemic stroke treated with mechanical thrombectomy: A case report.
abstract: RATIONALE: Central retinal artery occlusion (CRAO) is a form of ischemic stroke that may signal underlying cerebrovascular or cardiac disease. PATIENT CONCERNS: A 52-year-old man developed sudden, painless vision loss in the right eye. Nine days later, he presented with left-sided weakness and speech difficulty, with a National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score of 8. His medical history included dilated cardiomyopathy, and electrocardiography revealed atrial fibrillation. DIAGNOSES: Ophthalmologic examination and fluorescein angiography supported right CRAO. Computed tomography (CT) angiography at neurological presentation showed right internal carotid artery occlusion from its origin. CT perfusion demonstrated estimated infarct core and penumbral volumes of 37 and 186 mL, respectively. INTERVENTIONS: Emergency mechanical thrombectomy with aspiration and adjunctive balloon angioplasty achieved expanded Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction grade 2c reperfusion. OUTCOMES: The NIHSS score improved to 2 at discharge, 7 days after admission. At 3 months, the modified Rankin Scale score was 1, although right-eye visual loss persisted. LESSONS: CRAO warrants prompt cerebrovascular and cardiac evaluation, with reassessment when new neurological deficits develop. The nine-day interval between retinal symptoms and thrombectomy does not establish the duration of carotid occlusion or cerebral ischemia. The favorable individual outcome does not establish the efficacy of thrombectomy beyond 24 hours.

title: Genetic Polymorphisms in Rheumatoid Arthritis: From GWAS-Identified Loci to Functional, Biomarker, and Pharmacogenomic Insights.
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease with a complex, multifactorial aetiology, in which both environmental factors and genetic predisposition play a significant role. This narrative review summarises the genetic polymorphisms associated with RA that have been identified by genome-wide association studies (GWAS). Its aim is to synthesise the loci and single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) reported to date, to relate them to the immunological mechanisms through which they are thought to act, and to assess their emerging diagnostic, prognostic, and pharmacogenomic applications. Its scope covers large-scale GWAS and multi-ancestry meta-analyses together with the candidate-gene, functional, and pharmacogenomic studies required for their interpretation. Three principal conclusions emerge from the literature reviewed. First, the genetic architecture of RA remains dominated by the HLA-DRB1 shared epitope, which is associated primarily with seropositive, anti-citrullinated protein antibody-positive disease, whereas the numerous non-HLA loci identified to date each confer only a modest individual effect. Second, these non-HLA variants converge on a limited number of biological processes-the activation thresholds of T and B lymphocytes, NF-κB and JAK-STAT cytokine signalling, and the invasive behaviour of fibroblast-like synoviocytes-so that their value lies less in the prediction of risk by individual variants than in identifying pathways amenable to therapeutic targeting. Third, the most readily translatable findings are pharmacogenomic. Variants affecting adenosine signalling and nucleotide metabolism modulate the response to methotrexate. Several polymorphisms predict the response to TNFα inhibitors. Polygenic risk scores are beginning to support the differential diagnosis of early inflammatory arthritis. Progress remains constrained by the over-representation of European-ancestry cohorts, by the difficulty of moving from an associated locus to a causal variant and its target gene, and by the limited replication of pharmacogenomic associations. Integration of genomic with transcriptomic, epigenomic, proteomic, and metabolomic data, supported by machine learning approaches, is therefore required before genotype-guided management of RA can enter routine clinical practice.

title: Acute Cervical Carotid Management During Thrombectomy for Tandem Occlusion: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: The optimal cervical carotid strategy during thrombectomy for anterior-circulation tandem occlusion remains uncertain. We compared emergent carotid stenting, balloon angioplasty alone, and no targeted acute cervical revascularization. METHODS: We searched PubMed, Ovid Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, Web of Science, and Scopus for comparative studies published from January 2015 to 25 August 2026. A frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis estimated odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs), with outcome-specific cohort-overlap auditing. The event-count network was exploratory; adjusted evidence was analyzed separately. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 or ROBINS-I-aligned domains; confidence was assessed with CINeMA. PROSPERO registration: CRD420261494924. RESULTS: The review included 60 reports representing 49 cohort or report families. Fifteen cohorts contributed 1556 patients for functional independence and 15 contributed 1676 for symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH). Stenting was associated with greater 90-day functional independence than angioplasty alone (OR, 1.73; 95% CI, 1.22-2.45), without a detected difference in sICH (OR, 1.01; 95% CI, 0.60-1.67). All leave-one-cohort-out functional estimates remained above 1, with 95% CIs excluding 1. Evidence was predominantly nonrandomized. CONCLUSIONS: Emergent carotid stenting was associated with greater 90-day functional independence than balloon angioplasty alone, with no detected difference in sICH. Serious or critical risk of bias in all studies in the strict network limits causal interpretation. Imprecision and heterogeneous antiplatelet protocols preclude establishing noninferiority or excluding increased hemorrhagic risk.

title: Bivalent CD47 Immunotoxin for Targeted Therapy of Lung Cancer.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related death in the world, with ~2.5 million people diagnosed and ~1.5 million deaths each year. While the last two decades have yielded substantial progress, with systemic targeted and immune therapies improving treatment responses in subgroups of patients with advanced and refractory lung cancer, there is still a dire unmet clinical need to develop more effective therapies with durable responses. CD47 receptors are overexpressed on the surface of a variety of malignant tumor cells, including lung cancer. Although there has been increasing interest in developing targeting antibodies against CD47 for immunotherapy, they failed clinical trials due to their dose-limiting toxicities, primarily hematopoietic toxicity. Methods: Recently, using a unique diphtheria toxin-resistant Pichia pastoris yeast expression system, we developed a diphtheria toxin-based bivalent CD47 immunotoxin (bi-CD47-IT) for targeted therapy of CD47+ cancers. In this study, we extended application of the targeted therapy bi-CD47-IT to a solid tumor, specifically lung cancer. Results: Bi-CD47-IT demonstrated compelling preclinical efficacy in multiple non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) cell line-derived xenograft (CDX) and patient-derived xenograft (PDX) mouse models, including subcutaneous, orthotopic, metastatic, and humanized models. Conclusions: This study demonstrates the remarkable preclinical activity of bi-CD47-IT against various lung cancer models, making bi-CD47-IT a novel and promising therapeutic approach for NSCLC.

title: Real-World Renal Effects of Dapagliflozin in Bulgarian Patients with Chronic Kidney Disease of Predominantly Glomerular Origin: A Two-Year Comparative Cohort Study with Historical Controls.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors are established in the treatment of chronic kidney disease (CKD), but evidence in CKD caused by glomerular disease is limited, and patients on intensified immunosuppression have been excluded from the randomised trials. We examined the effect of dapagliflozin on proteinuria and kidney function over two years in such a population. Methods: In this single-centre retrospective cohort study, we compared 147 patients treated with dapagliflozin 10 mg daily between 2021 and 2025 with 170 historical controls followed between 2014 and 2021; most had biopsy-proven glomerular diseases. Proteinuria and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) were assessed at months 0, 12 and 24, and comparisons used analysis of covariance adjusted for baseline. Subgroups on intensified immunosuppression at entry were prespecified. Results: Proteinuria fell by 51.9% under dapagliflozin and by 22.2% in the historical cohort; the adjusted geometric mean ratio (GMR) was 0.684 (95% CI 0.534-0.878; p = 0.003). During the second year, eGFR declined more slowly with dapagliflozin (a difference of 4.61 mL/min/1.73 m2 per year; 95% CI 1.82-7.41; p = 0.001), although eGFR at month 24 did not differ significantly after adjustment for baseline (p = 0.15). An eGFR below 15 mL/min/1.73 m2 was reached by 0.7% of treated patients and by 11.8% of controls. Among patients on intensified immunosuppression, proteinuria fell by 67.5% when dapagliflozin was added, compared with 4.6% on the same treatment alone (adjusted GMR 0.371; 95% CI 0.234-0.586; p < 0.001). Conclusions: Dapagliflozin was associated with a progressive antiproteinuric effect, most marked in patients on intensified immunosuppression, and with a slower decline in kidney function during the second year. Because this study was observational, the true effects are likely to be smaller than those observed.

title: Prediction of Pathological Complete Response to Neoadjuvant Immunotherapy-Based Regimens for Non-Metastatic Colon and Rectal Cancer.
abstract: Background: Pathological complete response (pCR) after neoadjuvant immunotherapy is associated with improved prognosis in colon and rectal cancer. This study aimed to develop and validate a predictive nomogram for pCR in CRC patients receiving neoadjuvant immunotherapy. Methods: A total of 232 eligible CRC patients who received immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) followed by surgical resection at the Sixth Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-sen University (January 2018-December 2024) were retrospectively included, with 162 in the training set and 70 in the validation set. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors influencing pCR, and a nomogram was subsequently developed. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA) were used to evaluate the discrimination, calibration and clinical value of the nomogram. Results: The pCR rate in the entire cohort was 53.4%, with rates of 76.8% (73/95) and 37.2% (51/137) in the MSI-H/dMMR and MSS/pMMR subgroups, respectively. In multivariable analysis, MSI-H/dMMR status and pretreatment CEA level < 5 ng/mL were independent predictors of pCR and were used to construct the nomogram. The nomogram achieved AUCs of 0.741 in the training set and 0.730 in the validation set. Calibration curve analysis showed good agreement between predicted and actual pCR in both sets, and decision curve analysis demonstrated favorable net benefit. Conclusions: Our nomogram may predict pCR and help identify likely responders to neoadjuvant immunotherapy-based regimens in non-metastatic CRC patients. Prospective multi-center validation is warranted to confirm its clinical utility.

title: Diabetes-Associated Fibrin Enrichment in Cerebral Thrombi and Its Procedural Implications for Mechanical Thrombectomy.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Diabetes is associated with altered fibrin biology, but its relationship with fibrin content in cerebral thrombi and the procedural relevance of this relationship during mechanical thrombectomy remain unclear. We investigated the association between diabetes and fibrin content in thrombectomy-retrieved cerebral thrombi and whether diabetes-associated differences in fibrin content mediated procedural outcomes of mechanical thrombectomy. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed patients with acute ischemic stroke who underwent mechanical thrombectomy and had retrieved thrombi available for histological analysis. Red blood cell, platelet, and fibrin contents were quantified immunohistochemically. The association between diabetes and fibrin content was evaluated using multivariable linear regression, with complementary sensitivity analyses based on intravenous tissue-type plasminogen activator administration and atrial fibrillation status. Mediation analyses were performed to estimate the indirect effects of diabetes on procedural outcomes through diabetes-associated changes in fibrin content. Results: Among 312 patients, 98 (31.4%) had diabetes. Patients with diabetes had greater fibrin content than those without diabetes (median, 37.0% [interquartile range, 26.4-52.9] vs. 30.9% [17.7-45.0]; p = 0.004), whereas red blood cell and platelet contents did not differ significantly between the groups. Diabetes remained associated with greater fibrin content in the primary adjusted analysis (β = +6.68 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.19-11.18; p = 0.004), and the association persisted after additional conditioning on initial glucose and in sensitivity analyses. Among patients with diabetes, neither HbA1c nor initial glucose was associated with fibrin content. Mediation analyses did not identify a detectable indirect effect of diabetes through fibrin content on successful reperfusion, complete reperfusion, first-pass effect, number of passes, or the requirement for ≥3 passes. Conclusions: Diabetes was independently associated with greater fibrin content in cerebral thrombi retrieved during mechanical thrombectomy, supporting the presence of a diabetes-associated fibrin-enriched thrombus phenotype. However, no detectable indirect effect of diabetes-associated differences in fibrin content on the examined procedural outcomes of mechanical thrombectomy was identified. These findings suggest that although diabetes is associated with a distinct quantitative change in cerebral thrombus composition, a corresponding procedural consequence was not detectable in the present study.

title: Disease Knowledge Assessed by RAKE-T and Its Sociodemographic and Clinical Correlates in Patients with Rheumatoid Arthritis Receiving Biologic and Targeted Synthetic DMARDs: A Multicenter Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Disease-related knowledge is important in rheumatoid arthritis (RA), particularly for patients receiving biologic (bDMARD) or targeted synthetic (tsDMARD) disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs. This study aimed to assess disease knowledge using the Turkish version of the Rheumatoid Arthritis Knowledge Assessment Questionnaire (RAKE-T) in patients receiving bDMARD/tsDMARD therapy and to investigate its sociodemographic and clinical correlates. Methods: This multicenter cross-sectional study included 230 patients with RA receiving bDMARD/tsDMARD therapy at four rheumatology centers. Sociodemographic and clinical characteristics were recorded, and disease knowledge was assessed using the 45-item RAKE-T. Linear or robust regression analyses, as appropriate, were used to evaluate factors associated with total and domain-specific scores, except for the single-item comorbidity domain, which was analyzed using binary logistic regression. Results: The mean total RAKE-T score was 61.77 ± 19.00. Older age was associated with lower total RAKE-T and disease knowledge domain scores (p = 0.033 for both). University education or higher was associated with higher total RAKE-T scores (β = 14.503, p < 0.001) and higher scores in the disease knowledge, pharmacological treatments, non-pharmacological treatments, and adaptive skills domains. Place of residence was associated with disease knowledge, self-care, and adaptive skills scores. Disease duration, duration of biologic therapy, sex, marital status, and previous biologic agent use were not significantly associated with total or domain-specific RAKE-T scores. Conclusions: Among patients with RA receiving bDMARD/tsDMARD therapy, disease knowledge was associated with age, educational level, and place of residence, whereas no statistically significant associations were observed with disease duration or duration of biologic therapy. These findings suggest that longer disease or treatment experience should not be assumed to correspond to greater disease knowledge and support periodic reassessment of educational needs and individually tailored patient education.

title: The NLRP3 Inflammasome Across the AKI-AKD-CKD Continuum: Mitochondrial, Epigenetic and Endocrine-Metabolic Regulation.
abstract: The NLRP3 inflammasome has emerged as a potential molecular link between cellular stress, sterile inflammation, and progressive kidney damage. This review critically examines canonical, non-canonical, and mitochondrial mechanisms of NLRP3 regulation across the acute kidney injury (AKI)-acute kidney disease (AKD)-chronic kidney disease (CKD) continuum, integrating their relationships with pyroptosis, maladaptive repair, fibrosis, and epigenetic regulation. Particular attention is given to endocrine-metabolic signals that may shape renal inflammasome activity. Hyperglycemia, advanced glycation end products, mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, TXNIP signaling, lipotoxicity, impaired tubular fatty-acid oxidation, podocyte insulin resistance, obesity-related adipokine imbalance, and aldosterone-mineralocorticoid receptor activation may converge on NLRP3. Conversely, inflammasome-dependent cytokine release and pyroptosis may amplify insulin resistance, metabolic dysfunction, and cardiorenal injury, establishing a bidirectional endocrine-renal inflammatory loop. Importantly, increased NLRP3 mRNA or protein abundance is distinguished from functional inflammasome activation, which is more strongly supported by downstream evidence such as ASC recruitment/oligomerization, caspase-1 activation, mature IL-1β/IL-18 production, GSDMD cleavage, or pyroptotic cell death. A central issue is whether NLRP3 is a causal driver of kidney disease or a marker of ongoing tissue injury. Although genetic and pharmacological studies support a pathogenic role in experimental models, clinical evidence remains largely associative and disease-dependent. NLRP3-related signals should therefore be regarded as candidate, rather than validated, biomarkers. SGLT2 inhibitors, GLP-1 receptor agonists and finerenone may indirectly attenuate NLRP3 signaling, but mechanistic mediation of their clinical benefits remains unproven. Defining cell-specific activation and clinical target engagement will be essential to establish NLRP3 as a biomarker and therapeutic target.

title: HDL Remodeling in Severe Bacterial Infection in Children: A Potential Biomarker for Diagnosis and Therapeutic Monitoring.
abstract: Many pediatric patients with severe bacterial infection (SBI) present with a compromised general clinical picture. Early identification of the infectious and inflammatory state can improve clinical outcomes. Although microbiological culture remains the gold standard for diagnosis, its delayed results highlight the need for early biomarkers to improve clinical decision-making and patient outcomes. During infection, the acute phase response alters lipid metabolism, compromising cholesterol efflux. In this study, we characterized the serum lipid profile and HDL subclasses in 63 children with SBI at hospital admission (T0) and discharge (T1), comparing them with 63 age- and sex-matched healthy subjects. At T0, we found a significant reduction in serum total cholesterol, LDL cholesterol, and HDL cholesterol in subjects with SBI compared to controls. Interestingly, at a cut-off value of 41.5 mg/dL, HDL cholesterol discriminated the two groups with a sensitivity of 76% and a specificity of 86% for SBI. At T1, total and LDL cholesterol increased, while HDL cholesterol remained unchanged. Moreover, we observed at T1 a clear remodeling of HDL classes, with a significant decrease in large HDL with pro-inflammatory activity and an increase in the intermediate and small HDL with anti-inflammatory activity, compared to time T0. This study proposes serum HDL cholesterol as a candidate biomarker and highlights the role of HDL cholesterol and its classes in inflammatory and immune regulation in systemic bacterial infection, potentially identifying patients who could benefit from HDL-based therapies.

title: Genetic Risk Architecture of Late-Onset Alzheimer's Disease: Mapping Single-Nucleotide Polymorphisms to Disease-Defining Molecular Pathways.
abstract: Late-onset Alzheimer's disease (LOAD) is increasingly recognized as a complex, multifactorial disorder driven by the convergence of genetic susceptibility and interconnected molecular pathways, rather than a single linear pathogenic cascade. In this review, we integrate evidence from genome-wide association studies, sequencing analyses, and experimental research to map disease-associated single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) onto key biological processes underlying LOAD pathogenesis. Converging data consistently implicate a limited number of core domains, including amyloid-β metabolism, tau pathology, neuroinflammation, lipid homeostasis, endosomal-lysosomal trafficking, mitochondrial dysfunction, and synaptic impairment. Importantly, genetic risk variants are not randomly distributed, but cluster within these pathways, exerting coordinated effects across multiple biological systems and supporting a network-based organization of disease. We further examine how these pathways interact at a systems level, highlighting key interfaces such as the amyloid-tau, lipid-immune, inflammation-proteostasis, and mitochondria-synaptic dysfunction axes. These interconnected processes form self-reinforcing feedback loops that amplify neurodegeneration and contribute to disease progression. From a translational perspective, this integrated framework provides a mechanistic basis for the limited efficacy of single-target therapies and supports the development of multi-target and pathway-oriented strategies, as well as precision medicine approaches based on genetic and biomarker integration. Collectively, this review supports a unified model of LOAD as a polygenic network disorder and underscores the importance of pathway convergence in understanding disease heterogeneity and guiding future therapeutic development.

title: Cardiorenal Syndrome: Pathophysiology, Management, and the Challenge of Therapeutic Inertia.
abstract: Cardiorenal syndrome describes the clinical consequences of the bidirectional influence that cardiac and renal dysfunction exert on each other-a domain in which single-organ care proves insufficient. A 2024 meta-analysis estimated the pooled prevalence of chronic kidney disease among patients with heart failure at 49%. Across individual cohorts, this figure ranges between 30% and 60%, with the spread reflecting the population studied and the threshold used to define kidney disease. Among acute heart failure admissions, 64% of cases have an estimated glomerular filtration rate below 60 mL/min/1.73 m2, and mortality reaches 7.6% once it falls into the severe range (15-29 mL/min/1.73 m2). The same can be described in the other "direction": congestive heart failure is reported in 28% of adults aged 66 years or older with chronic kidney disease, compared to 6% of those without. The Acute Dialysis Quality Initiative distinguishes a five-subtype framework by direction and chronicity of organ injury, and each subtype shows characteristic prescribing failure patterns. In types 1 and 2, the dominant problem is premature de-escalation of neurohormonal therapy at the first creatinine rise. In type 4, the failure is upstream in the cascade: cardiovascular surveillance lags behind the increasing rate of chronic kidney disease. Randomized trials over the past decade have expanded the therapeutic options. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors showed cardiorenal benefit across every ejection fraction studied and at estimated glomerular filtration rate values down to 20 mL/min/1.73 m2. These findings have expanded treatment eligibility to patients with advanced CKD. The FINE-HEART pooled analysis of finerenone suggested a nominal reduction in all-cause mortality, alongside fewer heart failure hospitalizations and improvement in the kidney composite outcome. In the FLOW trial, semaglutide showed a reduction in the composite of major kidney events and cardiovascular death in diabetic adults with chronic kidney disease. In this cohort, the estimated glomerular filtration rate slope was slower in the active arm and secondary outcomes showed reductions in major adverse cardiovascular events and in all-cause mortality. However, observational registries show that these classes of drugs are less used in patients with the highest baseline risk, with advancing renal disease identified as an independent predictor of under-prescription. Therapeutic inertia in this setting reflects determinants at the patient, clinician, and system levels, which is compounded because each prescribing decision must be justified for both the heart and the kidney. The primary objective of the present narrative review is the therapeutic inertia that separates this evidence from routine prescribing: the sections on pathophysiology, imaging and biomarker tools, and subtype-specific pharmacotherapy supply the clinical rationale, and the closing sections cover the implementation strategies and the multidisciplinary framework required to act on the trial findings.

title: Vascular Access Complexity and Thrombectomy Efficiency in Proximal MCA M1 Occlusion: Evaluation of the Bovine Aortic Arch-Dolichoarteriopathy Score.
abstract: Background and Objectives: In this study, it was aimed to investigate the relationship between the Bovine Aortic Arch-Dolichoarteriopathy (B.A.D.) score and the procedural characteristics of mechanical thrombectomy, recanalization success, and 90-day functional outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke with proximal M1 occlusion of the middle cerebral artery (MCA). Materials and Methods: A total of 220 adult patients who underwent mechanical thrombectomy for proximal MCA M1 occlusion were included in this retrospective, single-center cohort study. The patients were divided into good B.A.D. (<2; n = 143) and poor B.A.D. (≥2; n = 77) groups. Admission National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) and Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score (ASPECTS) scores, collateral status, thrombectomy time intervals, number of passes, first-pass effect (FPE), and Modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction (mTICI) recanalization grades were evaluated. The primary outcome was functional independence at day 90 (mRS 0-2). Associations with procedural and clinical outcomes were evaluated using multivariable logistic and linear regression analyses. Results: The puncture-to-recanalization time was significantly longer in the poor B.A.D. group [67 (50.5-88.0) min vs. 43 (32.0-65.0) min, p < 0.001], and the FPE rate was lower (37.7% vs. 51.7%, p = 0.046). After adjustment for thrombectomy technique and clinical covariates, poor B.A.D. remained independently associated with lower odds of FPE success (aOR = 0.439, 95% CI: 0.229-0.839; p = 0.013). In the procedurally adjusted linear regression model, poor B.A.D. also remained independently associated with longer puncture-to-recanalization time after additional adjustment for the number of thrombectomy passes and thrombectomy technique (B = 0.294, 95% CI: 0.188-0.400; p < 0.001). Final mTICI ≥ 2b, ≥2c, and 3 recanalization rates did not differ between the groups. Although 90-day functional independence was lower in the poor B.A.D. group, the difference was not significant (51.9% vs. 63.6%, p = 0.092), and no statistically significant independent association between B.A.D. status and 90-day functional independence was observed in the multivariable analysis. Conclusions: Poor B.A.D. anatomy was associated with greater procedural complexity during mechanical thrombectomy for proximal MCA M1 occlusion, including longer puncture-to-recanalization time and lower odds of FPE success, even after adjustment for available procedural and clinical factors. However, no statistically significant independent association was demonstrated between B.A.D. status and 90-day functional independence, and final recanalization rates did not differ significantly between the groups. These findings suggest that the B.A.D. score may have potential value as a preprocedural marker of vascular access complexity; however, prospective external validation is required before its use for procedural planning can be recommended.

title: Frailty Phenotype Among Older Adults Receiving SGLT-2 Inhibitors in a CKD-Predominant Population: A Prospective Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: Background and Objectives: Frailty is a multisystem clinical syndrome characterized by reduced physiological reserve and increased vulnerability to adverse health outcomes. It is particularly relevant in older adults with chronic conditions such as chronic kidney disease (CKD). This study aimed to determine the prevalence of frailty and pre-frailty among older adults receiving sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT-2) inhibitor therapy in a CKD-predominant population and to evaluate clinical, anthropometric, and laboratory factors associated with frailty status. Materials and Methods: This prospective, cross-sectional study included patients aged ≥60 years receiving SGLT-2 inhibitor therapy for at least one month who underwent frailty assessment during a routine outpatient visit. Frailty status was assessed using a prespecified, modified Fried Physical Frailty Phenotype. Anthropometric and physical performance measurements were obtained using a standardized protocol by the same nephrologist. Results: A total of 163 adults aged ≥60 years receiving SGLT-2 inhibitor therapy were included in this CKD-predominant cohort. Frailty and pre-frailty were identified in 26.4% (95% CI 20.2-33.6%) and 46.0% (95% CI 38.5-53.7%) of participants, respectively. In multivariable logistic regression analysis, higher BMI (aOR 1.12, 95% CI 1.03-1.22; p = 0.010) and higher CCI scores (aOR 1.42, 95% CI 1.12-1.81; p = 0.004) were independently associated with higher odds of non-robust status, whereas higher hemoglobin levels were associated with lower odds (aOR 0.72, 95% CI 0.57-0.91; p = 0.007). Conclusions: Frailty and pre-frailty were common among older adults receiving SGLT-2 inhibitor therapy in this CKD-predominant population. Higher BMI and greater comorbidity burden were independently associated with higher odds of non-robust status, whereas higher hemoglobin levels were associated with lower odds. Frailty assessment may provide complementary information regarding physical reserve and vulnerability in this population rather than serving as a tool for determining eligibility for SGLT-2 inhibitor therapy. Given the study design and absence of a comparator group, no treatment-specific conclusions regarding SGLT-2 inhibitor therapy and frailty can be drawn.

title: Cardiovascular Risk Assessment in Childhood: Focus on Family History and Lifestyle Habits in the Real-World, Cross-Sectional, Community-Based RISCAPED Study.
abstract: Background and Objectives: Pediatric cardiovascular risk factors tend to track into adulthood, accelerating the atherosclerotic process. This study aimed to assess the prevalence of cardiometabolic risk factors, integrating anthropometric parameters, central adiposity indices, early growth trajectories, family history, and household lifestyle, in a primary-care pediatric cohort (the RISCAPED study). Materials and Methods: A cross-sectional multicenter study was conducted across primary care pediatric practices in the province of Alessandria, Northwest Italy, enrolling children aged 6 to 12 years. Weight status was classified according to World Health Organization 2007 criteria, abdominal adiposity by Waist-to-Height Ratio (WHtR > 0.5), and high blood pressure according to American Academy of Pediatrics percentiles (≥95th percentile). Family lifestyle habits were evaluated via the Family Nutrition and Physical Activity (FNPA) screening tool. Factors independently associated with high blood pressure and excess weight were identified using multivariable logistic regression models. Results: Among 479 children with complete anthropometric data (median age: 9.0 years), 42.3% presented with excess weight (21.9% overweight, 20.4% obesity). WHtR increased significantly across weight groups (median 0.44, 0.46 and 0.50, respectively; p < 0.001). Previously undiagnosed high blood pressurewas identified in 7.1% of the cohort, with a significant systolic blood pressure gradient (p < 0.001). Rapid weight gain during early infancy was significantly more frequent in children with obesity (10.6% vs. <5.3%, p = 0.025). In multivariable models, a family history of thrombophilic disorders (OR 3.16, 95% CI 1.27-7.41) and a less favourable FNPA score (OR 0.94 per point, 0.89-0.99) were independently associated with high blood pressure; a family history of hyperglycemia was associated overweight/obesity (OR 1.71, 1.06-2.78), and a family history of obesity wa associated with childhood obesity (OR 1.71, 1.02-2.88). Conclusions: Cardiovascular risk factors emerge early during primary school age, with central adiposity and silent high blood pressure manifesting prior to clinical disease. Multi-generational family history emerged as a consistent marker of risk, supporting routine multi-domain cardiovascular screening in primary pediatric healthcare.

title: Effects of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter Type 2 Inhibitors on Residual Kidney Function in Patients Undergoing Incremental Hemodialysis: A Two-Center, Retrospective, Exploratory Cohort Study.
abstract: Background and Objectives: The preservation of residual kidney function (RKF) is a major determinant of outcome in patients undergoing incremental hemodialysis (iHD). While sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT-2) inhibitors have established nephroprotective benefits in non-dialysis chronic kidney disease (CKD), evidence regarding their role in preserving RKF after the initiation of hemodialysis remains limited. The primary objective of this study was to explore the impact of SGLT-2 inhibitors on the preservation of RKF in incident patients undergoing iHD over a 12-month follow-up. Materials and Methods: This study involved a two-center retrospective exploratory observational longitudinal study over 12 months of follow-up, including 32 incident iHD patients (one or two sessions per week, 1WHD or 2WHD). Participants were divided into a study group (SGLT-2iG, n = 15) receiving SGLT-2 inhibitors and a control group (non-SGLT-2iG, n = 17). RKF parameters, including 24 h (h) urine output (UO), urea clearance (KrU), and creatinine clearance (CrCl), were monitored quarterly. Results: Over 12 months, 24 h UO increased significantly within the SGLT-2iG (+573.3 mL; p < 0.001) and did not change significantly within controls (-202.9 mL, p = 0.34). KrU and CrCl showed only non-significant within-group trends (upward in the SGLT-2iG, downward in controls). Between-group differences were not formally tested and are described descriptively. A total of 80% of patients in SGLT-2iG maintained a 1WHD regimen at 12 months, compared with 46.7% in the non-SGLT-2iG. Safety was favorable, with no cases of ketoacidosis or severe infections and a trend toward fewer cardiovascular events in the SGLT-2iG (6.7% vs. 35.3%). Conclusions: In this two-center, real-world cohort, SGLT-2 inhibitor use in incident iHD patients was associated with a within-group increase in 24 h UO and non-significant trends toward preservation of KrU and CrCl over 12 months, together with an apparently favorable safety profile. Given the observational design and small sample, these hypothesis-generating findings should be interpreted with caution and warrant confirmation in dedicated randomized controlled trials.

title: HDL-C Levels Are Associated with Clinical Outcomes and Hospital Mortality in Critically Ill Patients with Sepsis: A Prospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Background and Objectives: Metabolic perturbations frequently occur during the acute phase of critical illness and may disrupt lipid homeostasis. Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is a severe condition and is associated with high mortality in critically ill patients with sepsis. This study aimed to evaluate the association between conventional plasma lipid parameters and clinical outcomes in critically ill sepsis patients. Materials and Methods: We conducted a prospective observational cohort study of critically ill sepsis patients in Taiwan between October 2020 and July 2025. Conventional plasma lipid parameters and clinical variables were measured at intensive care unit admission. Clinical outcomes were compared between patients stratified by plasma HDL-C levels. Results: A total of 285 critically ill patients with sepsis were included. Pneumonia was the presumed source of infection in 91% of patients, and 78% met the criteria for ARDS. The overall hospital mortality rate was 37.9%. Patients with ARDS had significantly higher C-reactive protein (CRP) and interleukin-6 (IL-6) levels, higher risk of organ failure (i.e., APACHE II and SOFA scores), and lower plasma HDL-C levels (all p < 0.05). Non-survivors exhibited significantly greater organ failure severity and lower HDL-C levels compared with survivors (all p < 0.05). Patients with low HDL-C (≤17.5 mg/dL; n = 106, 37.2%) had significantly higher CRP and IL-6, greater organ failure severity, and increased 28-, 60-, 90-day, and hospital mortality, compared with those with high HDL-C (> 17.5 mg/dL; n = 179, 62.8%) (all p < 0.05). In multivariable analyses, lower HDL-C were independently associated with hospital mortality. Conclusions: Lower HDL-C levels were associated with hospital mortality in critically ill patients with sepsis, most of whom had pneumonia and concomitant ARDS. These findings suggest that HDL-C may have prognostic value in this selected critically ill population, although external validation in broader sepsis populations is warranted. An easily accessible and useful for early risk stratification.

title: The Interplay Between Oophorectomy and Alzheimer's Disease: A Narrative Review.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the leading cause of dementia worldwide and affects women more frequently than men. Although age remains the main risk factor, reproductive aging and changes in ovarian hormone exposure may also contribute to this difference. Premenopausal bilateral oophorectomy causes an abrupt loss of ovarian hormones, including estradiol, progesterone, and testosterone, and several observational studies have associated this change with a higher risk of later cognitive impairment or dementia, particularly when surgery is performed at a younger age. However, these studies have assessed different outcomes, including dementia, mild cognitive impairment, subjective cognitive changes, and AD-related imaging findings, and current evidence does not establish a direct causal relationship between oophorectomy and AD. Possible biological pathways include neuroinflammation, synaptic dysfunction, amyloid-β and tau-related changes, and cerebrovascular dysfunction, although much of the mechanistic evidence remains experimental or indirect. Genetic background, vascular health, age at surgery, and the duration of hormone deprivation may further influence individual risk. Hormone replacement therapy has an established role in the management of premature or early surgical menopause when there is no contraindication, but its effect on long-term AD prevention remains uncertain; the timing of treatment may be important, but current evidence does not confirm a preventive effect. This review summarizes current epidemiological, neuroimaging, and experimental evidence linking oophorectomy with cognitive health and AD, and discusses hormone therapy, pharmacological and non-pharmacological management, emerging research approaches, and remaining knowledge gaps. Future studies with detailed information on surgical timing, hormone exposure, genetic risk, vascular factors, longitudinal cognition, and AD-related biomarkers are needed to better define which women may be most vulnerable after premenopausal oophorectomy.

title: Impact of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists on Cognitive Performance in Adults at Risk of Alzheimer's Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Type 2 diabetes, a widely recognized risk factor of Alzheimer's disease (AD), is mainly due to the role played by insulin resistance on neuronal degeneration. Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) also significantly increases the risk of developing AD by approximately 40%. Epidemiological studies have demonstrated correlations between glucagon-like peptide-1 agonists (GLP-1RAs) on reducing the risk of AD. We synthesize current data from randomized controlled trials (RCTs) to summarize the effects of GLP-1RA treatment in adults with Type 2 diabetes or with MCI on cognitive performance. Methods: We searched databases from inception to 1 January 2026 investigating effects of GLP-1RA(s) on cognition. PubMed, Web of Science and Scopus databases were explored following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA). We selected only RCTs in adults investigating GLP-1RA(s) on cognitive performance. Results: Overall mean age was 64.5 yrs with an average follow-up period of 28.4 months. A total of 13,711 participants from five RCTs were included. Following a source-data audit, four randomized controlled trials contributed analytically compatible data to at least one cognitive domain. Cognitive domains were analyzed separately using Hedges' g. Random-effects models used restricted maximum likelihood (REML) estimation with Knapp-Hartung inference when at least two compatible studies contributed. For global cognition, three studies yielded g = 0.014 (95% CI: -0.061 to 0.088; p = 0.515; I2 = 0%). For attention, two studies yielded g = 0.072 (95% CI: -2.164 to 2.308; p = 0.753; I2 = 31.1%). For delayed memory, executive function, and verbal function, only one compatible study was available per domain; these were therefore reported as single-study estimates rather than pooled effects. A sensitivity analysis excluding the dominant Cukierman trial yielded an imprecise and non-significant effect estimate for global cognition (g = -0.205, 95% CI: -2.678 to 2.269) indicating that the robustness of the pooled result could not be established. Conclusions: Current randomized evidence is insufficient to establish a consistent beneficial effect of GLP-1RA(s) on cognitive function in adults at risk of AD. The available findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating because few analytically compatible trials were available within each cognitive domain.

title: Changes in Nutrition and Physical Activity up to 4 Years Following a Hypertensive Pregnancy: A Blood Pressure Postpartum Longitudinal Sub-Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Postpartum lifestyle interventions may mitigate increased cardiovascular disease (CVD) risks following hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP). The study aimed to examine longitudinal changes in post-HDP lifestyle behaviors and women's perceptions towards healthy living. METHODS: This study was a longitudinal sub-study of the 3-armed, multicenter Blood Pressure Postpartum (BP2) randomized controlled trial in post-HDP women, comprising different postpartum care/lifestyle intervention strategies 6-12 months postpartum and post-intervention observational follow-up to 3-4 years postpartum. The NSW Health Population Survey captured lifestyle variables 6-12 months postpartum. At 3-4 years post-HDP, the Australian Eating Survey and the International Physical Activity Questionnaire were alternatively used for diet and physical activity, respectively. Linear mixed-effects models analyzed daily consumption of vegetables/fruit, moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA), and perception scores of healthy living for motivators, barriers, and satisfaction. RESULTS: In 180 participants, reported mean (SD) vegetable/fruit daily intake increased (vegetable servings/day: 2.6 (1.3), 6 months vs. 2.7 (1.4), 12 months vs. 4.2 (2.0), 3-4 years, p < 0.001; fruit servings/day: 1.7 (1.0), 6 months vs. 1.7 (1.0), 12 months vs. 2.2 (1.3), 3-4 years, p < 0.001), while accompanied by other unfavorable dietary changes. Reported median [IQR] MVPA increased (minutes/week, 330 [280], 6 months vs. 313 [331], 12 months vs. 515 [690], 3-4 years, p < 0.001). Motivators to engage in healthy behaviors decreased (p < 0.001), perceived barriers increased (p < 0.001), and satisfaction with diet and body appearance worsened over time (p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Overall, women reported higher intake of both health-promoting and less health-promoting foods and higher MVPA; however, different tools were used for lifestyle measurement. Worsening perceptions were observed using the same instrument.

title: Baseline Food Supply-Based Dietary Scores and Ischemic Heart Disease Mortality: A Longitudinal Cross-Country Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives: National food environments may be associated with cardiovascular risk, but how their association with country-level ischemic heart disease (IHD) mortality differs across diet-quality indices remains unclear. We compared six food supply-based dietary scores calculated using 2010 food data in relation to annual IHD mortality from 2010 to 2021. Methods: We conducted a longitudinal study of 148 countries with populations ≥ 1 million. Using 2010 FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheet data, we calculated the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) score, the Alternative Healthy Eating Index (AHEI), Mediterranean Diet Score (MDS), Traditional Japanese Diet Score (TJDS), Planetary Health Diet Index (PHDI), and Quantitative Index for Dietary Diversity (QUANTIDD). The outcome was age-standardized IHD mortality during 2010-2021. Associations between time-invariant baseline dietary scores and annual IHD mortality were assessed using multivariable-adjusted linear mixed-effects models. Effect sizes were expressed as mortality rate ratios (MRRs) per 1-standard deviation (SD) higher score; model fit was compared using Akaike information criterion (AIC) weights and marginal R2, and effect estimates were compared pairwise. Results: Higher DASH and AHEI scores were associated with lower IHD mortality. MRRs per 1-SD higher score were 0.914 (95% confidence interval, 0.849-0.983) for DASH and 0.908 (95% confidence interval, 0.838-0.985) for AHEI. No significant associations were observed for MDS, TJDS, PHDI, or QUANTIDD. DASH had the highest AIC weight (0.434), followed by AHEI (0.341), with a slightly higher marginal R2 for DASH. Pairwise comparisons showed no statistically significant differences in effect estimates between DASH and AHEI or between either of these scores and the other dietary scores. Conclusions: Higher baseline DASH and AHEI scores were associated with lower IHD mortality during 2010-2021, with similar effect estimates per 1-SD higher score and broadly comparable model fit. However, direct pairwise comparisons revealed no statistically significant differences in standardized effect sizes between these scores (DASH and AHEI) and the other dietary scores. These findings suggest that the relevance of dietary scores may depend on the outcome and analytic context rather than the superiority of a single index. Because this was an ecological study, these findings should not be interpreted as individual-level causal effects.

title: Beyond Weight Loss and Glycemic Control: Molecular Mechanisms and Hypothesis-Generating Therapeutic Potential of Incretin-Based Therapies Against Peritoneal Fibrosis in Peritoneal Dialysis.
abstract: Background: Peritoneal dialysis (PD) is an established kidney replacement therapy, but long-term exposure to bioincompatible dialysate, uremic toxins, recurrent peritonitis, glucose degradation products, oxidative stress, and sterile inflammation progressively remodels the peritoneal membrane and contributes to peritoneal fibrosis (PF). This review summarizes the molecular basis of PF in PD and evaluates the therapeutic rationale for incretin-based interventions beyond weight loss and glycemic control. Methods: This narrative review synthesizes mechanistic, translational, and clinically relevant literature on PD-associated PF, with emphasis on DPP-4 biology, GLP-1 receptor agonism, inflammatory and oxidative signaling, angiogenesis, mesothelial-to-mesenchymal transition, glycemic management in PD, and selected author-conducted translational studies interpreted alongside independent evidence. Results: Available evidence supports a model in which DPP-4 activation, altered GLP-1/GLP-1R signaling, TGF-β/Smad3-driven mesothelial transition, NF-κB/MyD88 inflammation, ROS-mediated oxidative stress, angiogenesis, apoptosis, and cytoskeletal remodeling converge to impair peritoneal membrane integrity. DPP-4 inhibition, exendin-4, and dulaglutide attenuated these pathways in experimental models, while GLP-1 receptor agonists have established metabolic benefits in appropriate diabetic and obese populations. Conclusions: Direct clinical evidence that incretin-based therapies prevent or treat peritoneal fibrosis in humans undergoing PD is currently lacking. Therefore, peritoneal membrane protection, reduced ultrafiltration failure, and improved technique survival should be regarded as investigational, hypothesis-generating possibilities that require prospective clinical validation.

title: Population-Specific Pharmacogenetic Variants Associated with Chemotherapy Response in the Bulgarian Population.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Pharmacogenetic variability influences the efficacy and toxicity of anticancer therapies. However, Eastern European populations remain underrepresented in pharmacogenetic databases. This study aimed to characterize pharmacogenetic variants relevant to chemotherapy response in the Bulgarian population and compare their allele frequencies with reference populations. Methods: Ninety individuals were included, comprising 50 patients with colorectal, non-small cell lung, or breast cancer and 40 healthy controls. Genomic DNA and circulating cell-free DNA were analyzed by next-generation sequencing targeting pharmacogenetic genes involved in drug metabolism, transport, and DNA repair. Allele frequencies were compared with gnomAD v2.1.1 reference data. Sensitivity analyses compared Bulgarian controls with Bulgarian non-cancer and combined Southern European, Northwestern European, and Other non-Finnish European non-cancer populations. Results: Twenty-three pharmacogenetic variants were evaluated. Six variants remained statistically significant after Benjamini-Hochberg correction in both Fisher's exact test and the two-proportion Z-test. Five variants-DPYD c.2194G>A, XPC c.2815C>A, EGFR c.1562G>A, XRCC1 c.1196A>G, and ERCC2 c.2251A>C-showed higher allele frequencies, whereas ERCC2 c.934G>A was less frequent in the Bulgarian cohort. DPYD c.85T>C remained significant after correction in the Z-test but not in Fisher's exact test. Sensitivity analyses confirmed the significance of XPC c.2815C>A in both reference-population comparisons, while DPYD c.85T>C remained significant only against the combined European reference population. Conclusions: Several pharmacogenetic variants showed distinct allele frequencies in the Bulgarian cohort. XPC c.2815C>A demonstrated the most robust population-specific pattern across sensitivity analyses. These findings highlight the value of locally derived pharmacogenetic data for precision oncology and pharmacogenetically guided treatment strategies.

title: Selenium Nanoparticles Functionalized with Tumor-Targeting Peptides for Lung Cancer Therapy: A Comprehensive Review.
abstract: Lung cancer is among the most fatal malignancies worldwide, with approximately 85% of diagnosed cases being non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Despite the considerable progress in surgical, chemotherapeutic, radiotherapeutic, and immunological treatments, the prognosis of NSCLC remains poor due to late-stage diagnosis, molecular heterogeneity, treatment resistance, recurrence, and systemic toxicity. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop more effective and less toxic therapies, and cancer nanotechnology has emerged as a promising approach. Selenium nanoparticles (SeNPs) are a viable option for lung cancer treatment because of their unique physicochemical and biochemical properties. They can be used for targeted drug delivery into cancer cells, as selenium possesses inherent anti-cancer properties, such as the induction of reactive oxygen species (ROS), mitochondrial disruption, DNA damage, cell-cycle arrest, and modulation of several signaling pathways, including PI3K/Akt, MAPK, NF-κβ, STAT3, and p53, leading to cancer cell death and repression of tumor progression. Green synthesis of SeNPs using plant-derived phytochemicals is a sustainable strategy as it allows for simultaneous reduction and stabilization of nanoparticles, with an additional therapeutic phytochemical effect against cancer. Various phytochemicals, such as flavonoids, polyphenols, terpenoids, and alkaloids, have the ability to chelate metal ions and act as reducing agents and stabilizers in the synthesis of SeNPs. The antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, anti-proliferative, and anti-metastatic activities of phytochemicals, along with their ability to inhibit the overexpressed enzymes, e.g., matrix metalloproteinases, in cancer cells, could provide an additional therapeutic benefit. However, the application of SeNPs in practice is limited by their low targeting ability, which results in poor bioavailability due to fast clearance from the bloodstream, reduced tumor accumulation, and poor cellular uptake. Conjugation of SeNPs with tumor-targeting peptides could enhance their delivery into the cancer cells. There is a variety of cell surface receptors that are overexpressed in lung cancer cells and can be used for targeted drug delivery. The most common receptors are EGFR, integrins, gastrin-releasing peptide receptor, neuropilin-1, and transferrin receptor. The ligands for these receptors, including the GE11 peptide for EGFR (epidermal growth factor receptor), RGD for integrins, bombesin for GRPR, and iRGD for neuropilin-1, could be used for targeting, as well as cell-penetrating peptides, such as TAT. This review discusses the current knowledge on the application of functionalized SeNPs for lung cancer treatment, specifically synthetic methods, physicochemical properties, mechanisms of action, and targeting strategies. Particular attention is paid to the combination of the anti-cancer effects of selenium and phytochemicals and their synergistic impact on tumor cell death. In addition, the challenges of the application of SeNPs for lung cancer treatment and possible future developments for functionalized SeNPs as novel therapeutic nanocarriers are discussed.

title: SGLT-2 Inhibitors Versus GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Propensity Score-Matched Cohort Study Comparing Adherence and Persistence with Specific Reference to Cardiovascular Disease.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Poor adherence and persistence to sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT-2is) and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are a critical issue in the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), especially in patients with cardiovascular disease (CVD). We aimed to compare adherence and persistence to these drugs in routine care. Methods: A retrospective propensity score-matched (PSM) cohort study was conducted using pharmacy claims data. Patients aged 40 years or older with T2DM initiating SGLT-2is or GLP-1 RAs from 1 January 2019 to 31 December 2024 were included. Adherence was measured using the Medication Possession Ratio (MPR), and persistence was defined as the time to discontinuation (gap ≥ 60 days between refills). Results: At the 1-year follow-up, the SGLT-2i cohort showed significantly higher adherence compared to the GLP-1 RA cohort (86.66% vs. 76.53%; OR = 2.02) and higher persistence (71.48% vs. 66.52% at 12 months; HR = 0.83). The main factors associated with lack of persistency were newly diagnosed T2DM (HR = 1.25) and insulin use (HR = 1.32). In the CVD subgroup, the differences in favor of the SGLT-2i cohort were more pronounced for adherence (89.57% vs. 78.12%; OR = 2.44) and persistence (73.9% vs. 63.59%; HR = 0.66). Conclusions: In real-world clinical practice, adherence and persistence rates were higher in patients on SGLT-2is compared to those on GLP-1 RAs, particularly in the CVD subgroup. Our findings suggest that the new strategies are necessary to improve adherence and persistence to these medications, particularly in patients with CVD.

title: Cryptococcosis After Initiation of Janus Kinase Inhibitors or Biologic DMARDs in Rheumatoid Arthritis: Three Pairwise Active-Comparator Analyses of Propensity Score-Matched TriNetX Cohorts, 2005-2025.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Comparative safety evidence for cryptococcosis during advanced rheumatoid arthritis (RA) therapy is limited. We compared newly recorded cryptococcosis after initiation of Janus kinase inhibitors (JAKi), tumor necrosis factor (TNF) inhibitors (TNFi), and non-TNF biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (non-TNF bDMARDs). Methods: Three retrospective active-comparator analyses were conducted in the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network: JAKi versus TNFi, JAKi versus non-TNF bDMARDs, and TNFi versus non-TNF bDMARDs. After 1:1 propensity score matching, outcomes from day 1 to 10 years after initiation, capped at 30 June 2025, were analyzed using Cox proportional hazards models. E-values assessed sensitivity to unmeasured confounding. Results: Matched cohorts included 27,833, 32,440, and 37,351 patients per group, respectively; all absolute standardized mean differences were <0.10. Events occurred in 20 JAKi and 12 TNFi initiators (hazard ratio [HR], 2.20; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.06-4.54) and in 22 JAKi and 13 non-TNF bDMARD initiators (HR, 2.15; 95% CI, 1.07-4.31). In the secondary comparison, 17 TNFi and 19 non-TNF bDMARD initiators had events (HR, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.43-1.60). Point-estimate E-values for the JAKi comparisons were 3.82 and 3.72; CI-limit E-values were 1.31 and 1.34. Conclusions: JAKi initiation was associated with an approximately twofold higher hazard of newly recorded cryptococcosis than either biologic comparator, while estimated 10-year cumulative event probabilities were below 0.2% in all groups. The separately selected and matched populations do not support an indirect ranking of treatment classes. Low event counts, wide CIs, possible outcome misclassification, fixed exposure classification, and residual confounding preclude causal conclusions. The findings require independent confirmation.

title: Precision Microbiome Interventions in Oncology: From Predictive Biomarkers to Therapeutic Modulation of Immunotherapy Outcomes.
abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed the treatment of multiple malignancies, yet durable clinical responses remain limited to a subset of patients. Accumulating evidence identifies the gut microbiome as a regulator of antitumour immunity that can influence treatment efficacy and toxicity through microbial metabolism, epithelial barrier integrity, inflammatory signalling, and host immune responses. This review critically evaluates the microbiome as both a predictive biomarker and therapeutic target in precision oncology. It moves beyond descriptive taxonomic associations by assessing emerging functional and mechanistic models that integrate microbial metabolites, ecological interactions, strain-level variation, and host-microbiome communication. Clinical and translational evidence from melanoma, non-small cell lung cancer, colorectal cancer, hepatocellular carcinoma, renal cell carcinoma, and urothelial carcinoma reveals marked differences in the reproducibility and clinical maturity of reported microbial signatures. Emerging microbiome-targeted strategies, including dietary modulation, faecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), live biotherapeutic products (LBPs), and defined microbial consortia, may enhance ICI responsiveness, with responder-derived FMT providing important early clinical proof of concept. However, inter-individual variability, donor-recipient compatibility, microbial engraftment, the lack of standardised analytical approaches, and unresolved safety and regulatory requirements continue to limit clinical translation. Pending prospective validation, reasonable clinical practice is to avoid unnecessary microbiome-disrupting antibiotics, systematically document diet and concomitant medications, evaluate FMT and LBPs within regulated clinical trials, and interpret microbiome profiles alongside established tumour and host biomarkers rather than as stand-alone tests. Current evidence therefore supports a cautious shift towards functional microbiome-guided precision oncology, providing a foundation for personalised strategies to improve cancer immunotherapy outcomes.

title: Hemicyanine-Based Wash-Free Near-Infrared Fluorescent Probe for Imaging Amyloid-β Aggregates in Alzheimer's Disease.
abstract: As a key biomarker of Alzheimer's disease (AD), amyloid-β (Aβ) is frequently employed for the diagnosis of AD. Near-infrared fluorescence (NIRF) imaging is a non-invasive, low-cost route for visualizing Aβ in vivo. However, most existing Aβ NIRF probes require tedious washing steps, show modest fluorescence turn-on (<50-fold), and stain normal tissue non-specifically. In this work, by fine-tuning the amphiphilicity of a hemicyanine scaffold to place its log P within the appropriate range, we identified P3 as a wash-free NIRF probe for Aβ aggregates. P3 bound Aβ aggregates with high affinity. In vivo, P3 distinguished AD mice from wild-type mice with a 4.8-fold signal ratio, together with adequate brain uptake (1.5 ± 0.1 ID/g at 20 min) and rapid clearance. Unlike Thioflavin T, which indiscriminately labels Aβ aggregates and normal neurons, P3 specifically labeled Aβ aggregates with negligible background, which enabled wash-free imaging with a signal-to-noise ratio of 80 ± 4. This work provides a wash-free, high-affinity NIRF probe for Aβ imaging.

title: Flocculent Ti3AlC2-Based Two-Dimensional Material Flexible Microneedle Patch for Screening Alzheimer's Disease Animal Biomarkers and In Situ Revealing Spatial Aggregation of Arachidonic Acid.
abstract: Efficient diagnosis and pathological elucidation of Alzheimer's disease (AD) are constrained by the lack of technologies for in situ capture of metabolites in living brain tissues. Metabolic disorders in the parietal lobe highly correlate with AD progression, yet existing methods cannot achieve in situ capture and spatial analysis. A petal-like flocculent Ti3AlC2-based flexible microneedle patch was developed for in situ extraction and mass spectrometry of parietal metabolites in AD rabbits. Sodium hydroxide etching and cetyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTAB) self-assembly constructed a flocculent micro-/nanostructure, enhancing enrichment ~4-fold (2.5-fold after etching + 1.6-fold after CTAB). The stretchable substrate enables conformal attachment to the curved parietal lobe. Application to the exposed cortex demonstrates mechanical flexibility, linear glucose response (R2 = 0.9958) and resistance to salt/protein interference. Serum profiling of 15 AD patients and 15 controls with OPLS-DA shows clear discrimination (top-5 markers combined area under the curve (AUC) = 0.84). Spatial analysis reveals arachidonic acid's unique pattern of centralized aggregation with peripheral gradient diffusion. This novel in situ device enables brain metabolite detection and reveals abnormal arachidonic acid aggregation, providing evidence for lipid-pathway AD interventions.

title: Immunogenicity and Protective Efficacy of a Trivalent Whole-Virion Inactivated SARS-CoV-2 Vaccine Against Vaccine-Matched Ancestral, Delta, and Omicron BA.5 Variants in K18-hACE2 Mice.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Continuous antigenic evolution of SARS-CoV-2 has reduced the effectiveness of vaccines based on a single ancestral strain, highlighting the need for multivalent vaccine strategies. We developed a trivalent whole-virion inactivated vaccine containing ancestral (ERAGEM), Delta, and Omicron BA.5 antigens and evaluated its immunogenicity and protective efficacy in K18-hACE2 transgenic mice. METHODS: β-propiolactone-inactivated ERAGEM, Delta, and Omicron BA.5 antigens were combined at 1 μg each (3 μg total) with aluminium hydroxide and administered intraperitoneally on days 0 and 21. Variant-specific binding and neutralizing antibody responses were assessed by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) and microneutralization assays. On day 42, mice were challenged with ERAGEM, Delta, or Omicron BA.5. Survival, body weight, body temperature, infectious viral titers, and viral RNA loads were evaluated. RESULTS: The trivalent vaccine induced binding and neutralizing antibodies against all three vaccine components, and titers rose after the booster dose. Neutralizing responses were highest against the BA.5 component. Vaccinated mice showed 100% survival following challenge with each vaccine-matched variant and maintained stable body weight and temperature throughout the observation period. Unvaccinated controls challenged with Omicron BA.5 showed no mortality, so protection against this component could be assessed only virologically. No infectious virus was detected in the lungs of vaccinated animals, while viral titers and RNA loads in the nasal turbinates were significantly reduced compared with unvaccinated controls. CONCLUSIONS: A trivalent whole-virion inactivated SARS-CoV-2 vaccine containing ancestral, Delta, and Omicron BA.5 antigens elicited variant-specific humoral immunity and protected mice against challenge with each vaccine-matched component: against lethal challenge for the ancestral and Delta components, and against viral burden for Omicron BA.5, which was not lethal in unvaccinated controls. These outcomes were obtained at a lower per-antigen dose than in our previously reported monovalent and bivalent formulations; because those were independent studies rather than contemporaneous comparators, this suggests a dose-sparing potential that warrants formal evaluation rather than demonstrating one. Cross-protection against variants not included in the formulation was not assessed.

title: A Blockchain Platform for Vaccine Beneficiary Registration, Side Effects, Cold Supply Chain, and Personnel Training and Employment Management.
abstract: The world has faced pandemics throughout its history. The most recent, COVID-19, took lives and disrupted healthcare and economies. COVID-19 vaccine programs were launched worldwide; however, the record time in which vaccines were developed raises questions about side effects and their severity. Also, as vaccines are delicate medical products, their cold supply chain must be continuously tracked and monitored to ensure their efficacy. Moreover, vaccine supply chain management is complex and requires trained staff to handle its different activities. As such, it is important to connect beneficiaries' symptoms and registration systems with the vaccine supply chain to enable healthcare authorities to investigate whether observed side effects may be linked to cold chain handling conditions or production factors. Consequently, the need arises for a system that manages trained personnel certificate generation, which could also be used as a verification tool for employing the right experts for the right job. Therefore, our study developed a blockchain platform that integrates individuals' registration and side effect data with vaccine cold supply chain information. The developed platform also includes a certification system for cold supply chain personnel training to support authenticated certificate generation and role assignment management. Blockchain was selected due to its features of security, decentralization, traceability, and trust.
