The key contributions of this work lie in providing a digital collaborative management and data tracing platform for vaccine side effects that are linked to beneficiaries' registration and cold supply chain data to enable healthcare authorities to investigate whether any observed side effects may be linked to cold chain handling conditions or production factors while managing the issuance of certificates for trained cold supply chain personnel and controlling their employment in the correct chain(s). Our platform creates training certificate IDs without a central entity to regulate certificate generation and uses the created certificate information to control the employment of personnel with the appropriate training in the right chain to perform the right role. Our platform identified personnel employed in any chain where violations were recorded and side effects were subsequently reported, and presents their training and employment data, providing the interconnected data record necessary for accountability. The platform was tested successfully, producing the desired outcome of secure, traceable, and transparent vaccine data sharing, linking, and verification.

title: Prescribing SGLTis and GLP-1 RAs for Patients With Type 2 Diabetes, Guideline Updates, and Longitudinal Knowledge Assessment Scores.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2is) and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) reduce cardiovascular and kidney events in patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D) who have established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, heart failure, or chronic kidney disease, yet prescribing to these patients remains low. OBJECTIVES: To describe temporal patterns in SGLT2i and GLP-1 RA prescribing before and after the 2019 American Diabetes Association (ADA) guideline update and to assess whether these patterns differed across physicians with subsequently measured different first-year American Board of Internal Medicine Longitudinal Knowledge Assessment (LKA) scores. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This serial cross-sectional study was conducted from October 2025 through January 2026, using 2017 to 2022 traditional Medicare claims. Endocrinologists first participating in the 2022 to 2023 LKA and the Medicare beneficiaries with T2D they treated were included. EXPOSURE: Time relative to the 2019 ADA guideline update. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The annual patient-year SGLT2i and GLP-1RA guideline-targeted and nontargeted patient fill rates were the main outcome. Linear physician, year, and target subgroup fixed-effects regression models were estimated, with patient demographic and health risk controls to evaluate within-physician associations between guideline-targeted vs nontargeted patient-year fill rates each year relative to 2018 (the year before the guideline update). The variation in these associations across first-year LKA score quartiles was also evaluated. RESULTS: A total of 1061 endocrinologists caring for 177 284 Medicare beneficiaries with T2D (mean [SD] age, 74.5 [6.1] years; mean [SD] 54.4% [49.8] female; mean [SD] 9.3% [29.1] Black, 6.6% [24.9] Hispanic, and 76.2% [42.6] White non-Hispanic) were included. Adjusted guideline-targeted SGLT2i and GLP-1 RA fill rates increased monotonically from 2018 to 2022 by 11.4 percentage points (pp) (95% CI, 10.5 to 12.3 pp; P < .001) and 2.4 (95% CI, 1.4 to 3.3 pp; P < .001) for SGLT2is and GLP-1 RAs targeted vs nontargeted subgroups, respectively. The associated SGLT2i increase was 3.9 pp (95% CI, 1.4 to 6.5 pp) larger for patients of endocrinologists with top vs bottom LKA quartile scores (P = .003), but for GLP-1 RAs, this association was not statistically significant with wide confidence intervals. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cross-sectional study, 2019 ADA guideline update timing was associated with substantially increased SGLT2i and moderately increased GLP-1 RA guideline-concordant prescribing among guideline-targeted, compared with nontargeted, patient subgroups by 2020. These increases in SGLT2i guideline congruent prescribing were associated with higher subsequently measured first-year LKA scores.

title: GLP-1 RA Prescribing in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes and Cancer.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are increasingly used to treat type 2 diabetes, yet little is known about its utilization patterns in patients with cancer history, given limited oncology-specific guidance. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate trends and factors associated with GLP-1 RA use among Medicare beneficiaries with type 2 diabetes, comparing those with and without cancer history. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This retrospective cohort study used Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results-Medicare linked data to identify patients diagnosed with 7 common cancers in 2010 to 2021 and preexisting type 2 diabetes before cancer diagnosis. A noncancer cohort with type 2 diabetes was identified from a 5% random sample of Medicare beneficiaries and matched 1:1 to patients with cancer based on sociodemographic characteristics; controls were assigned a pseudo-index date corresponding to their matched patient's cancer diagnosis date. Beneficiaries were followed up annually until death or December 31, 2022, for TM or December 31, 2021, for MA. Data were analyzed from December 2025 to July 2026. EXPOSURES: Diagnosis of 1 of 7 common cancers. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Any GLP-1 RA use. Proportions of beneficiaries with any GLP-1 RA use annually were stratified by traditional Medicare (TM) and Medicare Advantage (MA). Multivariable logistic regression examined (1) differences in GLP-1RA use between cancer and noncancer cohorts with and without adjusting for sociodemographic characteristics and comorbidities and diabetes-related complications; (2) cancer-specific factors associated with GLP-1RA use among the cancer cohort after 2018. RESULTS: A total of 373 278 Medicare beneficiaries (mean [SD] age, 76.1 [6.6] years; 188 746 [50.6%] female) with cancer and diabetes and 373 278 noncancer controls (153 358 unique beneficiaries) were included. GLP-1 RA use increased from 85 beneficiaries (0.5%) to 9083 beneficiaries (8.2%) and from 138 beneficiaries (0.9%) to 9300 beneficiaries (6.2%) in the cancer and noncancer cohorts, respectively, from 2010 to 2022 under TM; a similar increase was observed under MA. Despite higher unadjusted GLP-1 RA use among the cancer cohort than the noncancer cohort (probability difference, TM: 1.19 [95% CI, 0.94 to 1.44] percentage points [pp]; P < .001; MA: 0.45 [95% CI, 0.21 to 0.68] pp, P < .001), adjusted analysis showed no significant differences in GLP-1 RA use under TM (adjusted probability difference, 0.16 [95% CI, -0.10 to 0.41,] pp; P = .22) and lower use among cancer cohort under MA (-0.52 [95% CI, -0.76 to -0.28] pp; P < .001). Complications or comorbidities, including obesity (adjusted probability difference, TM: 3.35 [95% CI, 3.10 to 3.61] pp; P < .001; MA: 2.42 [95% CI, 2.19 to 2.64] pp; P < .001), dyslipidemia (adjusted probability difference, TM: 2.26 [95% CI, 2.03 to 2.50] pp; P < .001; MA: 1.80 [95% CI, 1.57 to 2.03] pp; P < .001), neuropathy (adjusted probability difference: TM: 3.91 [95% CI, 3.64 to 4.19] pp; P < .001; MA: 3.17 [95% CI, 2.94 to 3.41] pp; P < .001), retinopathy (adjusted probability difference, TM: 2.02 [95% CI, 1.78 to 2.27] pp; P < .001; MA: 1.84 [95% CI, 1.63 to 2.06] pp; P < .001), and chronic kidney disease (adjusted probability difference, TM: 2.01 [95% CI, 1.76 to 2.26] pp; P < .001; MA: 1.63 [95% CI, 1.40 to 1.85] pp; P < .001) were associated with greater likelihood of GLP-1RA use. Within the cancer cohort, breast (adjusted probability difference, TM: 1.05 [95% CI, 0.43 to 1.66] pp; P = .001; MA: 0.89 [95% CI, 0.37 to 1.41] pp; P = .001), gynecologic (adjusted probability difference, MA: 1.13 [95% CI, 0.45 to 1.81] pp; P = .001), and prostate (adjusted probability difference, TM: 1.30 [95% CI, 0.72 to 1.88] pp; P < .001; MA: 1.07 [95% CI, 0.56 to 1.58] pp; P < .001) cancers were associated with higher GLP-1 RA use than colorectal cancer, while pancreatic cancer was associated with lower GLP-1 RA use (adjusted probability difference, TM: -2.55 [95% CI, -3.17 to -1.93] pp; P < .001; MA: -1.64 [95% CI, -2.23 to -1.05] pp; P < .001). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this retrospective study of Medicare beneficiaries with type 2 diabetes, GLP-1 RA use increased substantially and primarily was associated with metabolic risk profile, with limited associations with cancer status. Variation across cancer types and stages suggests oncologic context may influence prescribing.

title: Iguratimod combined with tofacitinib in rheumatoid arthritis patients with inadequate response to conventional synthetic or biological DMARDs: a retrospective study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a common, chronic immunologically mediated inflammatory disease causing joint inflammation and damage. While disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) are effective, some patients respond inadequately. This study evaluates the efficacy and safety of combining iguratimod, an anti-rheumatic agent originally developed in Japan, with tofacitinib, an oral Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor, in RA patients with inadequate response to conventional synthetic or biologic DMARDs. METHODS: A retrospective study analyzed the medical records of adult RA patients with moderate-to-high disease activity (DAS28 > 3.2) despite prior treatment with conventional DMARDs, biologics, or monotherapy with either iguratimod or tofacitinib for at least 3 months. Patients received combination therapy with standard doses (iguratimod 25 mg bid, tofacitinib 5 mg bid) for 24 weeks. Primary outcomes were the change in DAS28-ESR score and ACR20/50/70 response rates at 24 weeks. Secondary outcomes included serial measurements of erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP) at weeks 4, 8, 12, and 24. Proportions were summarized with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and repeated measures of ESR and CRP were analyzed with a linear mixed-effects model with estimated marginal mean changes from baseline and a linear trend test. RESULTS: 28 patients were included, and all 28 completed the 24-week follow-up and constituted the full analysis set, without withdrawal or loss to follow-up. After 24 weeks of combination therapy, DAS28-ESR decreased from 5.30 ± 0.50 to 3.07 ± 0.83 (mean change - 2.23, 95% CI - 2.48 to - 1.97; P < 0.001). Seventy-five percent of patients (21/28, 95% CI 56.6 to 87.3%) achieved the treatment target (remission, DAS28-ESR < 2.6, in 25%, 95% CI 12.7 to 43.4%; low disease activity, DAS28-ESR ≤ 3.2, in 50%, 95% CI 32.6 to 67.4%). ACR20, ACR50, and ACR70 response rates were 85.7% (95% CI 68.5 to 94.3%), 67.9% (95% CI 49.3 to 82.1%), and 32.1% (95% CI 17.9 to 50.7%), respectively. ESR and CRP levels showed significant and progressive reductions from baseline at weeks 4, 8, 12, and 24 (all P < 0.001), with a significant linear trend over time in the mixed-effects model. Most patients successfully tapered glucocorticoids and discontinued NSAIDs and prior DMARDs. One adverse event (herpes zoster) was reported and resolved with standard management. CONCLUSION: In this retrospective study of refractory RA patients, combination therapy with iguratimod and tofacitinib for 24 weeks demonstrated significant improvements in disease activity (DAS28-ESR, ACR response rates) and inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) with limited adverse events observed. Given the small sample size and single-arm design, these findings are exploratory and hypothesis-generating. The results suggest this oral combination therapy warrants further evaluation in larger, prospective, randomized controlled trials.

title: Pancreatic δ cells are resistant to auto- and paracrine inhibition in human type-2 diabetes.
abstract: Somatostatin secretion from pancreatic δ cells inhibits nearby α- and β cells and tunes the body's glycemic set-point. The role of δ cells in diabetes remains unclear, in part due to the difficulty separating intrinsic regulation from intraislet paracrine effects. Here, we compared the function of isolated δ cells of cadaveric nondiabetic and type-2 diabetic donors by single cell total internal reflection microscopy, electrophysiology, and secretion measurements. Elevated glucose stimulated exocytosis of somatostatin, which was further amplified by glucagon, exendin-4, or forskolin, independent of diabetic status. gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) enhanced exocytosis and electrical activity, while insulin had no detectable effect. Adrenaline and somatostatin strongly inhibited δ cell activity, leading to autocrine feedback inhibition of somatostatin exocytosis. In type-2 diabetes, δ cell inhibition by somatostatin and adrenaline was impaired, together with a marked reduction in somatostatin receptor (SSTR2) surface expression. The data suggest that selective loss of inhibitory control of δ cells may dysregulate intraislet somatostatin signaling in type-2 diabetes.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Genomic characteristics and immunotherapy benefit in MSI-H/dMMR lung cancer: Insights from comparative analyses of Chinese and Western cohorts.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Microsatellite instability (MSI) is a pivotal pan-cancer biomarker for immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy. However, due to the low frequency of MSI-high (MSI-H) in lung cancer (LC), the genetic characteristics and prognosis of this subgroup were rarely reported. METHODS: A total of 4539 Chinese LC patients were screened for microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H)/deficient DNA mismatch repair (dMMR) status. Of these, 344 patients with available detailed clinical and genomic data were further analyzed to assess clinicopathologic correlates and genomic differences compared to 1053 samples from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA). Comparative analyses were performed between MSI-H/dMMR and microsatellite stable (MSS)/proficient mismatch repair (pMMR) groups, as well as between the Chinese and TCGA dMMR cohorts. Additionally, we performed a systematic literature review to evaluate clinical outcomes. RESULTS: We observed an overall MSI-H/dMMR prevalence of 1.08% in Chinese patients. While the rate in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) was 1.94%, the phenotype was predominantly observed in lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC, 3.81%), which was approximately four-fold higher than that in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD, 0.89%). TCGA data showed similar LUSC predominance (1.85% vs. 1.41% in LUAD). MSI-H/dMMR status were correlated with younger age, early-stage, and non-metastatic disease. Chinese MSI-H/dMMR LC samples showed frequent TP53, EGFR, and BRCA2 mutations, enriched indel mutations and C>T transitions. TCGA MSI-H/dMMR tumors had higher TP53 (82.4% vs. 52.3%) and lower EGFR mutations than Chinese patients. A literature review of 16 MSI-H/dMMR patients suggests prolonged progression-free survival (PFS) with ICI regimens. CONCLUSIONS: MSI-H/dMMR LC exhibits distinct clinicogenomic features between Chinese vs. TCGA population, with histotype- and cohort-specific mutational landscapes. These findings inform MMR-driven tumor biology and ethnic-dependent therapeutic strategies.

title: Neoadjuvant and perioperative chemoimmunotherapy versus chemotherapy for resectable non-small-cell lung cancer: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Although neoadjuvant and perioperative chemoimmunotherapy improve outcomes in resectable non-small-cell lung cancer, treatment effects remain incompletely defined for specific subgroups. We searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science through 3 December 2025 and pooled eight randomized trials involving 3387 patients using random-effects models. Exploratory event-free survival (EFS) analyses yielded hazard ratios (HRs) of 0.57 for perioperative and 0.66 for pure neoadjuvant regimens versus chemotherapy. The indirect ratio of HRs was 0.86 (95% CI, 0.63-1.18; interaction P = 0.347), with insufficient precision to establish equivalence. Among patients with PD-L1 tumor-cell expression <1%, the pooled EFS HR was 0.77 (95% CI, 0.65-0.91), although all six trial-specific CIs included 1. China-only trials had numerically lower EFS HRs than international trials (0.48 versus 0.63; interaction P = 0.053). Surgery occurred in 82.2% versus 77.9% (risk ratio, 1.06; risk difference, 4.7 percentage points); nominal significance varied with study omission. Overall EFS and overall survival favored chemoimmunotherapy (HRs, 0.59 [95% CI,0.52-0.66] and 0.68 [0.57-0.80], respectively). Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events increased in the two eligible perioperative trials (risk ratio, 1.12; 95% CI, 1.02-1.24). Trial-level pathological response-survival analyses did not establish surrogate validity. Subgroup findings remain hypothesis-generating, and the surgical difference does not establish a clinically meaningful improvement in resectability.

title: Mining key differentially expressed genes and construction of a prognostic risk score model for colorectal cancer based on bioinformatics.
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains the third most common malignancy and the second leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide, with limited biomarkers available for accurate prognostic stratification. This study integrates multi-cohort transcriptomic data from four GEO datasets (GSE39582, GSE17536, GSE14333, GSE33113; n = 1123) and the TCGA-CRC cohort (n = 621) to identify key differentially expressed genes and construct a validated prognostic risk score model. Differential expression analysis using the limma framework identified 642 upregulated and 588 downregulated genes (|log2FC|>1, FDR<0.05). Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) extracted hub genes from modules significantly correlated with overall survival. LASSO Cox regression then reduced the hub gene set to an eight-gene prognostic signature (MMP1, AURKA, TOP2A, CDH1, COL1A1, CLDN1, ETV4, CDX2) that stratified patients into high- and low-risk groups with significantly different survival outcomes (p < 0.001, log-rank test). The model achieved AUCs of 0.824, 0.796, and 0.768 for 1-, 3-, and 5-year overall survival in the training cohort and was validated in three independent datasets. High-risk patients exhibited immunosuppressive microenvironments (elevated M2 macrophages, Tregs) and increased resistance to standard chemotherapy agents. Integration of the risk score with clinical variables improved prognostic accuracy (C-index 0.812). These findings offer a robust bioinformatics-derived prognostic tool with implications for immunotherapy patient selection and personalized treatment planning in CRC.

title: Pretreatment platelet count exhibits a U-shaped association with outcomes after immune checkpoint blockade with a mid-range stratum for dual-checkpoint immunotherapy.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Platelets contribute to tumor progression and immune regulation, but the relationship between pretreatment platelet count and immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) outcomes across the clinical range remains unclear. METHODS: This study conducted a retrospective multicohort study of patients treated with ICB. In a Memorial Sloan Kettering pan-cancer cohort (n = 1,479), platelet count was modeled using penalized cubic splines and clinically defined strata, with 150-249 × 109/L as the reference. Cox models adjusted for age, sex, prior chemotherapy, ICB class, tumor stage, cancer type, and tumor mutational burden. Findings were evaluated in a validation cohort (n = 717) and in non-small cell lung cancer (n = 666) and melanoma (n = 377) analyses. An exploratory pooled analysis (n = 2,196) compared mono-ICB with dual PD-1/PD-L1 plus CTLA-4 blockade across platelet strata. RESULTS: Platelet count showed a U-shaped association with overall survival. Relative to 150-249 × 109/L, adjusted mortality hazards were higher at 49-124 × 109/L (hazard ratio [HR], 1.83; p = 0.0001), 300-399 × 109/L (HR, 1.56; p < 0.0001), and 400-977 × 109/L (HR, 1.93; p < 0.0001). High counts were also associated with shorter progression-free survival (HR, 1.27 for 300-399 × 109/L and 1.32 for 400-977 × 109/L; both p = 0.003), whereas associations at low counts were weaker. Similar patterns were observed in the validation and cancer-specific cohorts. Dual ICB was associated with longer median overall survival than mono-ICB only in the 150-300 × 109/L stratum (2.34 vs 1.42 years; p < 0.0001). CONCLUSIONS: Pretreatment platelet count is an inexpensive biomarker with a nonlinear association with ICB outcomes. Both low and high counts identify increased mortality risk, supporting flexible modeling rather than a single thrombocytosis threshold. The platelet-defined signal for dual ICB is hypothesis-generating and requires prospective validation before treatment selection.

title: Thyroid surveillance practices in GLP-1 receptor agonist use and its potential influence on thyroid cancer detection: A scoping review.
abstract: Rodent data prompted a boxed warning for medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) with glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), yet human findings remain inconsistent and may reflect how intensively patients are screened. We mapped reported thyroid screening practices and detection bias reporting. Following JBI methodology and PRISMA-ScR reporting guidance, we searched PubMed, Scopus, Embase, CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov from 2010 to July 2026. Empirical studies and trial registry records reporting thyroid screening in adult GLP-1RA users were eligible. Records were charted and synthesised descriptively. Thirty-nine records were included (29 published studies, 10 registry records). Screening was predominantly biochemical. Calcitonin was reported in 16/29 studies (55.2%) and all registry records, whereas ultrasonography was reported in 13/29 (44.8%) and no trials. 19/29 studies (65.5%) described a screening protocol. Screening intensity was reported in 18/29(62.1%) but detection bias in 11/29 (37.9%). All registry records excluded personal or family history of MTC or multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 before screening. Thyroid screening in GLP-1RA users is heterogeneous, calcitonin-centred, and inconsistently reported, while patients at highest C-cell risk are excluded from trials. Detection bias is seldom addressed despite documented increases in imaging. Standardised reporting of screening intensity is needed to interpret thyroid cancer rates.

title: Semaglutide and Panic Attacks: Active-Comparator Disproportionality Analysis, Temporal Assessment of Notoriety Bias and Evidence Triangulation in Post-Marketing Pharmacovigilance.
abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate how confounding by indication and notoriety bias shape the apparent semaglutide-panic attack signal in the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) and to interpret this signal using an evidence-triangulation framework integrating randomized and observational studies. METHODS: We conducted an active-comparator restricted disproportionality analysis of FAERS (2018Q1-2024Q4), including individual case safety reports in which semaglutide, dulaglutide or empagliflozin was the primary suspect drug. Panic attack was identified using the MedDRA preferred term. Crude and adjusted reporting odds ratios (RORs, aRORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using logistic regression, adjusting for age, sex and indication (Type 2 diabetes, obesity/weight management). Notoriety bias was assessed using prespecified temporal analyses (analyses restricted to reports received before July 1, 2023 and a drug-by-period comparison of 2018-2022 with 2023-2024) and reporting proportions per 10 000 reports. A sensitivity analysis used all other primary-suspect drugs in FAERS as the reference set. In parallel, we conducted a systematic review (MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL to November 24, 2025) of randomized trials, cohort and cross-sectional studies, pharmacovigilance analyses and case reports reporting panic attacks or acute anxiety outcomes with semaglutide. RESULTS: Among 33 267 semaglutide, 54 282 dulaglutide and 25 380 empagliflozin reports, panic attacks were recorded in 87 (0.26%), 28 (0.05%) and 13 (0.05%) cases, respectively. Crude RORs were 5.08 (95% CI 3.32-7.78) versus dulaglutide and 5.12 (95% CI 2.86-9.17) versus empagliflozin, attenuating after adjustment to 2.82 (95% CI 1.74-4.56) and 2.75 (95% CI 1.41-5.36). In the pre-warning period crude RORs were 2.24 (95% CI 1.23-4.07) and 2.15 (95% CI 1.00-4.58), attenuating to 1.38 (95% CI 0.69-2.75) and 1.14 (95% CI 0.48-2.68) after adjustment. Panic-attack reports per 10 000 semaglutide reports rose from 6.7 in 2018-2022 to 42.0 in 2023-2024 (drug-by-period interaction p = 0.007). Against all other primary-suspect drugs, the aROR was 1.48 (95% CI 1.18-1.87) overall and 0.76 (95% CI 0.48-1.18) before July 1, 2023. Across 12 studies, randomized trials and active-comparator observational cohorts did not show a consistent increase in panic attacks or anxiety-related outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: Crude FAERS analyses suggested a semaglutide-panic attack signal that attenuated after adjustment was no longer significant before the July 2023 regulatory communication and rose sharply thereafter in a pattern consistent with notoriety bias. Triangulation with randomized trials and active-comparator observational studies does not support a consistent pharmacological association. Disproportionality analyses are hypothesis-generating and cannot estimate incidence or establish causality. This case study illustrates how active-comparator design, temporal assessment of notoriety bias and evidence triangulation can improve the interpretation of post-marketing safety signals.

title: SGLT2 Inhibitors and risk of bacteriuria, candiduria, and UTI-related hospitalization: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: SGLT2 inhibitors induce glycosuria; however, pathogen-specific real-world data on UTI risk are scarce, particularly in individuals without diabetes. We compared positive urine cultures, UTI-related hospitalizations, and Gram-negative, Gram-positive, and yeast-positive cultures after the initiation of SGLT2 inhibitors vs. GLP-1 receptor agonists in adults with and without type 2 diabetes. METHODS: We conducted parallel propensity score-matched, active-comparator, new-user cohort studies within Clalit Health Services, Israel (2015-2024). Matching and Poisson regression were performed separately in all patients and in the strata with and without documented UTI in the preceding two years. RESULTS: We analyzed 153,660 SGLT2 inhibitor initiators (134,060 with diabetes) and 172,262 GLP-1 receptor agonist initiators (93,086 with diabetes). Yeast-positive cultures were markedly more frequent with SGLT2 inhibitors (diabetes IRR 3.31, 95% CI 2.79-3.94; no diabetes 7.76, 2.34-47.99), as were Gram-positive uropathogens (1.34, 1.23-1.45; 1.53, 1.13-2.10), whereas Gram-negative uropathogens were not (0.74, 0.72-0.77; 1.05, 0.94-1.18). Overall culture positivity was lower with SGLT2 inhibitors in patients with diabetes (0.84, 0.81-0.86), but not in those without prior UTI (1.00, 0.96-1.04), and higher in patients without diabetes (1.14, 1.03-1.27). UTI-related hospitalization was uncommon (0.85, 0.74-0.97; 1.01, 0.58-1.83). CONCLUSIONS: Compared with GLP-1 receptor agonists, SGLT2 inhibitor initiation was associated with a marked increase in yeast-positive urine cultures irrespective of diabetes status, a smaller increase in Gram-positive uropathogens, and no increase in Gram-negative uropathogens. Culture positivity was higher in patients without diabetes, and UTI-related hospitalization remained uncommon. These findings support the continued use of SGLT2 inhibitors when indicated, with candiduria as a specific safety signal warranting further characterization.
journal: Clinical microbiology and infection : the official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology and Infectious Diseases

title: Lactate-Induced PPP1R1B Upregulation Drives Resistance to Neoadjuvant Immunotherapy in NSCLC via IRF3 Dephosphorylation.
abstract: Neoadjuvant immunotherapy has improved clinical outcomes in resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC); however, a substantial proportion of patients fail to achieve durable responses, and the mechanisms underlying therapeutic resistance remain incompletely understood. Here, we identified protein phosphatase 1 regulatory inhibitor subunit 1B (PPP1R1B) as a metabolic driver of immunotherapy resistance in NSCLC through RNA sequencing of tumors with differential responses to neoadjuvant anti-PD-1 therapy. PPP1R1B was significantly upregulated in non-responders and correlated with poor prognosis in NSCLC patients. Mechanistically, PPP1R1B directly interacted with IRF3 through the Arg29 residue and promoted dephosphorylation of IRF3 at Ser396, thereby suppressing IRF3 activation and downstream interferon-β (IFN-β) signaling. PPP1R1B-mediated inhibition of IFN-β signaling reduced CD8+ T-cell infiltration and impaired antitumor immunity, ultimately conferring resistance to anti-PD-1 therapy in vivo. Blockade of IFN-β signaling abrogated the antitumor effects induced by PPP1R1B depletion, supporting an immune-dependent mechanism. Notably, tumors resistant to neoadjuvant immunotherapy exhibited impaired oxidative phosphorylation and excessive lactate accumulation. Lactate induced PPP1R1B expression through NF-κB-dependent transcriptional activation, linking metabolic reprogramming to innate immune suppression. Collectively, our findings identify a lactate/NF-κB/PPP1R1B/IRF3 signaling axis that drives immune evasion and resistance to neoadjuvant immunotherapy in NSCLC, and nominate PPP1R1B as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target for overcoming anti-PD-1 resistance.

title: Venous Thromboembolism Reporting in Fusion-Positive NSCLC Treated with Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors: A Systematic Review of Safety Reporting and Protocol-Level Provisions in Phase I-IV Clinical Trials.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is increasingly recognized as a clinically relevant complication in patients with fusion-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, the completeness and consistency of thromboembolic safety reporting in clinical trials of tyrosine kinase inhibitors remain poorly characterized. METHODS: We performed a systematic review of phase I-IV clinical trials evaluating targeted therapies in fusion-positive NSCLC. Protocols, publications, and online trial registry updates were systematically reviewed to assess thromboembolic event ascertainment, reporting practices, protocol-level anticoagulant therapy provisions, and VTE-related eligibility criteria. RESULTS: A total of 108 reporting sources from 61 study entries (58 unique trials) were reviewed. Pulmonary embolism and deep vein thrombosis were the predominant reported events. VTE-related information was highly fragmented across reporting sources: 14 study entries reported events exclusively through full-text publications, 19 exclusively through online trial updates, and 15 through both sources. Study protocols rarely prespecified thromboembolic events as dedicated safety outcomes, more commonly addressing them in eligibility criteria, anticoagulant therapy provisions, or differential diagnosis guidance. More than 40% of study entries lacked protocol-level anticoagulant therapy provisions and nearly 60% lacked VTE-related eligibility restrictions. Marked heterogeneity was observed in event definitions, reporting practices, safety ascertainment, and observation periods. CONCLUSIONS: In fusion-positive NSCLC trials, heterogeneity in event ascertainment and reporting, rather than a true scarcity of thromboembolic events, represents a major limitation of the available evidence. Greater standardization of safety reporting and integration of trial registry and publication data may improve the completeness, comparability, and interpretability of future studies.

title: Better After CHoosing in rheumatoid arthritis (the BACH trial): patients who have the opportunity to choose their treatment are more satisfied.
Abscopal-like Regression of Lung Metastases After Near-infrared Photoimmunotherapy Plus Nivolumab in Laryngeal Carcinoma.
abstract: BACKGROUND/AIM: Near-infrared photoimmunotherapy (NIR-PIT) combines tumor-selective cytotoxicity with the induction of immunogenic cell death and may therefore augment the systemic activity of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). However, clinical evidence of responses in distant, non-illuminated lesions is lacking. We describe a distant visceral response following NIR-PIT administered during programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) blockade. CASE REPORT: A man in his 60s presented with recurrent laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma involving the base of the tongue and multiple pulmonary metastases that had progressed after definitive chemoradiotherapy, salvage total laryngectomy, re-irradiation, and platinum- and pembrolizumab-containing regimens. Nivolumab monotherapy was initiated, and NIR-PIT of the base-of-tongue lesion was added one month later. Using the pre-NIR-PIT status as baseline, the target pulmonary metastasis decreased from 12.1 to 8.0 mm and a cervical lymph node from 15.3 to 11.1 mm at 4 months (sum -30.3%; partial response by RECIST 1.1), with both lesions located outside the illuminated field. This response deepened and was maintained at 10 months (7.6 and 8.2 mm; sum -42.3%). In contrast, the illuminated base-of-tongue lesion persisted despite a second NIR-PIT at 5 months. Adverse events were limited to grade 2 facial and cervical edema and local pain. CONCLUSION: The addition of local NIR-PIT to nivolumab was followed by durable, abscopal-like regression of non-illuminated pulmonary metastases in immunotherapy-refractory head and neck cancer. While causality cannot be established from a single case, this observation supports formal investigation of NIR-PIT-ICI combinations in patients with distant metastases.

title: Treatment-specific Association of H&E-based Stromal Tumor-infiltrating Lymphocytes With Survival in Pleural Mesothelioma Treated With Ipilimumab/Nivolumab or Chemotherapy.
abstract: BACKGROUND/AIM: Pleural mesothelioma lacks robust biomarkers to guide personalized treatment selection. Although stromal tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (sTILs) on hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained sections represent a cost-effective biomarker in various cancers, their clinical significance in pleural mesothelioma remains unclear. This study evaluated the prognostic impact of sTILs in pleural mesothelioma patients treated with platinum-pemetrexed chemotherapy or dual immune checkpoint inhibition (ICI) using ipilimumab plus nivolumab (Ipi/Nivo). PATIENTS AND METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 179 patients with unresectable pleural mesothelioma who received either platinum-pemetrexed chemotherapy (n=127) or Ipi/Nivo (n=52). sTILs were assessed according to the International TILs Working Group guidelines and categorized as high (>10%) or low (≤10%). Overall survival (OS) and associations between sTIL status and clinicopathological characteristics were evaluated. RESULTS: High and low sTIL status was observed in 82 (45.8%) and 97 (54.2%) patients, respectively. Within each treatment cohort, baseline clinicopathological characteristics were generally well-balanced according to sTIL status. In the entire cohort, sTIL status was not significantly associated with OS (p=0.559). Subgroup analyses according to treatment modality showed no significant association between sTIL status and OS in the platinum-pemetrexed cohort (p=0.664). In contrast, in the Ipi/Nivo cohort, OS was significantly longer in the low sTIL group than in the high sTIL group (p=0.027). CONCLUSION: sTILs may have treatment-specific prognostic significance in pleural mesothelioma. Notably, low sTIL status was associated with longer survival among patients treated with dual ICI but not chemotherapy. Standardized H&E-based sTIL assessment may provide a simple and accessible approach for refining treatment selection in pleural mesothelioma.

title: Integration of TRM-Cell Infiltration and PD-L1 Expression Improves Prognostic Stratification After Resection of NSCLC.
abstract: BACKGROUND/AIM: Tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes, including tissue-resident memory T (TRM) cells, are associated with prognosis in patients after resection of non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, their clinical significance in the context of tumor immune suppression, such as through expression of programmed cell death ligand-1 (PD-L1), remains unclear. We hypothesized that integrating TRM-cell infiltration with PD-L1 expression would improve prognostic stratification. PATIENTS AND METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 316 patients with NSCLC who underwent curative resection between 2017 and 2020 without perioperative immunotherapy. TRM cells were quantified by CD103 immunohistochemistry using tissue microarrays and digitally analyzed with QuPath. PD-L1 expression was assessed using the 22C3 assay. Recurrence was evaluated using competing-risks analysis. Recurrence-free survival (RFS) and overall survival (OS) were analyzed using the Kaplan-Meier method and Cox proportional hazards models. RESULTS: The median TRM density was 54.8 cells/mm2 and was used to define TRM-high and TRM-low groups. TRM-high tumors were associated with non-adenocarcinoma histology and PD-L1 expression ≥1%. Patients with TRM-high tumors showed a significantly lower cumulative incidence of recurrence (p=0.039), whereas PD-L1 expression ≥1% was associated with worse RFS and OS. When combined, TRM-high/PD-L1 expression <1% demonstrated lowest cumulative incidence of recurrence (p=0.017) and significantly improved RFS and OS (p=0.0035 and p=0.0031, respectively). In multivariable analysis, TRM-high/PD-L1 expression <1% was independently associated with lower recurrence (hazard ratio=0.36) and improved RFS (hazard ratio=0.47). CONCLUSION: The combined assessment of TRM-cell infiltration and PD-L1 expression provides robust prognostic stratification in resected NSCLC and may serve as a useful biomarker for predicting postoperative outcomes.

title: Ovalbumin Functionalized Au-Pd Nanodumbbells Enable Photothermal-Immunotherapy With OVA-Associated Immune Activation.
abstract: Melanoma remains highly lethal due to rapid progression and limited response to conventional therapies. Photothermal therapy (PTT) offers precise tumor ablation, yet its efficacy is restricted by shallow light penetration and weak immunogenicity. Here, we develop a multifunctional immuno-photothermal nanoplatform based on bimetallic Au-Pd nanodumbbells coated with a genipin crosslinked ovalbumin (OVA) antigenic shell (AuPd-G-OVA NDs). The bilateral Pd coating enhances NIR-II (1064 nm) absorption and photothermal conversion, enabling effective NIR-II heating. Genipin crosslinking provides stable antigen loading and promotes dendritic cell activation. Upon irradiation, AuPd-G-OVA NDs induce potent photothermal ablation and promote reactive oxygen species (ROS)-mediated oxidative stress with ICD-associated immunogenic damage, facilitating enhanced antigen presentation and OVA-associated T-cell responses. In vivo, this platform significantly suppresses B16-OVA melanoma growth and elicits durable systemic antitumor immunity. These findings demonstrate a synergistic strategy integrating PTT with OVA-associated immunotherapy, offering a promising approach for advanced melanoma treatment.

title: Tumor plasticity in macrophage niches promotes dormancy, EMT and chemoresistance of non-small cell lung cancer stem cells.
abstract: Macrophages are the major immune cell type in the microenvironment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), playing a key role in tumor development, progression, and response to therapies. Elucidating the interplay between macrophages and NSCLC is crucial to fulfill the potential of macrophage-targeting strategies. We used NSCLC surgical specimens to generate multicellular spheroids enriched in cancer stem cells (CSCs) and highly responsive to microenvironmental cues. NSCLC spheroids were used to characterize state transitions induced by macrophage-tumor cell interactions in terms of proliferation, epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT), expression of stemness-related factors, self-renewal, and drug resistance. To define whether state transitions were induced by cell-cell contact or soluble factors, we compared direct co-cultures of spheroids and macrophages with transwell cultures, where cells are separated by a porous membrane. Cellular interactions were recorded by time-lapse microscopy and immunofluorescence (IF), whereas EMT, dormancy, stemness and chemoresistance were evaluated by real-time PCR, immunoblotting and functional assays. We found that co-cultures allowing cell-cell contact, but not transwell cultures, induced robust state transitions in NSCLC CSCs, promoting a state of dormancy associated with increased stemness, EMT and chemoresistance. In direct co-cultures (named NIDO, for Niche-Induced DOrmancy), macrophages and tumor cells formed nest-shaped aggregates and underwent a specular modulation of TGF-β levels, suggesting a physical transfer of this cytokine from macrophages to NSCLC cells within cellular nests. Treatment with Bafilomycin A1, an inhibitor of autophagosome-lysosome fusion and autolysosome acidification, inhibited TGF-β relocation and prevented the full spectrum of TGF-β-induced state transitions, including chemoresistance, EMT, and nest formation. By contrast, antibody-mediated TGF-β neutralization had only a partial effect, indicating secretory autophagy as a key mechanism underlying macrophage-tumor cell interplay. Altogether, these results show that lung macrophages crucially influence CSC phenotype, proliferation, and therapy resistance, pointing to a key role of local cell circuits in regulating tumor cell plasticity.

title: mRNA-1273 SARS-CoV-2 vaccination in people with HIV: an immune correlates analysis of CD4 + T cell responses in the multicenter CoVPN 3008 observational study.
abstract: T cell correlates of COVID-19 risk are poorly defined, particularly in people with HIV (PWH). CoVPN 3008 ( NCT05168813 ) Part A was a prospective 14,002-participant cohort study that administered one or two doses of mRNA-1273 COVID-19 vaccine, depending on baseline SARS-CoV-2 serostatus, in participants (83% PWH) in sub-Saharan Africa. Participants self-monitored for prespecified COVID-19 symptoms, defined by Centers for Disease Control and Prevention symptom criteria. Previous work showed that protection from COVID-19 was superior for hybrid versus vaccine-induced immunity, and that neutralizing antibody titers inversely associated with COVID-19 risk. In the present work, we measured T cell responses to Spike and Nucleocapsid at baseline and 4 weeks post last-vaccination (Peak) in a case-cohort study and assessed them as correlates of risk. In Hybrid Group PWH (n = 22 cases), COVID-19 risk over 6 months decreased with increasing Peak Spike BA.4/5-specific CD4 + T cell responses, from 15.8%, 4.7%, and 0% risk at 0.1%, 0.2%, and 0.3% IFN-γ and/or IL-2 response magnitude, respectively. Including baseline Spike-specific neutralizing antibody titer and Peak CD4 + T cell functionality score in the same model increased the association's strength (overall p < 0.001). Thus, CD4 + T cell responses are an independent correlate of COVID-19 risk among PWH with pre-existing SARS-CoV-2 immunity.

title: Targeting exosomal circSENP5 prevents immune escape of macrophages in pMMR-CRC via regulating mitochondrial metabolism.
abstract: Proficient mismatch repair colorectal cancer (pMMR-CRC) exhibits resistance to immunotherapy, presenting a significant clinical challenge that must be addressed. Exosomes, which serve as mediators of intercellular communication, play a crucial role in the tumor microenvironment (TME). However, the mechanisms that exosomes regulate tumor immunity in pMMR-CRC need to be fully elucidated. In this study, we discovered that circSENP5, a circular RNA (circRNA), is highly expressed in pMMR-CRC and is derived from exosomes that are transferred to tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs). This transfer enhances the oxidative phosphorylation of macrophages and promotes immunosuppressive characteristics, as well as increased levels of inhibitory receptors on CD8+ T cells. Mechanistically, circSENP5 binds to the deubiquitinase USP10, stabilizing LRPPRC, a key regulator of mitochondrial function. This interaction protects LRPPRC from ubiquitin-mediated degradation, resulting in enhanced mitochondrial respiration and immune suppression. in vivo, the overexpression of circSENP5 accelerates tumor progression, while its mutation disrupts the interaction with USP10, leading to reduced TAM infiltration and improved CD8+ T cell function. Targeting circSENP5 in combination with anti-PD-L1 immune checkpoint therapy effectively suppresses tumor progression, highlighting a potential therapeutic strategy. These findings suggest that exosomal circSENP5 plays a pivotal role in immune evasion in pMMR-CRC by modulating mitochondrial metabolism in TAMs, thereby providing potential therapeutic targets for overcoming immune resistance in pMMR-CRC.

title: Cardiovascular Effects of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Across Age Groups: An Updated Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
abstract: AIMS: To evaluate whether cardiovascular effects of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) differ by age. MATERIALS AND METHODS: PubMed and Embase were searched to 1 July 2026 for randomized placebo-controlled GLP-1RA trials in adults with type 2 diabetes or overweight/obesity reporting age-stratified major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; a composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, and non-fatal stroke). Hazard ratios (HRs) for participants aged < 65 and ≥ 65 years were pooled using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation and Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Effect modification was assessed by pooling trial-specific ratios of HRs (RHRs) for ≥ 65 versus < 65 years. Where reported, effects were assessed across < 65, 65 to < 75 and ≥ 75 years. RESULTS: Eight trials (SUSTAIN-6, EXSCEL, Harmony Outcomes, PIONEER 6, REWIND, AMPLITUDE-O, SELECT and SOUL) comprising 71 926 participants were included. GLP-1RAs reduced MACE at < 65 years and ≥ 65 years, with pooled HRs of 0.81 (95% CI 0.69-0.94; I2 = 64.1%) and 0.84 (95% CI 0.79-0.90; I2 = 0.0%), respectively. The pooled RHR showed no clear evidence of effect modification (1.03, 95% CI 0.85-1.25), although between-trial heterogeneity was high (I2 = 59.3%). Among trials reporting three age strata, RHRs showed no clear evidence of effect modification for 65 to < 75 or ≥ 75 years versus < 65 years, but data were available from only four trials, and the ≥ 75-year group was relatively small. CONCLUSIONS: Across the included trial populations, GLP-1RAs lowered MACE in the age groups examined, with no clear evidence that relative cardiovascular effects differed by age.

title: UNICAL: Uncertainty-Aware Multimodal Learning with MRI-Derived Synthetic Amyloid PET for Alzheimer's Disease Classification.
abstract: Limited availability of amyloid positron emission tomography (PET) motivates imaging-informatics methods that derive complementary molecular-imaging representations from routinely acquired magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). We developed UNICAL, an uncertainty-aware multimodal framework for Alzheimer's disease-spectrum versus cognitively normal classification that combines a self-supervised three-dimensional MRI encoder, Contourlet Wavelet Stationary Radiomics (CoWS-Rad) engineered MRI features, and MRI-derived synthetic 18F-florbetapir (AV45) PET. CoCoLIT generated four stochastic PET realizations per MRI; their mean and voxelwise variance were used for uncertainty gating before probability-anchored transformer fusion. Synthetic PET was validated in 228 paired OASIS-3 MRI-AV45 examinations, achieving a mean per-examination voxelwise Pearson correlation of r = 0.864 and strong cortical-composite SUVR agreement with acquired PET (Pearson r = 0.954). In the OASIS-3 development cohort (813 sessions from 811 participants), participant-grouped five-fold cross-validation repeated across 20 seeds yielded AUROC 0.868 and expected calibration error (ECE) 0.061. The OASIS-3 development endpoint used the manuscript's AD-spectrum reference standard, whereas ADNI3 used AD-versus-CN research-group labels, providing cross-dataset evaluation on a related but non-identical prediction endpoint. Without retraining, feature refitting, threshold optimization, or recalibration, the frozen framework was evaluated in an independent matched ADNI3 cohort of 261 participants (87 AD, 174 CN), achieving AUROC 0.836 (95% CI 0.791-0.876). ECE increased to 0.089 under external transfer, indicating that calibration was more sensitive to domain shift than rank discrimination. Ablation analysis and K-sample sensitivity supported the contributions of uncertainty gating, adaptive weighting, modality dropout, residual correction, and the K = 4 synthesis configuration. UNICAL therefore provides an uncertainty-aware MRI-derived multimodal representation for AD-spectrum classification that retains substantial cross-dataset discrimination while remaining distinct from acquired molecular imaging and not replacing amyloid PET as a clinical biomarker.
journal: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine

title: Interpreting Diabetic Retinal Outcomes After GLP-1 Receptor Agonist and Tirzepatide Initiation: Clinical Evidence and Its Limits.
abstract: AIMS: Reports of diabetic retinopathy after potent glucose-lowering treatment create uncertainty for clinicians, particularly when studies measure different outcomes in patients with different baseline retinal disease. This review examines diabetic retinal outcomes after glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist or tirzepatide initiation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This critical narrative review uses targeted, non-systematic study selection. It distinguishes disease onset or progression from detection, treatment use and subsequent visual function. RESULTS: The SUSTAIN-6 retinopathy-complication signal remains clinically relevant; post hoc associations with early glycated haemoglobin reduction do not establish causal mediation. Contemporary cohorts report differing associations across baseline retinal strata, comparators and endpoints. Positive signals should be presented alongside their absolute event proportions and limitations, rather than dismissed because observational adjustment is imperfect. Conversely, non-significant results do not establish equivalence or class-wide safety. CONCLUSIONS: Current guidance supports establishing retinal status and coordinating diabetes and eye care during treatment intensification. The implications differ between patients with recent screening and no known retinopathy, established non-proliferative disease, and active sight-threatening disease or recent retinal treatment. No universal safe rate of glycated haemoglobin decline or retinal-protective titration regimen has been established. Future studies should align eligibility and treatment initiation, distinguish incident disease from progression, and use scheduled retinal assessments. A comparison between two specific medicines can inform treatment choice but cannot exclude risks shared by both.

title: GLP-1-Based Therapy in Type 1 Diabetes: Balancing Efficacy, Safety, and Patient Selection.
abstract: AIMS: To critically examine the evolving evidence on glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) and the dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP)/GLP-1 receptor agonist tirzepatide as adjuncts to insulin therapy in type 1 diabetes (T1D), with particular emphasis on their benefit-risk balance in individuals with overweight or obesity. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This narrative review examines evidence on liraglutide, semaglutide and tirzepatide in T1D, focusing on effects on body weight and insulin requirements, alongside hypoglycaemia, ketosis, diabetic ketoacidosis and gastrointestinal tolerability. RESULTS: Early trials with liraglutide demonstrated reductions in body weight and insulin requirements but raised concerns regarding hypoglycaemia and ketosis. More recently, semaglutide and tirzepatide have renewed interest in incretin-based therapy in T1D, particularly among individuals with obesity. Their greater effects on weight and insulin requirements introduce a clinically important safety challenge: insulin must be reduced sufficiently to prevent hypoglycaemia while maintaining adequate insulinization to suppress lipolysis and ketogenesis. Gastrointestinal adverse events may further destabilize this balance through reduced carbohydrate intake and dehydration. CONCLUSION: Current evidence supports a phenotype-directed approach centred primarily on adults with T1D and obesity, accompanied by careful patient selection, individualised insulin adjustment, glucose and ketone monitoring, and structured patient education. The clinical question has shifted from whether GLP-1-based therapies are effective in T1D to which patients are most likely to achieve a favourable benefit-risk balance and how these therapies can be used safely.

title: Comparison of cardiac adverse event signal profiles for GLP-1 receptor agonists: an analysis of the FAERS database.
abstract: PURPOSE: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) are widely used in the management of type 2 diabetes owing to their effectiveness in glycemic control and weight reduction. Given the increasing use of GLP-1RAs, further research is warranted to better understand their cardiac effects. METHODS: Individual Case Safety Reports from the U. S. Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System database from July 6, 2007, to February 17, 2026, were evaluated for the post-marketing cardiac adverse events associated with dulaglutide, liraglutide, semaglutide, and tirzepatide. To detect signal differences among drugs, disproportionality analysis was conducted using the Proportional Reporting Ratio (PRR) and Reporting Odds Ratio (ROR) methods, along with standard statistical tests to evaluate categorical variables and to estimate odds ratios. RESULTS: A total of 7,023 cardiac adverse events were identified among 305,877 reports. GLP-1RAs were associated with a higher reporting frequency of tachyarrhythmias than bradyarrhythmias. In the 65-85-year age group, an increase in the signal for cardiac events was observed. Pairwise post hoc comparisons demonstrated no statistically significant differences in reporting frequency of cardiac events between semaglutide and liraglutide, whereas all other drug pairs demonstrated statistically significant differences. CONCLUSION: Semaglutide and liraglutide had higher relative reporting of cardiac events whereas tirzepatide had lower PRR and ROR values against the total background of reports. These findings suggest a lower reporting tendency of cardiac events for tirzepatide. This study may assist healthcare professionals in recognizing the frequency of cardiac events associated with GLP-1RA use and drive new hypotheses to clarify underlying mechanisms.

title: Metabolic health at breast cancer diagnosis and two-year survival: a prospective cohort study in a public healthcare setting.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Metabolic syndrome is common among women with breast cancer and may adversely affect prognosis. However, prospective evidence on changes in metabolic health after breast cancer diagnosis and their association with survival remains limited, particularly in routine public healthcare settings. This study evaluated metabolic health during the first two years after diagnosis and examined the association between metabolic syndrome at diagnosis and overall survival in women with breast cancer. METHODS: This prospective cohort study was conducted in a Brazilian public healthcare service and included women aged ≥ 40 years with newly diagnosed stage I-III invasive breast carcinoma who were followed for two years. Clinical, anthropometric, and laboratory assessments were performed at baseline and at 6, 12, 18, and 24 months. Metabolic syndrome was defined according to the National Cholesterol Education Program Adult Treatment Panel III criteria. Overall survival was defined as the time from breast cancer diagnosis to death from any cause or last follow-up. Survival according to metabolic syndrome status at diagnosis was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox proportional hazards models. RESULTS: A total of 165 women were recruited, of whom 126 were included in the analysis and 111 completed the two-year assessment. Among participants with longitudinal data, significant reductions were observed in the prevalence of dysglycemia, elevated systolic blood pressure, and low HDL cholesterol. No significant changes were found in obesity, increased waist circumference, hypertriglyceridemia, or overall metabolic syndrome prevalence. During follow-up, 15 patients died. Women who died had a higher prevalence of metabolic syndrome at diagnosis than survivors (73% vs. 41%, p = 0.020) and higher baseline fasting glucose levels (p = 0.021). Metabolic syndrome at diagnosis was associated with lower overall survival (log-rank p = 0.021) and a higher risk of mortality (hazard ratio 9.09; 95% confidence interval 1.73-47.9), although this estimate should be interpreted as exploratory because of the limited number of events. CONCLUSIONS: In this prospective cohort of women with breast cancer treated in a Brazilian public healthcare setting, metabolic syndrome was highly prevalent at diagnosis and was associated with poorer two-year overall survival in an exploratory analysis. Although favorable changes were observed in selected metabolic parameters during follow-up, obesity and the overall prevalence of metabolic syndrome remained largely unchanged. These findings support the incorporation of metabolic assessment and multidisciplinary cardiometabolic care into breast cancer management and survivorship programs and require confirmation in larger cohorts with longer follow-up.

title: Trends in treatment and survival of stage IV non-squamous NSCLC from 2010 to 2022.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Advances in immunotherapy (IT) and targeted therapy have transformed treatment for stage IV non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer (NS-NSCLC). However, real-world data comparing modern regimens to previous standards remains limited. Herein, we aim to determine whether survival outcomes have improved with contemporary therapies, METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of de novo stage IV NS-NSCLC at diagnosis treated at the Cleveland Clinic, OH, from 1/2010 to 12/2022. Baseline variables, including age, sex, race, performance status, smoking history, PD-L1 testing, and molecular profiling, were collected along with treatment regimens. Treatment responses were assessed. Overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) were estimated. Multivariable Cox regression (CPH) was used to adjust for confounding. RESULTS: We identified 1,518 patients with NS-NSCLC, of which 97% had adenocarcinoma (N = 1,472). Median age was 65 (IQR 58-73); 51% were female, 82% white, and 42% current smokers. Treatments included conventional chemotherapy (CTX) (744, 49%), IT (186, 12%), CTX + IT (318, 21%), and targeted therapy (270, 18%). Common regimens were carboplatin + pemetrexed/paclitaxel (502, 80%) and bevacizumab + carboplatin + pemetrexed/paclitaxel (127, 20%) for CTX, pembrolizumab (167, 89%) for IT, and carboplatin + pemetrexed + pembrolizumab (153, 41%) for chemo-IT. Overall disease control rate was 58% with a median follow-up of 69.7 months. The 2- and 5-year OS were 30% and 12%, respectively. OS improved from 20% (2010-2012) to 38% (2019-2022) (P < 0.05). Modern regimens were associated with a 23% reduced hazard of death (HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.66-0.90, p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: Modern regimens were associated with improved survival in stage IV NS-NSCLC, but long-term survival remains poor, underscoring the need for further research.

title: Whole-phase DCE-MRI radiomics for differentiating benign and malignant BI-RADS 4 breast lesions: a comparative machine learning study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Breast Imaging Reporting and Data System (BI-RADS) category 4 breast lesions have a wide probability of malignancy, with substantial overlap in imaging findings between benign and malignant lesions. Whole-phase dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) radiomics may provide information on tumor enhancement and heterogeneity. This study primarily aimed to evaluate whole-phase DCE-MRI radiomics for differentiating benign from malignant BI-RADS 4 breast lesions and secondarily explored its feasibility for HER-2 status prediction in malignant lesions. METHODS: This retrospective study included 484 women with BI-RADS 4 breast lesions who underwent DCE-MRI at the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang Chinese Medical University between January 2022 and October 2024, including 264 benign and 220 malignant lesions. Among the malignant lesions, 52 were HER-2 positive and 168 were HER-2 negative. Patients were randomly divided into training and internal test sets at a ratio of 7:3. Whole-phase DCE-MRI radiomics features were extracted. Eight machine-learning algorithms were used to build radiomics models, clinical models, and combined models. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, and F1 score. Decision curve analysis (DCA) was performed as an exploratory assessment of potential net benefit. RESULTS: For differentiating benign from malignant BI-RADS 4 lesions, the support vector machine (SVM) radiomics model achieved the best radiomics performance, with a test-set AUC of 0.893. The combined model further improved the AUC to 0.913. In the secondary exploratory HER-2 analysis, the random forest (RF) radiomics model yielded a test-set AUC of 0.879, whereas the combined model showed a lower AUC of 0.830. Owing to the limited number of HER-2-positive cases and the internal validation design, these HER-2 findings should be interpreted as preliminary and hypothesis-generating. CONCLUSIONS: Whole-phase DCE-MRI radiomics showed favorable internal performance for differentiating benign from malignant BI-RADS 4 breast lesions. The SVM-based combined model performed favorably for the primary malignancy task, whereas the HER-2 analysis should be regarded only as a secondary exploratory observation requiring further validation. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable. This was a retrospective single-center imaging study and did not prospectively assign participants to any intervention.

title: Manganese dioxide-entrapping dendrimers as a therapeutic peptide vaccine for combined tumor chemodynamic/immune therapy and tumor prevention.
abstract: Developing a vaccine that can both elicit robust antitumor immune responses and exert potent tumoricidal effects remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we design a functional dendrimer nanocarrier to co-deliver manganese dioxide (MnO2) nanoparticles (NPs) and ovalbumin peptide antigen OVA257-264 for synergistic tumor chemodynamic/immunotherapy and tumor prevention. Specifically, generation 5 (G5) poly(amidoamine) dendrimers functionalized with methoxy poly(ethylene glycol) (mPEG) and heptafluorobutyric acid (HFBA) were used to entrap MnO2 NPs with an average size of 2.6 nm and complex OVA257-264. The ultimately constructed MnO2@G5-mPEG-HFBA/OVA257-264 (MGPF/OVA257-264) NPs respond to tumor microenvironment for rapid release of Mn2+ that can catalyze a Fenton-like reaction to initiate chemodynamic therapy (CDT) for tumor cell immunogenic cell death (ICD) induction and promote tumor-associated macrophage M1 polarization. The generated ICD combined with Mn2+-mediated stimulator of interferon genes (STING) pathway activation can synergize the co-delivered OVA257-264 antigen to facilitate maturation of dendritic cells for cross-presentation of antigens. In a mouse subcutaneous colorectal cancer model, the MGPF/OVA257-264 nanovaccine exhibits potent therapeutic and prophylactic efficacy, markedly suppressing tumor growth and recurrence through CDT cytocidal effect and robust immune activation. The developed dendrimer-based theranostic peptide nanovaccine may be extended to tackle other types of solid tumors through cooperatively potentiating antitumor immune responses.

title: Association between type 2 diabetes mellitus and breast cancer risk: results from a population-based cohort study in Chinese women.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although numerous epidemiological studies have reported significant associations between type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and breast cancer incidence, considerable heterogeneity exists across studies. Moreover, the breast cancer risk in relation to T2DM duration remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the associations between T2DM, T2DM duration, and breast cancer risk in Chinese women. METHODS: A total of 72,295 women aged 40-70 years from the Shanghai Women's Health Study were included. T2DM was defined as diagnosis after age 30, and categorized as prevalent at enrollment or incident during follow-up. Incident T2DM was treated as a time-dependent exposure in Cox proportional hazards regression models. The risk trajectory of breast cancer following T2DM diagnosis was characterized using categorical modelling analysis. RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 19.08 years, 1,759 incident cases of breast cancer were identified. Compared to individuals without diabetes, overall T2DM was associated with an increased risk of breast cancer (HR = 1.22, 95%CI: 1.05-1.43). This association was significant in women diagnosed with incident T2DM during follow-up (HR = 1.28, 95% CI: 1.05-1.55) but not in those with prevalent T2DM at enrollment (HR = 1.15, 95% CI: 0.90-1.46). A clear trajectory of trend was observed, with the highest risk occurring within the first 5 years after T2DM diagnosis (HR = 4.22, 95% CI: 3.27-5.44). CONCLUSIONS: T2DM was associated with an elevated breast cancer risk in Chinese women, which peaked at approximately 5 years post-diagnosis. Future studies should collect detailed information on treatment and lifestyle changes in study populations, to enable more in-depth analysis.

title: Associations of Cancer Rehabilitation During Hospitalization for Cancer Treatment With Survival and Post-Discharge Healthcare Utilization: A Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Rehabilitation is increasingly recognized as an essential component of oncology care, but there remains limited evidence regarding its broader impact on patient outcomes. This study examined the associations of inpatient cancer rehabilitation with survival and post-discharge healthcare utilization among patients with diverse cancer types. METHODS: We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study using cancer registry-linked claims data from designated cancer care hospitals in Osaka Prefecture, Japan. The study cohort comprised adults newly diagnosed with cancer from 2020 to 2022. The exposure was receipt of inpatient cancer rehabilitation during the initial cancer treatment hospitalization. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality within 1 year of diagnosis, and the secondary outcomes were unplanned readmissions and out-of-hours outpatient visits within 28 days of discharge. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards and Fine-Gray subdistribution hazards models were used, adjusting for demographic and clinical factors. RESULTS: Among 123,955 patients from 69 hospitals, 20,561 (16.6%) underwent inpatient cancer rehabilitation. Rehabilitation was associated with a lower risk of mortality (hazard ratio, 0.83; 95% confidence interval, 0.79-0.87). Lower mortality risks were also observed for the following cancer types: lung, upper gastrointestinal, colorectal, hepato-biliary-pancreatic, breast, and hematologic cancers. Among 115,046 patients included in the post-discharge healthcare utilization analyses, rehabilitation was associated with lower risks of unplanned readmissions (subdistribution hazard ratio, 0.79; 95% confidence interval, 0.73-0.85) and out-of-hours visits (0.92; 0.84-0.999). CONCLUSIONS: Inpatient cancer rehabilitation was associated with lower mortality and reduced post-discharge healthcare utilization. These findings support the further integration of rehabilitation into routine oncology practice.

title: Brain rare metastatic tumors: a clinicopathological analysis of 14 cases.
abstract: BACKGROUND: As one of the most common types of malignant brain tumors, brain metastases are associated with poor clinical outcomes. Lung cancer, breast cancer, colorectal cancer, and renal cell carcinoma are the most frequent primary tumors causing brain metastases. This study explores the clinicopathological characteristics and diagnostic challenges of brain metastases from rare tumors to provide references for clinical diagnosis and treatment. METHODS: This study retrospectively analyzed the clinical data of 14 patients with brain metastases originating from rare tumors, treated from 2013 to 2025. The data included primary tumor pathological types and follow-up records, supplemented by a literature review. RESULTS: Among the 14 patients, the primary tumor types included 3 cases of ovarian serous carcinoma, 3 cases of papillary thyroid carcinoma, 2 cases of hepatocellular carcinoma, 2 cases of urothelial carcinoma, 1 case of breast rhabdomyosarcoma, 1 case of uterine leiomyosarcoma, 1 case of penile squamous cell carcinoma, and 1 case of prostate adenocarcinoma. The median age was 62.9 years, and the average maximum tumor diameter was 4.7 cm. Common symptoms included headache and limb weakness. Pathological immunohistochemical analysis revealed key markers such as WT-1, TG, hepPar-1, GATA3, NKX3.1, caldesmon, MyoD1, and P40 were positive staining. CONCLUSION: Brain metastases from rare tumors lack specific clinical manifestations, and definitive diagnosis relies on pathology and immunohistochemistry. Multidisciplinary comprehensive treatment may improve prognosis, but overall survival rates remain low, necessitating further exploration of novel strategies such as targeted therapy.

title: Short-interval variability and test-retest reliability of Alzheimer's disease plasma biomarkers in a clinically heterogenous cohort.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Assessment of short-term within-subject variability and test-retest reliability of Alzheimer's disease (AD)-related plasma biomarkers is important for real-world clinical implementation and interpretation in research studies. In this study we aimed to assess short-term variability and reliability of core AD plasma biomarkers, proposed ratios, and evaluate a broader proteomic panel. METHODS: Two serial plasma samples were collected from each of the 92 participants enrolled in observational research studies over intervals ranging from 30 minutes to three months. Test-retest reliability and within-subject variability were assessed for 131 biomarkers measured on three immunoassays (Lumipulse G plasma p-tau217; Fujirebio, NULISAseq CNS Disease Panel and NULISAqpcr AD 5-Plex; Alamar Biosciences). We subsequently evaluated the stability of a dual cut-point approach for AD probability diagnostic categorisation and examined whether within-subject variability was associated with inter-sample interval (time between serial blood sampling). RESULTS: All core AD plasma biomarkers assessed in this study (Aβ42, BD-p-tau181, BD-p-tau217, BD-p-tau231, p-tau181, p-tau217, p-tau231, GFAP and NfL) demonstrated strong correlations (r ≥ 0.79) and high reliability (ICC ≥ 0.84). Within-subject variability was moderate to low for core AD plasma biomarkers. Using a validated dual cut-point approach for plasma p-tau217, most individuals (92%) remained within the same diagnostic category (high/indeterminate/low) across both timepoints, and no individual moved across two boundaries (i.e. from high to low AD probability categorisation or vice versa). For the majority of analytes, within-subject variability was not associated with inter-sample interval after adjustment for age and sex, however, the core AD plasma biomarker, NfL did have a significant association. CONCLUSIONS: While core AD plasma biomarkers had limited variability and high reliability over short-intervals, other central nervous system (CNS)-relevant biomarkers showed greater variability, which may be relevant for interpretation in association studies and clinical applications.

title: Plasma β-synuclein associates with hippocampal synaptic density measured with [11C]UCB-J PET and plasma tau markers in Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Plasma β-synuclein is a promising blood-based synaptic biomarker, but relationships with synaptic density as indicated by [11C]UCB-J positron emission tomography (PET), and blood biomarkers of Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology, neurodegeneration, and astrocyte activation need further characterization. METHODS: Middle-aged and older adults with and without cognitive impairment (N = 83 total, 68.7% cognitively unimpaired) underwent blood draw, PET imaging, and neuropsychological testing. Primary analyses focused on relationships between plasma β-synuclein and synaptic density, and associations with related plasma biomarkers (tau phosphorylated at threonine 217 [p-tau217], brain-derived tau [BD-tau], glial fibrillary acidic protein [GFAP], and neurofilament light chain [NfL]). RESULTS: Plasma β-synuclein levels were higher in cognitively unimpaired and impaired participants with positive amyloid PET. Synaptic density was lower in cognitively impaired participants only. In the full sample, higher plasma β-synuclein levels associated with lower synaptic density in the hippocampus, higher concentrations of plasma tau markers, and higher plasma GFAP. DISCUSSION: This work further supports utilization of plasma β-synuclein to track synaptic degeneration in AD.
journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association

title: Caregiver positivity as a psychosocial modifier of lecanemab-related outcomes in Alzheimer's disease: A multicenter longitudinal study in China.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Real-world modifiers of lecanemab benefit in Alzheimer's disease (AD) remain elusive. We examined associations between caregiver positivity and longitudinal outcomes in AD. METHODS: This seven-center longitudinal study followed 127 biomarker-supported AD patient-caregiver dyads over 18 months. Mixed-effects, spline, and propensity-score analyses evaluated continuous Positive Aspects of Caregiving (PAC) scores. RESULTS: Higher baseline PAC scale scores were associated with more favorable 18-month outcomes in cognition (Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE): β = 0.42, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.24-0.59; p < 0.001), daily function (Alzheimer's Disease Cooperative Study-Activities of Daily Living [ADCS-ADL]: β = 0.68, 95% CI: 0.42-0.93; p < 0.001), disease severity (Clinical Dementia Rating-Sum of Boxes [CDR-SB]: β = -0.26, 95% CI: -0.37 to -0.14; P < 0.001), patient quality of life (Quality of Life in Alzheimer's Disease [QOL-AD]: β = 0.53, 95% CI: 0.34-0.71; p < 0.001), and lower apathy (β = -0.09, 95% CI: -0.16 to -0.03; p = 0.003); these associations remained significant after multiplicity correction (all q's ≤ 0.004). Patient QOL-AD showed the most consistent sensitivity-analysis association. Apathy was associated with caregiver burden and caregiver quality of life, but mediation was not established. DISCUSSION: Caregiver positivity may stratify lecanemab efficacy in AD, supporting psychosocial assessment in personalized, caregiver-inclusive management pathways.
journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association

title: Relative handgrip strength is associated with nutritional status and quality of life in women with overweight and obesity diagnosed with breast cancer undergoing surgery: a cross-sectional study in Brazil.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Handgrip strength (HGS) is a low-cost and efficient tool for risk stratification of patients diagnosed with chronic diseases. This cross-sectional observational study investigated associations between absolute and relative HGS (AHGS and RHGS, respectively) and physical performance and quality of life (QoL) in women with overweight and obesity diagnosed with breast cancer, who were admitted to hospital for surgical treatment of cancer. METHODS: AHGS, RHGS (AHGS/weight), body mass index (BMI), waist circumference (WC), muscle mass, gait speed, and Functional Assessment of Cancer Therapy (FACT) Breast QoL, were assessed in 97 participants. RESULTS: Women with low RHGS exhibited higher BMI (r=-0.42, P<0.001) and WC (r=-0.48, P<0.001). RHGS was positively correlated with QoL (r=0.36, P<0.001). Higher QoL scores (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.001-0.003) and physical performance (95% CI, 0.034-0.163) were associated with higher RHGS values. Positive correlations were found for RHGS, and not for AHGS, including the FACT emotional well-being (r=0.21, P=0.035) and breast cancer (r=0.32, P=0.001) subscales. CONCLUSION: RHGS was more strongly associated with nutritional characteristics, physical performance, and QoL than AHGS in a sample population of women with overweight and obesity diagnosed with breast cancer before surgery. RHGS has the potential to reveal a more accurate overall health status. Further research involving diverse age and population groups and clinical settings to explore causality and, potentially, confirm the utility of relative HGS as an early screening tool for dynapenia and guiding nutritional interventions to improve QoL during and after antineoplastic treatment, is warranted.

title: CSF and plasma lipid profiling predicts risk of cognitive impairment in cognitively unimpaired older adults.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Age-related cognitive decline and Alzheimer's disease (AD) are strongly influenced by lipid metabolism, yet how central and peripheral lipid profiles relate to disease risk before symptom onset remains unclear. METHODS: We performed comprehensive shotgun lipidomics in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and plasma from cognitively unimpaired older adults, with longitudinal follow-up for Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR) conversion. RESULTS: CSF lipidomes were primarily associated with age and established CSF AD biomarkers, whereas plasma lipid profiles were strongly influenced by sex. Specific CSF phosphatidylethanolamine subspecies showed robust positive associations with CSF total tau, phosphorylated tau 181, neurogranin, and chitinase-3 like-1. CSF triacylglycerol TAG(C49:6), phosphatidylglycerol PG(18:0-18:1), cholesteryl ester CE(20:3), and phosphatidylethanolamine PE(D16:0-18:1) independently predicted CDR conversion, improving risk prediction. Plasma sphingomyelin subspecies were modestly associated with cognitive decline risk. DISCUSSION: These findings identify distinct CSF and plasma lipid signatures linked to preclinical cognitive decline and highlight brain lipid metabolism as a promising source of predictive biomarkers and therapeutic targets.
journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
