The tumour showed tall columnar cells with focal reversed nuclear polarity, keratin 5/6 positivity with strong S100 and anti-mitochondrial antibody expression, moderate oestrogen receptor positivity, and absence of myoepithelial markers. Molecular testing identified an IDH2 R172 mutation, confirming the diagnosis. This is a notable example of oestrogen receptor-positive tall cell carcinoma with reversed polarity. While most such tumours are triple-negative, the oestrogen receptor positivity, which initially led to consideration of papilloma with usual ductal hyperplasia, does not preclude the diagnosis. Accurate preoperative diagnosis is essential to avoid misclassification and to guide appropriate surgical management. The patient underwent wide local excision with sentinel lymph-node biopsy, with adjuvant radiotherapy and endocrine therapy recommended, and no recurrence at last follow-up. This report demonstrates that the diagnosis can be reliably established on limited biopsy material when morphological, immunophenotypic, and molecular data are integrated. We also provide a diagnostic algorithm for papillary neoplasms with unusual morphology.

title: RA-BCNet: Residual attention breast cancer network for high-precision breast cancer detection.
abstract: BackgroundBreast cancer remains a major global health concern, and early and accurate detection is critical for improving clinical outcomes. However, variations in lesion characteristics and imaging conditions in Digital Breast Tomosynthesis (DBT) images present substantial challenges for automated breast tumor classification.ObjectiveThis study aims to develop a robust and interpretable deep learning framework, termed RA-BCNet-PReLU, by integrating residual attention mechanisms with Parametric Rectified Linear Unit (PReLU) activation for accurate multi-class breast tumor classification.MethodsThe proposed framework employs a structured processing pipeline comprising Min-Max normalization, stratified sampling, and targeted image augmentation for data preprocessing and generalization. Lesion segmentation is performed using a convolutional neural network (CNN), with segmentation further optimized using the Dynamic Hybrid Grey Wolf-Sunflower Optimization (DHGWSFO) algorithm. Subsequently, handcrafted shape, color, and spatial descriptors are integrated with deep features extracted using ResNet-50 to obtain a comprehensive lesion representation. The fused features are then classified using a residual attention-based CNN with PReLU activation. The model was evaluated on a DBT mammography dataset and externally validated on the CBIS-DDSM dataset. Model reliability was assessed using five-fold cross-validation, ANOVA, paired t-tests, and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, while Grad-CAM was employed to improve model interpretability.ResultsThe proposed RA-BCNet-PReLU achieved a mean classification accuracy of 96.87% ± 0.42 on the DBT dataset and 98.72% ± 0.35 on the CBIS-DDSM dataset, with corresponding AUC values of 0.967 and 0.981, respectively. Statistical analyses demonstrated the reliability of the obtained results, while Grad-CAM visualizations highlighted clinically relevant regions contributing to the model's predictions.ConclusionThe proposed RA-BCNet-PReLU framework demonstrates high classification performance, robustness, and interpretability across DBT and external mammography datasets. Its integration of optimized lesion segmentation, hybrid feature representation, residual attention, and explainable visualization indicates its potential as an effective computer-aided tool for automated breast cancer detection and clinical decision support.
journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine

title: Synergistic Promotion of Ferroptosis in Cardiomyocytes by Tumor Cell Secretory Factors and PD-1 Blockade.
abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) targeting PD-1 frequently cause severe cardiotoxicity, yet the mechanisms involving tumor-host crosstalk remain poorly defined. Emerging evidence implicates ferroptosis, an iron-dependent regulated cell death, in cardiac injury during cancer immunotherapy. Primary neonatal murine ventricular cardiomyocytes (NMVCs) were exposed to lung cancer-derived tumor-conditioned media (TCM; tumor-conditioned media) enriched with exosomes, anti-PD-1 antibody, or both. Ferroptotic markers, mitochondrial bioenergetics, inflammatory signaling, and exosomal microRNA cargo were systematically evaluated using standardized biochemical assays, quantitative PCR, and targeted pharmacological rescue experiments. TCM primed cardiomyocytes for ferroptosis by downregulating the GPX4/SLC7A11/Nrf2 antioxidant axis, depleting glutathione, and elevating labile iron and lipid peroxidation. Anti-PD-1 treatment alone induced minimal oxidative stress but synergized with TCM to amplify ferroptosis > 4.7-fold, triggering profound mitochondrial depolarization and upregulating pro-ferroptotic enzymes ACSL4/LPCAT3. Tumor-derived exosomal miR-214-3p and miR-23a-3p directly suppressed GPX4 and Nrf2, mediating cellular vulnerability. The combined insult hyperactivated NF-κB and STING pathways in a mitochondria-dependent manner, markedly increasing pro-inflammatory cytokine secretion. Co-treatment with ferrostatin-1, deferoxamine, or Nrf2 activators effectively reversed ferroptotic markers and restored mitochondrial function. Tumor-derived exosomal factors and PD-1 blockade synergistically drive ferroptotic cardiomyocyte death by crippling antioxidant defenses and amplifying inflammatory signaling. Targeting ferroptosis or its upstream regulators presents a promising cardioprotective strategy for patients receiving cancer immunotherapy.
journal: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology

title: TRACER: response-protected cross-domain alignment of cancer pharmacogenomic models with patient tumors.
abstract: Pharmacogenomics integrates tumor molecular features with drug responses to support precision oncology, but biological domain shifts and optimization conflicts hinder transfer from screened cell lines to unlabeled patient tumors. We developed TRACER (Transfer of Response Across domains via Conflict-aware End-to-end Regulation), an end-to-end framework combining supervised drug-response prediction, biologically conditioned neighbor alignment and response-protected gradient regulation. By projecting only conflicting components of the auxiliary alignment gradient, TRACER preserves the response-optimization direction learned from experimental labels. Across ModelID-disjoint, seen-drug splits, TRACER-Full achieved a global Pearson correlation of 0.5125 $\pm $ 0.0192 on per-drug z-standardized test pairs, compared with 0.5179 $\pm $ 0.0193 for Response-only, a mean difference of $-0.0054$. Mean oncogenic Hallmark neighbor consistency increased by $0.1162 \pm 0.0210$ in alignment-excluded The Cancer Genome Atlas audit samples. At the patient level, a source-validation-defined drug partition and uniform stability analysis supported four predicted pharmacological response subtypes (PRSs) in breast invasive carcinoma (BRCA), four in uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma (UCEC) and two in sarcoma (SARC). PRS-construction-excluded drugs characterized distinct predicted mechanism-level profiles, and pan-cancer indication recovery provided a lineage-aware internal consistency assessment of the patient rankings. TRACER provides an interpretable and auditable framework for response-preserving cross-domain alignment and it generates patient pharmacogenomic hypotheses for subsequent functional validation.

title: Diet quality and blood pressure among adults with hypertension living in a high-altitude region of the Peruvian Andes.
abstract: Diet quality plays an important role in the management of non-communicable diseases, including hypertension. A better understanding of dietary profiles in high-altitude populations with hypertension could help improve the effectiveness of interventions. We aimed to characterize diet quality and its association with blood pressure among adults with hypertension living at high-altitude. Cross-sectional study of baseline data from an ongoing trial in Puno, Peru. We enrolled 154 adults with hypertension participating in a community health worker-led intervention aimed at improving hypertension management in a high-altitude region of Peru. Diet was assessed by 24-hour recalls which were analyzed to calculate the Global Diet Quality Score (GDQS, range 0 - 49 with higher scores indicating better diet quality) and categorized into quartiles. We assessed blood pressure using a digital oscillometric tensiometer. We used multivariable linear regression to study the association between diet quality and blood pressure adjusted for sociodemographic characteristics, food security status, hypertension awareness and treatment, BMI, HbA1c and lifestyle habits. We further stratified the analyses by hypertension awareness and treatment. Mean ± standard deviation (SD) age of participants was 66.5 ± 10.9 years and 51.9% were females. Overall mean GDQS was 15.7 ± 3.4 points. While no statistically significant association in the overall sample in multivariable models, we found an inverse association between GDQS quartiles and systolic blood pressure (adjusted mean difference of -4.13 mmHg, 95% CI: -7.72 to -0.53 p-trend = 0.03) among participants who were aware of having hypertension and receiving treatment (n = 102). We found that study participants had generally low diet quality based on GDQS. Among those aware of and receiving treatment for hypertension, higher GDQS scores were associated with lower systolic blood pressure.

title: Spatial distribution of the time between diagnosis and treatment of breast cancer among women in Brazil.
abstract: Female breast cancer presents high incidence and mortality rates and is considered a significant public health problem. The timeliness of oncological treatment is a fundamental factor in the prognosis and survival of patients. The objective of this study was to analyze the spatial distribution pattern of the percentage of women who initiated breast cancer treatment within 60 days and its association with socioeconomic indicators and the availability of health services in Brazil. An ecological study was conducted using 133 Intermediate Regions of Urban Articulation (IRUA), based on records from the period 2013-2019. Data on the percentage of treatment initiation within 60 days were obtained from the Hospital Cancer Registry Integrator (IHCR). Socioeconomic variables were collected from the Atlas of Human Development in Brazil and the Institute for Applied Economic Research (IPEA). Data on the availability and density of health professionals and services were obtained from the National Registry of Health Establishments (NRHE) and the Hospital Information System (HIS). The Global Moran's Index and the Local Indicator of Spatial Association (LISA) were used to verify the existence of territorial clusters. Multivariate analysis employed models with global spatial effects. The percentage of breast cancer cases that initiated treatment within 60 days was 48.9% (95% CI: 48.6% - 49.1%), with the highest adherence observed in the IRUA of Cascavel (85%) and the lowest in the IRUA of Rio de Janeiro (16.6%). In the final Spatial Lag Model, positive associations were observed with the density of Family and Community Physicians (β = 0.35; p = 0.007) and the proportion of surgical procedures (β = 0.30; p = 0.001). The analysis indicates that compliance with the 60-day law is related to the structure and organization of health services, highlighting the importance of primary health care as the coordinator of care and the role of surgical capacity in the spatial distribution pattern.

title: Use of Portable Ultrasound by Nonradiologists to Triage Women With Abnormal Clinical Breast Examination Findings: A Prospective Study in India.
abstract: PURPOSE: Clinical breast examination (CBE) is widely used for breast cancer screening and evaluation of symptomatic women in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). However, its limited specificity leads to high false-positive rates and unnecessary referrals. We evaluated a point-of-care triage strategy using portable ultrasound devices (PUDs), performed by nonradiologist clinicians, to improve the positive predictive value (PPV) of CBE and reduce referrals. METHODS: Women age 40-75 years with abnormal CBE findings were recruited from two settings: asymptomatic women identified through community-based screening and symptomatic women presenting to breast clinics. Trained nonradiologist clinicians used PUDs to classify findings as triage-negative (no abnormality/benign) or triage-positive (suspicious). All participants underwent standard diagnostic evaluation irrespective of PUD findings. RESULTS: A total of 319 women were enrolled (149 screening; 170 diagnostic). PUD triage was positive in 44.3% of women in the screening group and 72.4% in the diagnostic group. Breast cancer was diagnosed in 37 (24.8%) women in the screening group and 121 (71.2%) in the diagnostic group. PUD triage identified all cancers in the screening setting and all but nine in the diagnostic setting, yielding an overall sensitivity of 94.3% and specificity of 76.7%. Use of PUD substantially improved PPV and reduced referrals by approximately 50%. CONCLUSION: Point-of-care ultrasound performed by trained nonradiologist clinicians can effectively triage women with abnormal CBE findings, improving PPV and reducing unnecessary referrals. This approach may enhance efficiency of breast cancer early detection programs in LMICs. Further studies are warranted to assess performance in routine program settings.

title: Immunotherapy With Stereotactic Body Radiation Therapy in Early-Stage Non‐Small Cell Lung Cancer: Matching Risk, Biology, and Timing.
